<a id="abstract"></a>
## Abstract

This directive specifies the development of a native Android cinematography application combining three independently accountable systems: the best practically accessible capture path on a particular Samsung Galaxy S23 Ultra; a non-destructive, high-precision motion-picture film development engine; and an optional, offline, temporally coherent virtual-lens renderer. The application is intended to exceed the user's current film-camera simulation workflow through observable improvements in source preservation, film-response control, large-format interpretation, depth-aware optics, movie-recipe scholarship, reliability, and professional operation. It must not claim to enlarge the physical sensor, recreate unrecorded scene information exactly, or acquire proprietary Samsung Log merely by relabelling processed video.

The research programme separates mathematical correctness, implementation correctness, physical measurement, and artistic preference. A reference transform passing numerical tests is not proof of sensor-derived capture. A playable ten-bit file is not proof that its source retained ten-bit precision. A visually pleasing shallow-focus still is not proof of stable video rendering. Each claim therefore has a required evidence class, a defined observation protocol, a failure condition, and a reproducibility record. Test-driven development is required throughout, with positive controls, negative controls, independent oracles, mutation tests for critical defects, and explicit unavailable outcomes when hardware is absent.

The design preserves the existing application's useful capture, source-reading, storage, and recovery foundations. The inspected repository documentation describes saved-RAW development and extensive capture evidence, while explicitly withholding physical S23 calibration and live RAW-derived Log certification. Those are documentation observations, not a complete source-code audit; the executing developer must inspect the current revision before modifying it.[^R01][^R02]

The programme contains 160 numbered development phases across twenty workstreams, with an expanded acceptance laboratory attached to every phase. A standalone host reference implementation and tests demonstrate selected arithmetic, provenance, timing, packing, and state-machine contracts. These examples are deliberately narrower than the production application. They provide executable starting points and falsification tools, not a substitute for Android integration or real-phone measurement. The final product is a source-preserving camera and film laboratory whose claims remain proportional to its evidence.

**Keywords:** Android Camera2; RAW video research; LogC3; camera characterization; film emulation; virtual large format; temporal depth; computational bokeh; offline inference; reproducibility; test-driven development; media integrity.

<a id="agent-charter"></a>
## 1. Governing agent charter

Act as the lead engineer of this project and as a skeptical reviewer of your own results. Implement the next dependency-ready slice rather than replacing the application with an unrelated demonstration. The owner wants a real app for a real phone, not a collection of impressive screenshots, disconnected shader experiments, or generated documentation that claims features exist because their names appear in a menu.

The normative words **MUST**, **MUST NOT**, **SHOULD**, and **MAY** are used as project-level requirements. MUST denotes a release or evidence invariant unless a later owner-approved revision explicitly changes it. SHOULD permits a documented alternative supported by measurements. MAY identifies optional research rather than required shipping scope. These words describe this project's governance; they are not a claim that this document is an external industry standard.

The developer MUST preserve irreplaceable user footage. Capture and development errors may produce an incomplete or unverified result, but they must not silently delete the only retained source. The developer MUST preserve exact source lineage. RAW-derived, HLG-derived, SDR-derived, and synthetic fixtures are different categories even when they eventually share an output codec. The developer MUST preserve a clean master or original source whenever the selected workflow promises non-destructive development.

The developer MUST distinguish physical source controls from virtual processing controls. Physical lens focus, exposure time, sensor gain, and white-balance metadata are not the same as virtual focus, print exposure, creative temperature, or a simulated film format. A user must be able to understand which choice affects the recorded source and which choice can be changed later.

The developer MUST NOT use a cloud video-generation API as a required part of capture, film rendering, depth estimation, catalogue search, or export. Optional downloads of approved model or recipe packages are allowed only as explicit asset installation. Once required assets are present, the core workflow must operate without an internet connection. The recorded scene remains the user's footage; learned models may estimate depth, masks, confidence, or motion, but must not silently replace people, objects, text, or textures with generated content.

The developer MUST NOT promise firmware success before a specific blocked capability is identified. Firmware investigation is a separate research track, not a dependency of the usable film laboratory. Any device modification with potential irreversible consequences requires a fresh, explicit authorization and a device-specific safety decision. This directive does not itself authorize flashing, bootloader changes, disabling protections, or installing unverified system images.

The developer SHOULD use the existing branch and repository layout, minimizing new modules, folders, build systems, and caches. A named workstream is not an instruction to create a new Gradle module. Prefer a small number of coherent packages and interfaces over a framework for every subsection. Add a native dependency only when a measured performance, correctness, or compatibility need justifies its lifecycle cost.

During a coding session, read the governing sections, the active phase, its acceptance laboratory, and the referenced contracts. Do not repeatedly load the entire long document merely to perform a small change. Record the active phase and exact requirement IDs in the handoff so later agents can continue without rediscovering decisions. A phase is a bounded research or development increment, not necessarily a calendar week, a commit, or a complete feature visible to users.

<a id="scope"></a>
## 2. Product scope, user outcomes, and non-goals

### 2.1 Required user outcomes

The user must be able to discover the actual capture modes exposed on the phone, select an honestly described source route, record with dependable controls and recoverable storage, and understand whether the route is merely advertised, software-tested, or physically qualified. The interface must not hide maximum-resolution aspirations, but it must keep unmeasured configurations visibly experimental.

The user must be able to retain a source, select a virtual format and stock interpretation, adjust the development process, and export a result without destroying the source. The initial virtual-format registry must include Super 8, Super 16, standard 35mm, Super 35, five-perforation 65mm, and horizontal fifteen-perforation large-format acquisition associated with IMAX film presentation. The exact gate definition and any approximation belong in the profile, not in undocumented constants scattered through shaders.

The user must be able to enable optional shallow-depth-of-field rendering, select a focus target, and understand when focus controls are relative rather than measured in metres. Moderate, stable rendering is the default goal. Dramatic blur that repeatedly fails at hair, glass, or foreground boundaries is not acceptable merely because it looks impressive on an isolated frame.

The user must be able to search a local movie-recipe catalogue and inspect both documented production information and our reconstruction choices. The catalogue must not invent a stock, lens, camera, development process, or scene-specific setting merely to avoid an empty field. A recipe may be useful while remaining openly reconstructed.

The user must be able to compare source and result at matched times, save recipe versions, cancel and resume expensive development where supported, inspect retained partial files, and export technical metadata with the result. A professional interface includes clear failure and recovery states, not only attractive controls during the happy path.

### 2.2 Explicit non-goals

The initial product is not a general-purpose nonlinear editor, a cloud collaboration service, a social network, or a generative movie application. Do not add timelines, subscription infrastructure, remote storage, chat, account systems, or broad marketplace features unless a later requirement justifies them. The first objective is a reliable camera and digital film laboratory for this user's phone.

The product is not an ARRI camera emulator in the sense of reproducing all physical sensor, readout, spectral, optical, and processing characteristics. LogC3/AWG3-compatible output describes an encoding and color workflow. It does not transfer the dynamic range, noise behavior, highlight response, lens coverage, or physical image formation of an ARRI camera to a phone.[^C01]

The product is not guaranteed to produce native 8K RAW-derived Log at any specified frame rate. Higher resolutions remain explicit research targets whose complete paths must be qualified. Upscaled output, retimed footage, duplicated frames, or a larger container dimension cannot satisfy a native acquisition requirement.

The product does not promise exact reconstruction of clipped highlights, unrecorded shadow detail, hidden backgrounds, absent lighting, or different camera viewpoints. Conservative approximations may improve appearance. They must not be relabelled as recovered measurements.

### 2.3 Priority order

The priority order is source preservation, honest capture evidence, numerical correctness, reliable development, temporally stable optics, useful film rendering, clear interaction, and finally breadth of presets. This ordering does not make visual quality unimportant. It prevents visual quality from becoming an excuse to conceal data loss or false capture claims.

A smaller stock library with well-controlled behavior is preferable to hundreds of unsupported names. A qualified 1080p path is more useful than an unverified 8K button. A deferred renderer with stable edges is more useful than a live preview that corrupts the take. These are project decisions, not claims that lower resolution or deferred processing is universally preferable for every filmmaker.

<a id="evidence-review"></a>
## 3. Evidence review and prior-system context

### 3.1 Existing repository boundary

The live README inspected for this directive identifies a Kotlin/XML Android application with Camera2 capture, evidence reporting, retained RAW sequences, on-device saved-RAW development, and explicit limitations. The on-device development document describes a row-streamed CPU reference, profile provenance, P010/Main10 qualification, full output comparison, and separately retained partial exports. Both documents state that physical S23 calibration and performance remain unverified. The executing agent must re-read the current files because repository state can change after this document is delivered.[^R01][^R02]

This directive therefore does not order a rewrite of the camera engine. It orders a live source audit, preservation of existing behavior, and incremental addition or repair of missing capabilities. Existing tests that cover recovery, timestamp pairing, manual-result confirmation, signal tags, and source identity are assets. Replacing them with simpler tests to make a new architecture pass would be a regression in evidence quality.

### 3.2 Super 16 as a comparison target

The current Android listing advertises manual controls, more than seventy filters, imported LUTs, grain, halation, gate weave, scratches, waveform or histogram monitoring, saved presets, and processing of existing video. These are documented capabilities, not features our app can claim to originate. A dated user review reports landscape and orientation difficulties, but that report does not prove the current version still has the defect. Our comparison protocol must test current behavior using identical source clips and recorded app versions.[^F06]

Our proposed differentiators are independent format and stock modelling, source and precision transparency, calibrated development where possible, a stable virtual-lens system, non-destructive high-quality deferred rendering, and a sourced movie-recipe catalogue. Whether these make the result better must be evaluated. The directive prohibits unmeasured numerical claims such as twenty times better realism.

### 3.3 Official Samsung Log scope

Samsung's current support page lists supported Galaxy families but does not list the S23 Ultra. That is sufficient to withhold a promise of an official Samsung Log switch for this phone. It is not proof that every custom RAW-derived or HDR-derived recording path is impossible. The app-level research must investigate the actual public interfaces and measured output of the user's device.[^S01]

### 3.4 Research foundations

Published grain research provides a physically motivated, resolution-independent rendering reference. The associated code has its own licence and is not automatically suitable for incorporation into any intended distribution. The project may learn from the published model, implement an independently reviewed approach, or obtain suitable rights; code and data adoption require separate decisions.[^F01]

The spektrafilm project explores negative, print, and scan simulation using manufacturer data. It is relevant as a research reference, not as proof that its full pipeline runs in real time on the S23. Its code, profiles, and LUT terms must be reviewed individually at the exact revision selected for any use.[^F02]

Google's portrait-camera research and DeepLens demonstrate meaningful precedents for depth-aware synthetic shallow focus. They do not establish that this app can render arbitrary difficult video at full resolution and frame rate. Video Depth Anything addresses temporal depth consistency, while Depth Anything V2 and Qualcomm's model catalogue provide candidates for on-device investigation. Model availability, licensing, conversion accuracy, and integrated performance remain separate gates.[^D01][^D02][^D03][^D04][^D05]

### 3.5 What the literature does not establish

No cited source establishes that this specific phone and firmware can sustain the entire proposed capture, depth, film, and encoding graph at 4K or 8K in real time. No cited source establishes exact movie reproduction from arbitrary phone footage. No cited source removes the ambiguity of reconstructing a light spectrum from three camera channels. The engineering programme must use these limits to design better experiments, not to manufacture certainty or abandon useful approximations.

<a id="scientific-model"></a>
## 4. Scientific model and image-domain contracts

### 4.1 Separate observation, inference, and rendering

An observation is a measured source value or device result. An inference is an estimated quantity such as scene depth or a reconstructed stock parameter. A rendering decision is a deliberate transformation such as virtual aperture, print contrast, or grain strength. The application must not collapse these categories into one opaque image pipeline.

For example, a sensor timestamp is an observation, a monocular depth field is an inference, and a focus curve selected by the user is a rendering decision. A capture-result neutral point is an observation, a manufacturer-metadata starting profile is a provisional interpretation, and a warmer final print is a creative decision. The metadata schema should make these distinctions inspectable.

### 4.2 Capture and development graph

The conceptual graph is:

```text
physical scene and phone optics
    -> sensor / available camera processing
    -> qualified source acquisition
    -> immutable source and capture evidence
    -> source-specific normalization
    -> high-precision working image
         -> clean grading-master branch
         -> monitoring branch
         -> optional depth / motion / virtual-optics branch
              -> film-negative exposure and material response
              -> grain and declared material scattering
              -> print / scan interpretation
              -> delivery transform
              -> codec / container / independent verification
```

This is a conceptual ownership graph, not a claim that every physical process can be reproduced by a simple serial filter. The implementation must document where effects interact and where an approximation changes their ordering. Optical scatter belongs to the image-formation interpretation; material grain belongs to the simulated material response; scanner or delivery filtering has a different meaning again.

The graph must retain the original source before irreversible operations. A clean Log master must branch before virtual defocus, creative film response, grain, and display tone mapping. A processed high-range master may be offered separately, but its name and metadata must reveal that it contains those operations.

### 4.3 Signal descriptor

Every image-bearing interface needs a descriptor containing source identity, geometry, channel layout, numeric type, transfer, primaries or working basis, white point where applicable, range convention, timestamp domain, frame identity, and processing lineage. A texture handle or byte buffer alone is insufficient.

At minimum, distinguish RAW mosaics, camera-linear RGB, working-linear RGB, encoded Log RGB, encoded YUV, film density, transmission, display-linear RGB, and display-encoded RGB. Blur, interpolation, reduction, and exposure operations must declare the domain in which they are defined. A graph validator should reject obviously invalid edges before allocating GPU resources.

Do not label every decoded image scene-linear. Inverting an HLG or SDR transfer yields a representation related to the encoded signal, but it does not necessarily undo the camera's local tone mapping, sharpening, denoising, or other ISP processing. The source lineage must retain that limitation.[^A01][^C03]

### 4.4 RAW normalization and clipping

For a simple channel sample with source code `r`, black reference `b`, and white reference `w`, the normalization reference is:

```text
x = (r - b) / (w - b), with w > b
```

This arithmetic does not imply that all real sensors use one constant black or white value. The production profile may need channel, row, frame, or mode-dependent references. The reference is useful because it makes units and failure cases explicit.

Preserve negative residuals when they arise from read noise or the declared color transform. Record source saturation before normalization. Do not clip every intermediate to zero-to-one merely because a display image eventually occupies a bounded range. Values above one can represent scene highlights relative to the chosen diffuse-white scale; negative channels can arise in a wide-gamut transform without meaning that the physical scene emitted negative light.

At a bounded delivery boundary, clipping or gamut compression becomes a deliberate operation. The user-facing policy must distinguish clipping that was already present in the source from clipping introduced by the selected development or export. A soft shoulder changes appearance but does not recover information lost earlier.

### 4.5 LogC3 reference

The bundled implementation uses the published LogC3 EI800 exposure-domain coefficient set. It is a scalar transfer reference, not an entire camera characterization. The correct input domain and the chosen encoding convention must remain explicit; the phone's ISO is not automatically the same quantity as the ARRI encoding EI.[^C01]

The reference functions are:

```text
encode(x) = c * log10(a*x + b) + d, when x > cut
            e*x + f, otherwise

decode(y) = (10^((y-d)/c) - b) / a, when y > e*cut + f
            (y-f)/e, otherwise
```

The coefficients are included in the executable code, with tests near the branch join. Published rounded coefficients can create a very small join discrepancy; test tolerances must reflect that rounding rather than asserting impossible bit-exact continuity. The implementation must reject nonfinite values and keep overflow behavior explicit.

AWG3 conversion is a separate matrix and colorimetry operation. Encoding a phone channel with the LogC3 function does not by itself make that channel AWG3, just as assigning a file extension does not make its contents a valid codec stream. The source profile must establish the camera-to-working transformation, and the export graph must establish the working-to-AWG3 transformation.

### 4.6 Optical geometry and terminology correction

The intended effect is shallow depth of field. Shadow detail and depth of field are different properties. A larger virtual format does not automatically mean every image should have extreme blur. Focus distance, field of view, aperture geometry, and the intended shot all matter.

Use f-number for the geometric entrance-pupil relationship. T-stop additionally describes transmission and must not be substituted blindly into the circle-of-confusion equation. A lens profile may store both when supported by evidence. A creative interface may present cinema-style terminology, but the internal model must remain dimensionally correct.

For a thin-lens reference with focal length `f`, f-number `N`, finite focus distance `s`, and object distance `u`, all lengths in the same units, a signed defocus diameter can be written:

```text
c = f*f / (N*(s-f)) * (1 - s/u)
```

The convention in this directive makes nearer objects negative and farther objects positive. The magnitude is the diameter, not the radius. Convert to output pixels using the corresponding virtual-gate width and output width. At the focus plane the value is zero; at positive infinity the expression has a finite limit. Reject impossible geometry rather than returning a plausible arbitrary blur.

For a horizontal virtual gate width `g` and horizontal field of view `theta`, the compatible focal length is:

```text
f = g / (2*tan(theta/2))
```

This relationship does not move the camera. Perspective depends on viewpoint; ARRI's lens technical explanation identifies the entrance pupil as the center of perspective. The app must preserve the captured viewpoint and explain any crop required by a virtual-lens selection.[^C02]

### 4.7 Existing source blur

The phone source already contains its own optical blur, motion blur, sampling, and processing. A renderer cannot generally make an out-of-focus source sharply focused merely by selecting a virtual focus plane. The initial capture guidance should favor a suitable source with enough genuine detail for the desired effect.

Do not subtract arbitrary blur radii as though all optical point-spread functions were Gaussian and independent. A variance-subtraction approximation may be investigated for a specifically declared Gaussian model, but it is not a universal lens-matching method. Exact matching of a target point-spread function can be impossible when the source has already discarded the required spatial information.

### 4.8 Relative depth and metric depth

A monocular model may return relative depth or relative inverse depth with an arbitrary scale and offset. The model interface must declare which representation it uses. A depth value of two is not two metres unless a validated metric contract says so.

For relative operation, offer a focus target and a bounded creative aperture or blur control without fabricated physical-distance readouts. For metric operation, define a calibration procedure with known geometry, uncertainty, and held-out validation. A scale fitted from one convenient scene must not silently become a universal phone calibration.

Temporal processing must account for scale changes. Independent min-max normalization per frame is prohibited as a default because a new near object can change all apparent depth relationships even when the background is stationary. Use robust alignment over valid correspondences, and reset or reduce confidence when the alignment is not supported.

### 4.9 Spectral and film-response limits

Three RGB values do not uniquely specify the incoming spectral distribution. Consequently, reconstructing how a different film emulsion would respond requires assumptions. A useful renderer can model broad photographic behavior and match controlled references without claiming exact spectral equivalence under arbitrary lighting.

Kodak's technical material includes sensitometric and spectral information under stated conditions. Such data informs model development, but it is not a complete, universal specification of every finished image made from that stock. Batch variation, exposure, development, printing, scanning, lighting, and camera optics remain relevant. Our profile must document which variables are represented and which are approximated.[^F03]

### 4.10 Film format versus stock versus finishing

Format controls the image-area geometry and its relationship to sampling and optics. Stock controls the selected material interpretation. Development controls modify the declared negative response. Printing and scanning control subsequent rendering. A final grade is another operation. The user may combine them creatively, but the data model must preserve their independence.

Kodak's production accounts distinguish five-perforation and fifteen-perforation 65mm acquisition and describe multiple stock choices within individual films. This supports a recipe model with multiple variants, not one universal movie LUT.[^F04][^F05]


<a id="architecture"></a>
## 5. System architecture and ownership contracts

### 5.1 Extend the existing application by seams, not by replacement

Start with the inspected repository, not a new demonstration project. The current documentation describes a Kotlin/XML application, saved RAW development, recording safeguards, and evidence reports. These are continuity obligations, not proof that every implementation is correct. Before editing an interface, inspect its actual source and callers. Record the revision against which the change is designed. If a documentation claim and source behavior disagree, add a characterization test and resolve the discrepancy explicitly.[^R01][^R02]

Organize responsibilities into logical components: capture planning, camera ownership, immutable acquisition, raw development, color transforms, render graph, model inference, virtual optics, film rendering, media jobs, catalogue, presentation, and evidence. These do not have to become separate Gradle modules. Initially, packages and narrow interfaces within the existing module may be sufficient. A new module must justify its build cost, ownership boundary, dependency direction, and independent testability.

The application-facing contracts should exchange explicit values and resource leases rather than share mutable global state. No component may discover its source interpretation by reading the current UI label. No renderer may infer whether a frame is RAW-derived from its filename. No catalogue recipe may reach into the recorder and silently change the acquisition mode. The user must see and accept changes affecting capture reliability, source lineage, field of view, audio, or storage.

### 5.2 Three product planes

The **acquisition plane** protects the source. It owns the selected camera route, session, image callbacks, encoder inputs, audio reader, clocks, bounded queues, and staging publication. Its priority is integrity. It may stop explicitly rather than silently change the requested source contract.

The **interpretation plane** turns that source into a declared working representation and then a selected appearance. It owns calibration, transforms, depth, motion, optics, stock models, grain, print rendering, and delivery. Its results must be reproducible from retained source plus a complete graph description. Expensive interpretation should be schedulable after acquisition.

The **interaction and evidence plane** owns user choices, previews, progress, searchable clips, accessible controls, provenance, and reports. It must not block camera callbacks with file browsing, thumbnail generation, model download, catalogue updates, or UI work. It exposes uncertainty instead of hiding it behind a cinematic name.

### 5.3 Capture plane contracts

A `CapturePlan` is immutable. It includes device and build identity; logical and requested physical route; ordinary or special sensor mode; stream sizes and formats; dynamic-range profile; frame-rate strategy; codec identity and input interface; audio selection; stabilization intent; orientation; and required evidence policy. A plan can be a candidate without being selectable for ordinary recording.

A `CaptureSessionOwner` serializes state transitions and owns native resources. Every asynchronous callback carries a generation token. The owner rejects callbacks belonging to a replaced session. Stopping is a terminal intent for that generation: a delayed first frame cannot return the application to recording. The transition from starting to recording requires the selected tracks to have actually produced acknowledged output, not merely an accepted start request.

Image ownership is explicit. A callback either transfers a lease to a bounded worker or releases it before returning. A worker must not access a released image. A retained source writer receives application-owned bytes or an explicitly owned image resource, never an undocumented borrowed pointer. When a queue reaches its limit, the policy is documented: optional preview may drop, but an archival source path must account for every missing frame or stop. A preview policy must never be reused silently for RAW acquisition.

Audio has an independent resource owner and bounded handoff. The requested track cannot disappear silently after permission denial, microphone silencing, or route failure. The user can choose video-only explicitly. A metadata timestamp test and a physical sound/light synchronization test answer different questions and need separate evidence.

### 5.4 Working-image and graph contracts

A `WorkingImageDescriptor` must include dimensions, crop, orientation, primaries, white point, transfer state, scene/display relationship, channel layout, precision, alpha convention, timestamp, source lineage, and calibration state. The graph compiler rejects incompatible edges before processing media. Implicit conversions are prohibited unless represented as named nodes in the saved graph.

Use a directed acyclic graph for spatial and color operations, with separately declared temporal state. Each node declares input and output descriptors, numerical domain, required neighborhood, precision needs, determinism, temporal context, allocation estimate, and failure policy. Parameters are immutable during a frame. A user edit creates a new graph version rather than mutating a running job's interpretation halfway through the export.

The graph must support a clean master branch and a display-preview branch independently. Preview overlays, false color, scopes, focus peaking, safe-area guides, and display tone mapping must not appear in the clean source unless the user explicitly requests a separately identified burn-in export. The selected monitoring transform is not automatically the archival transform.

Spatial ordering must be intentional. Lens effects, film exposure response, density-dependent texture, and print rendering are not generally interchangeable operations. A development change that reorders them needs a named graph migration and comparison evidence. A visually attractive result does not excuse an undocumented mathematical change.

### 5.5 Model service contracts

A model package contains a weight hash, implementation version, architecture identifier, license record, input normalization, supported dimensions, output semantics, quantization description, delegate requirements, and test-vector identity. Downloading a new file with the same display name must not change an existing job's result.

A model service reports initialization, ready, unavailable, failed, and cancelled states distinctly. It must verify the exact model before use, reject malformed tensors, and respect memory budgets. Delegate selection is a tested backend choice. A failed accelerator route may use a separately tested CPU route if the user-facing performance and quality implications are explicit; it must not pretend the original delegate succeeded.

Depth inference, optical flow, matting, and segmentation are different tasks. Their outputs must remain distinguishable in the data model. A person mask cannot stand in for a full depth map. A depth map cannot establish semantic identity. A flow field is not valid through every occlusion. The renderer must consume confidence and validity information alongside estimates.

### 5.6 Media-job ownership

A development job owns a source reference, verified source hash or stable identity policy, graph version, profiles, models, output contract, checkpoint, and cancellation token. Its checkpoint must identify the last durable completed output interval, the required temporal warm-up, and the hashes of all state-defining inputs. A recipe edit, source replacement, or model update invalidates incompatible checkpoints.

Do not append blindly to an arbitrary partially written MP4. A resumable design may use independently finalized intermediate chunks followed by verified assembly, or another explicitly supported container strategy. The implementation must prove timestamp continuity, audio handling, overlap trimming, temporal-state reconstruction, and output uniqueness. If the chosen format is not safely resumable, restart the derived output while retaining the source and explaining the reason.

Publication is a transaction, not a filename change alone. The application must distinguish processing complete, verification complete, durable local result, provider copy complete, published, and cleanup complete. Android shared-media APIs supply relevant pending-publication and storage mechanisms, but the exact provider behavior must be tested. A sidecar error must not delete a successfully retained original.[^A07]

### 5.7 Catalogue boundaries

The catalogue is local-first and versioned. A movie entry has stable identity, alternate titles, source references, acquisition claims, scene variants, reconstructed rendering parameters, rights state, and confidence. Search operates on these records without requiring camera permissions or uploading user footage.

A recipe is a composition of independently identified format, stock interpretation, lens interpretation, processing, and finishing parameters. It can suggest capture settings but cannot force a hidden change. Unsupported settings remain visible as suggestions with explanations. A recipe designed for daylight must not quietly rewrite tungsten footage as if it had been captured under daylight illumination.

Catalogue synchronization, if added, is separate from local capture and development. A network failure must not disable already installed recipes or models. An update must preserve earlier versions referenced by saved jobs, or provide an explicit migration that generates a new job rather than altering historical output provenance.

<a id="tdd-method"></a>
## 6. Test-driven development as the governing method

### 6.1 The required development cycle

Every implementation phase follows this sequence: inspect the relevant production seam; formulate an observable claim; construct a deterministic fixture; establish an independent oracle; write a test that fails for the intended missing behavior; capture that failure; implement the smallest coherent change; run the focused test; run regression tests; refactor without changing the contract; perform the relevant integration or hardware experiment; publish evidence and remaining limits.

A failing test caused by a misspelled import is not sufficient evidence that the requested behavior was missing. The red state must reach the intended assertion or a clearly identified unimplemented boundary. If a test already passes, determine whether the behavior is present, whether the test is weak, or whether the fixture misses the condition. Do not introduce a regression merely to manufacture a red screenshot.

Tests are production artifacts. Keep them readable, named by behavior, and small enough to explain their oracle. Favor several focused examples over one giant test that catches all exceptions. Assertions must inspect meaningful results: decoded sample values, source bytes, frame identities, state transitions, recovery artifacts, or rendered differences in an explicitly declared domain.

The executable reference appendix demonstrates a real red/green host cycle. It is not a substitute for applying this cycle inside the Android repository. Its numerical functions and state models are reference contracts; its synthetic images and toy film response are not calibrated S23 or Kodak models.

### 6.2 Evidence classes

Use at least these classes: static inspection; pure host unit test; property or fuzz test; CPU reference comparison; GPU differential test; codec encode/decode test; emulator instrumentation; physical-phone functional test; sustained physical recording test; controlled color/optics experiment; independently reviewed perceptual study; and external-consumer interoperability test.

A class does not automatically dominate all lower classes. A physical screenshot may provide less useful evidence about numerical precision than an independently decoded ramp. Conversely, a perfect arithmetic unit test says nothing about whether a camera route supplies genuine ten-bit source data. The claim and its evidence must match.

Outcomes are `passed`, `failed`, `blocked`, `unavailable`, `not_run`, and `inconclusive`, with a reason and artifact references. `Unavailable` means the specified capability or test environment could not be exercised; it is not a successful test. `Inconclusive` means the experiment ran but did not distinguish the hypotheses. Both are legitimate research outcomes.

### 6.3 Independent oracles

An oracle must not simply reproduce the same implementation in another function. For LogC arithmetic, use published reference values and independently written inverse/forward checks. For P010 packing, inspect bytes directly with a separate unpacker. For frame timing, use exact rational arithmetic and decoded timestamps rather than a timer driven by the same UI clock. For publication, inspect retained files and provider-visible results after injected failures.

For film appearance, distinguish numerical invariants from perceptual judgments. Monotonic density, deterministic grain coordinates, bounded energy, and stable neutral handling can have automated oracles. Whether a particular reconstruction resembles a desired release print requires reference material, controlled viewing, and human judgment. Do not hide that judgment inside an unexplained similarity score.

For depth-aware optics, synthetic layered scenes provide known geometry. Real scenes provide difficult boundaries and natural appearance. Both are necessary. Synthetic success cannot certify hair, glass, reflections, or motion blur. Human preference cannot certify metric depth accuracy.

### 6.4 Negative controls and mutation testing

Every claim susceptible to a superficially plausible false pass needs a deliberate negative control. A ten-bit container containing eight-bit-degraded values is a negative control for precision. Correct average cadence with duplicated frames is a negative control for timing. A movie title attached to an arbitrary LUT is a negative control for provenance. A fresh depth estimate with independently normalized scale each frame is a negative control for temporal stability.

A mutation is a deliberately introduced defect representing the failure the test should catch. Examples include replacing conjunction with disjunction in certification, removing a generation check, moving exposure after the negative curve, swapping chroma range, using tile-local random seeds, discarding confidence masks, or publishing before verification. The mutation must fail the appropriate test. Remove it immediately after the experiment; do not commit defective production code.

Mutation testing is evidence about test sensitivity, not proof that all possible defects are covered. Record which mutation was tried, where it was applied, which assertion detected it, and whether other tests also failed. A test that only notices a crash may still miss a silent corruption variant.

### 6.5 Property, boundary, and metamorphic tests

Use properties where exact expected images are unnecessary. Examples: a finite monotonic exposure encoding should preserve ordering; an inverse should approximately recover its input within the stated domain; padding must not change decoded pixels; a no-op graph should preserve the source interpretation; changing preview overlays must not change clean-master pixels; a focus plane should produce zero ideal geometric defocus; and a resumed deterministic render should match uninterrupted output under its declared tolerance.

Metamorphic tests compare related inputs. Doubling a synthetic incident exposure before a film model should correspond to one stop in that model's exposure domain. Changing output resolution while retaining the virtual film geometry should preserve the intended physical grain scale after appropriate resampling. Reordering asynchronous callbacks should not resurrect a stopped recorder. Renaming a profile should not change its content identity.

Boundaries include zero-length media, one-frame clips, odd crops, padded strides, negative channels, highlights above one, nonfinite values, extreme but permitted aperture values, missing metadata, cancelled permission prompts, interrupted writes, and unavailable delegates. The default response to ambiguous or malformed data should be explicit rejection, not an invented identity transform.

### 6.6 Golden images and their limitations

A golden image must have a provenance record identifying source, graph, environment, backend, and tolerance. It must not be regenerated automatically merely because the test failed. A change to a golden requires a documented explanation, side-by-side review, and evidence that the intended contract changed or the old reference was incorrect.

Compare in a meaningful domain. An eight-bit screenshot is not a suitable sole reference for a high-precision Log transform. A lossy delivery file is not a lossless source oracle. A display-referred difference may overemphasize harmless rounding or understate out-of-gamut clipping. The test report must identify the domain, spatial alignment, range handling, and any excluded pixels.

Use small, inspectable fixtures for continuous integration and larger sequences for scheduled or manually triggered hardware work. Keep deterministic seeds and content hashes. Do not bundle copyrighted movie frames merely because they are convenient goldens; use owned, licensed, synthetic, or otherwise appropriately authorized material.

### 6.7 Statistical and perceptual discipline

Do not summarize a sequence only by its average. Report relevant maxima, percentiles, temporal clustering, and failure counts. A single dropped archival frame may matter even when average frame rate is correct. A short burst of edge flicker may dominate perceived quality while mean image error remains low.

For comparative viewing, use identical source footage, matched output dimensions, appropriate display transforms, randomized order, and concealed implementation labels where practical. Record the number of viewers and clips, the question asked, viewing conditions, and uncertainty. A small informal panel is useful design feedback but not a universal superiority claim.

Do not select thresholds after seeing which values allow the implementation to pass. Establish provisional thresholds before the experiment, label them as project policy, and revise them only through a recorded decision. A threshold change must not erase the original failure or retroactively certify previously rejected output.

<a id="development-order"></a>
## 7. Development order, dependency gates, and milestone releases

### 7.1 Phases are work packages, not a waterfall calendar

The 160 phases in this directive are ordered work packages with explicit contracts. They are not estimates of days, weeks, or staffing. Many can proceed in parallel after their shared foundations are stable. The dependency graph, not the phase number alone, determines readiness.

The imported-footage renderer can advance while RAW throughput remains under investigation. The catalogue schema can advance with synthetic recipes before finished movie reconstructions exist. Depth research can use owned clips before live camera integration. Firmware research must not block the film lab or ordinary supported capture.

A phase can be software-verified while its device qualification remains pending. Keep both states. Do not mark the entire phase production-ready because one test class passed. A release scope may intentionally exclude unfinished capabilities rather than expose them with misleading labels.

### 7.2 Milestone A: trustworthy capture and import foundation

Complete the research charter, evidence vocabulary, repository baseline, capability reporting, core lifecycle protection, and source retention contracts. Preserve existing supported SDR/HLG and saved-RAW behavior. Demonstrate a clean import path and inspectable metadata. This milestone is successful when users can capture or import media without ambiguity about what has been acquired and where it is retained.

Its release gate excludes unverified claims of native Samsung Log, sustained maximum-resolution RAW, or physical color calibration. Unsupported routes remain diagnostic candidates rather than ordinary selectable recording modes. The test artifact must include at least one forced failure that leaves useful footage recoverable.

### 7.3 Milestone B: reference film laboratory

Implement the calibrated working-image interface, basic stock-response abstraction, deterministic texture, format geometry, print/display separation, and nondestructive recipe persistence. Begin with imported footage and CPU references. Introduce GPU acceleration only after reference behavior is established.

Produce coherent Super 16, Super 35, and 65mm interpretations from the same clip before multiplying stock names. Then complete all six requested format options. Every format must have an explicit gate/aspect policy and grain-scale relationship. Default large-format rendering should not inherit aged-film damage merely because that effect looks recognizable.

### 7.4 Milestone C: one reliable virtual lens

Integrate one well-defined depth model and a restrained depth-aware renderer. Stabilize depth scale and boundaries over time. Add focus selection and conservative confidence behavior. Prove the result on complete sequences, not selected frames.

The milestone must include a failure reel: hair, glasses, fences, reflective surfaces, translucent material, crossing subjects, rapid motion, and uncertain depth. Document where the algorithm reduces the effect or requests manual correction. A failure reel is a quality-control artifact, not a marketing asset.

### 7.5 Milestone D: integrated deferred development

Combine capture, retained clean source, versioned graph, model identities, resumable or restart-safe jobs, verified export, and a polished local library. Add a lightweight preview only after resource contention tests show it does not compromise acquisition.

The primary user journey is choose a source or supported capture mode, select a film/lens recipe, preview the intent, retain the original, develop locally, inspect the result, revise nondestructively, and export with an accurate description. A successful job must be reproducible from its manifest.

### 7.6 Milestone E: curated movie recipes and release qualification

Introduce a small, deeply sourced catalogue. Distinguish scene variants, format variants, and finishing interpretations. Review rights before distributing references, profiles, or weights. Validate accessibility, cold-start recovery, storage pressure, upgrade behavior, and release signing ownership.

A movie recipe can be released as a clearly labeled creative reconstruction even when exact production parameters are unknown. It cannot be labeled an exact stock/camera match merely because the film title is famous. The catalogue should explain the known and unknown parts without requiring the user to read a research paper during shooting.

### 7.7 Milestone F: advanced capture and firmware research

Only after a specific, measured bottleneck is identified should the team investigate deeper HAL, driver, or firmware access. Keep this work isolated from the ordinary application. Require device-variant identity, reversible preparation where possible, recovery planning, explicit user authorization for the actual action, and a clear benefit hypothesis.

Samsung documents hardware-backed state that can be affected by unapproved software configurations. Treat this as a meaningful device risk, not an inconvenience to bypass casually. A failed or deferred firmware study does not invalidate the application-level film and optics project.[^S02][^S03]

<a id="data-contracts"></a>
## 8. Data contracts and reproducibility records

### 8.1 Source manifest

A source manifest must identify acquisition class, media identity, byte or chunk hashes, original timestamps, frame count, dimensions, crop, orientation, color interpretation, camera route, requested controls, observed controls, audio selection, calibration references, and capture interruptions. Unknown values must remain unknown. Do not fill absent fields with attractive defaults that later appear measured.

Distinguish the file hash from the source-sequence identity. A remux can change container bytes without changing decoded images; a re-encode can change pixels while preserving a filename. Both facts may matter. The manifest should support explicit relationships such as captured-from, decoded-from, remuxed-from, developed-from, and reconstructed-with.

For long sources, a chunked hash tree or manifest of segment hashes may support bounded verification. Define the exact algorithm, byte ordering, included metadata, and version. The Python reference's sorted JSON serialization is deliberately a local deterministic convention, not a claim of compliance with a broader canonical-JSON standard.

### 8.2 Frame record

A frame record includes an immutable source frame identity, sensor timestamp where available, presentation timestamp, capture-result identity, exposure, sensitivity, focus metadata, white-balance information, dynamic black/white data where relevant, buffer layout, crop, and error flags. The reader must reject impossible lengths before allocation and check consistency between headers and payloads.

Do not pair RAW frames with whichever metadata arrives nearest in wall-clock time. Use the documented matching identity, preserve out-of-order arrival until a bounded decision can be made, and report missing pairs. A metadata timeout must not silently attach another frame's exposure settings.

The frame record must state whether timing represents sensor acquisition, encoder presentation, or a deliberately retimed output. These are related but not interchangeable. The exact original timing must survive development even when a separately labeled constant-frame-rate output is created.

### 8.3 Calibration profile

A profile includes device/build and route applicability, sensor mode, source dimensions, CFA interpretation, active crop, black/white policy, shading and defect models, neutral definition, color transforms, illuminant assumptions, exposure scale, fitting procedure, held-out validation results, uncertainty, and provenance. The status is synthetic, provisional, measured, or independently validated according to explicit criteria.

A manufacturer's matrix snapshot and a neutral patch can provide a useful starting point; they do not establish a complete measured color characterization. A profile with the same phone model name but a different route or firmware must not match automatically. Applicability can be broadened only through evidence and a versioned policy.

Store transforms with their direction, domain, row/column convention, reference white, and adaptation assumptions. A finite, invertible matrix can still be semantically wrong. Tests must include neutral behavior and known color relationships, not only determinant checks.

### 8.4 Render recipe and movie claim

A render recipe contains explicit source requirements, graph version, format geometry, stock interpretation, exposure controls, optical model, depth model, focus behavior, grain seed policy, halation, print/scan parameters, output transform, and user overrides. It must be possible to export a recipe without embedding the user's private footage.

A movie claim contains a proposition, evidence category, source references, scope, confidence, and contradictory information when relevant. For example, a documented stock used somewhere in a production is not automatically the stock used in every scene. A reconstructed contrast curve is not a sourced production fact. The schema should make these distinctions structurally difficult to erase.

Recipe search should support movie title, scene family, format, stock interpretation, lighting context, monochrome/color, and installed availability. A result should remain usable offline. Do not make an internet lookup part of pressing Record.

### 8.5 Evidence record and completion report

Every test or experiment records a stable identifier, claim, fixture identity, command or protocol, environment, source revision, relevant model/profile/graph hashes, outcome, metric values with units, thresholds and their policy version, artifacts, and limitations. A screenshot may accompany the report but must not replace machine-readable results when those exist.

A completion report summarizes changed behavior, preserved behavior, tests actually executed, negative controls attempted, hardware not available, unresolved failures, and the next dependency-ready work package. It must never describe a future command as an executed result. If a test was not run, say so directly in the record.

<a id="qualification"></a>
## 9. Physical-phone qualification and measurement design

### 9.1 Device identity and test preparation

Record the exact S23 Ultra variant, Android/One UI build, security patch, camera route, battery state, available storage, ambient conditions, case/accessory configuration, codec names, and app revision. Do not generalize one configuration's result to every S23 Ultra. Requalification is required after relevant firmware, codec, calibration, or application changes.

Use owned test scenes and maintain safe operating conditions. Do not disable thermal protection to complete a benchmark. Avoid irreversible settings changes during ordinary app qualification. Keep important media backed up before storage-pressure or upgrade tests. A test should never make the user's irreplaceable footage the only copy of an experimental fixture.

First run short functional tests, inspect their outputs, then progress to longer sustained tests under a declared policy. Duration is a variable in the evidence record, not an automatic guarantee. A five-second recording can establish basic operation but not long-form thermal reliability.

### 9.2 Capability and precision experiments

For each candidate route, record advertised support, configuration success, actual image or sample receipt, independently decoded output, and sustained behavior separately. Use controlled gradients and step patterns to examine the codec path. Include a deliberately degraded lower-precision control. Where source precision is the question, use controlled capture measurements rather than only synthetic encoder input.

A Main10 profile indicates an encoding profile, not necessarily genuine ten-bit information from the sensor. An image can contain more than 256 distinct values after interpolation even when its origin was eight-bit. Therefore, a unique-code count alone is not sufficient. Analyze the known input/output relationship, quantization behavior, negative controls, and the location at which the test enters the pipeline.

Existing repository codec thresholds are project-specific reference gates described by its documentation. Preserve them until a recorded policy change is justified; do not promote them into universal imaging standards. The new renderer needs additional tests for chroma, spatial effects, transfer interpretation, and source lineage.[^R02]

### 9.3 Timing and audiovisual synchronization

Measure original sensor cadence, encoder presentation cadence, decoded frame sequence, and physical sound/light synchronization independently. Include stationary and moving patterns so duplicated frames cannot hide behind identical images. For rational rates, generate expected timestamps from exact frame indices rather than repeatedly adding a rounded interval.

A physical synchronization fixture should provide a repeatable event visible to the camera and audible to the microphone. Record the event generation method and its uncertainty. Analyze multiple events across the clip to distinguish fixed offset from drift. Container start times alone are not proof of lip synchronization.

If the application intentionally creates constant-frame-rate output from acceptable source timing, preserve the original timestamp series and state the mapping. Frame duplication, interpolation, or speed changes must be explicit user-visible processing choices, never silent repairs used to pass a recording benchmark.

### 9.4 Color characterization

Use a controlled illuminant, stable exposure, known neutral references, and suitable color targets. Record lighting spectrum or the limits of its characterization, target identity and condition, geometry, flare control, and measurement repeatability. Divide fitting and validation data. A fit evaluated only on its own training patches does not establish generalization.

Report error distributions and failure regions rather than one attractive mean. Examine neutral scale, skin-like colors, saturated objects, mixed lighting, highlights, and shadows separately. Any denoising, sharpening, lens shading, or tone mapping in the acquisition path must be acknowledged because it affects the relationship being characterized.

Do not claim ARRI-equivalent dynamic range from a Log curve or a grey patch. Define the dynamic-range measurement method, noise criterion, exposure sequence, clipping criterion, and uncertainty before measuring. Results describe the tested route and processing policy, not an abstract phone sensor detached from its actual readout.

### 9.5 Virtual-lens evaluation

Create a layered static scene with known distances and fine boundary structure, followed by moving scenes that challenge occlusion and temporal consistency. Include bright point sources for bokeh, foreground objects, textured backgrounds, hair-like structures, glass, reflective surfaces, and subjects crossing each other.

Evaluate focus-plane accuracy only when the depth contract is metric. For relative depth, assess ordering, stability, and consistency with the selected artistic control. Never score a relative-depth model as physically accurate by assigning arbitrary units after the fact.

Inspect normal-speed playback, slow playback, and selected diagnostic views. Normal playback reveals distracting pumping; diagnostic views locate the cause. Retain confidence, depth, flow, and matting outputs for development, but do not expose private diagnostic imagery outside the user's device without permission.

### 9.6 Reliability and recovery

Exercise permission denial, camera interruption, rotation, activity recreation, application backgrounding according to supported policy, storage pressure, thermal warnings, process death, encoder failure, provider write failure, and cancelled development. The primary question is what survives and how accurately it is labeled.

A playable partial file is not automatically a verified completed take. A failed sidecar write is not permission to destroy the media. Recovery interfaces must distinguish original sources, verified outputs, unverified partials, and absent files. Deletion requires an explicit user action with enough context to avoid confusing an original with a regenerable derivative.

<a id="performance"></a>
## 10. Performance engineering without unsupported promises

### 10.1 Budget the whole pipeline

Measure camera acquisition, buffer import, color conversion, model inference, temporal processing, optical rendering, film rendering, encoding, storage, and UI separately and together. Include initialization, warm-up, steady state, and sustained thermal behavior. A fast isolated model is not proof of a fast camera application.

Use bytes and time units explicitly. A 3840 by 2160 RGBA buffer with four sixteen-bit channels occupies 66,355,200 bytes, approximately 63.28 MiB. At 7680 by 4320, the same layout occupies approximately 253.13 MiB. Two such 8K buffers plus one full-resolution float32 depth map already require approximately 632.81 MiB, before codec surfaces, models, staging buffers, and the rest of the application. These are arithmetic examples, not measured S23 allocations.

This motivates tiling, bounded pools, reduced-resolution inference, edge-aware refinement, and deferred work. It does not justify silently lowering archival quality. Each approximation must have a declared effect and comparison test.

### 10.2 Tiling and temporal context

A tile needs enough halo for every spatial operation it contains. Blur, halation, resampling, demosaic, and edge refinement have different support requirements. The graph compiler should derive the combined required neighborhood rather than rely on a universal guessed overlap. Stochastic texture must use global coordinates so changing tile dimensions does not change the image.

Temporal chunks need context too. A resumed depth or denoising job may need earlier frames to reconstruct state. Process the context, discard duplicate overlap output, and emit each intended frame exactly once. Scene cuts require explicit state reset or transition behavior. A checkpoint that stores only a frame number is insufficient for a stateful renderer unless the state can be deterministically reconstructed.

### 10.3 Quality modes

Define quality modes by measurable algorithms and budgets, not adjectives alone. A live mode may use smaller depth input, fewer optical samples, and simplified halation. A development mode may use higher-quality matting, larger support, more samples, and fuller precision. Both must preserve the same recipe semantics where possible and document unavoidable differences.

The preview must not imply that the final result will be identical when it is only approximate. Show a restrained status such as preview quality and allow inspection of a developed short segment. Do not let optional scopes or thumbnails consume resources reserved for capture finalization.

### 10.4 Thermal and cancellation policy

Android provides thermal-status mechanisms, but the application must define and test its own response. Reduce optional preview work before altering acquisition. If the source contract cannot be maintained safely, stop in a controlled manner, finalize what can be finalized, and retain recoverable data. Never disable system protection to preserve a frame-rate claim.[^A09]

Cancellation is a normal state transition. Check it at bounded intervals and release resources in a documented order. A cancellation request must not delete the original, leak a model context, leave an accepted filename on an incomplete output, or prevent the next job from starting. Measure cancellation latency and report uninterruptible operations explicitly.

<a id="agent-execution"></a>
## 11. Operating instructions for implementation agents

### 11.1 Before each work session

Read the charter, the current evidence index, the selected phase, its dependencies, and the relevant production files. Inspect the repository status and preserve unrelated changes. Establish whether the requested action includes repository writes or only analysis. This directive does not itself authorize destructive changes, remote publication, firmware modification, account operations, or release-key handling.

Select one dependency-ready vertical slice. A slice should connect a real input to an observable output and evidence, not merely add a collection of unused classes. Prefer completing one verified path over scaffolding every future option. Keep the existing capture route functional while adding an experimental renderer behind an explicit feature boundary.

Do not ingest this entire long document into every development context. Use its phase index, stable anchors, and machine-readable companion records. Read the active workstream and cross-cutting contracts that affect it. The document is a reference system, not a requirement to repeatedly pay the context cost of all laboratory cases.

### 11.2 During implementation

Write the focused failing test before changing the behavior. Capture the red result, implement, and capture green. If hardware is required but absent, implement testable contracts and report the hardware gate pending. Do not replace a physical test with a mock and retain the physical-test name.

Keep code comments explanatory rather than promotional. Explain units, ownership, non-obvious constraints, and failure policies. Avoid comments claiming cinematic quality, sensor equivalence, or production readiness unless they point to specific evidence and a bounded claim.

When an API differs from the assumed version, inspect the pinned project and current official documentation. Do not upgrade the whole toolchain as the first response. Record compatibility decisions. New dependencies need a purpose, size and licensing review, supported ABI/API range, and removal path.

### 11.3 Integration and handoff

Run focused tests, the relevant existing regression suite, static checks, and build commands appropriate to the change. Report commands actually executed with their outcomes. Distinguish a buildable Android artifact from a tested physical application. Include failed and unavailable checks in the handoff.

When repository writes are explicitly requested, preserve the current branch policy and concurrent work. Inspect the remote head before integrating. Do not force-push or delete branches merely to make the history appear clean. After an authorized push, verify the resulting remote revision rather than assuming the command's intent proves success.

The handoff must contain the selected phase, implemented contracts, source changes, test evidence, negative controls, artifact locations, remaining gates, and next dependency-ready step. Avoid a vague percentage complete unless the denominator is a stable requirement set and the evidence status is explicit.

### 11.4 Prohibited shortcuts

Do not loosen thresholds only to make tests green. Do not delete difficult fixtures. Do not catch every exception and return success. Do not replace missing calibration with an identity matrix. Do not generate a visually flat SDR output and label it sensor Log. Do not infer native resolution from encoded dimensions. Do not mark model inference as offline while making undisclosed network calls. Do not call a reconstructed movie look a measured production profile. Do not hide a lost original behind a successful preview.

A prototype is allowed to be limited. It must label the limitation, preserve data, and expose a clear path to the next experiment. Honest failure is preferable to uninspectable success.

<a id="limitations"></a>
## 12. Research limitations and release ethics

### 12.1 Physical limits

The application cannot manufacture sensor measurements that were clipped, never sampled, obscured, or irreversibly processed away. A larger virtual gate does not enlarge the sensor. A mathematical Log transform does not increase the source's measured dynamic range. A depth estimator does not guarantee metric geometry. A synthetic bokeh renderer cannot reliably observe all background light that a physically larger aperture would have collected.

These limits do not make the product uninteresting. The intended achievement is a coherent, controllable approximation of photographic appearance with strong capture hygiene and transparent uncertainty. Evaluate it on what it actually produces rather than on an impossible claim of hardware transformation.

### 12.2 Scientific and perceptual limits

Manufacturer curves, published algorithms, and production accounts provide valuable constraints, but they do not uniquely determine a finished movie image. Reference releases may differ. Lighting, lenses, filtration, development, printing, scanning, grading, compression, and display all contribute. A reconstruction should state which layers it models.

The scholarly parts of this directive distinguish sourced facts from proposed engineering policy. The phase specifications are normative proposals, not claims that every technique is already implemented or validated. The expanded laboratory cases are test plans, not executed experiments. Only the explicitly identified companion reference tests were run while producing this artifact.

### 12.3 Rights, privacy, and distribution

Review the exact code, weights, profiles, LUTs, textures, reference images, and names intended for distribution. A repository license does not automatically cover every bundled asset. A research paper's publication does not itself settle implementation licensing or patent questions. Record provenance and obtain qualified review where necessary; this directive is not a legal clearance opinion.

Default to local processing and minimal permissions. Keep user footage, faces, depth maps, and diagnostic captures private. If optional telemetry is later introduced, make it explicit, bounded, and separate from core operation. No cloud video-generation service is required for the proposed product.

### 12.4 Product truthfulness

Use concise user-facing labels supported by deeper inspectable reports. Examples include RAW-derived, HDR-derived, SDR-derived, provisional calibration, reconstructed stock interpretation, approximate preview, and unverified recovery clip. Avoid turning every uncertainty into a warning wall, but never conceal it behind a confident badge.

The release decision should reward stable, well-characterized behavior. A smaller set of convincing film and lens interpretations, supported by reliable capture and recovery, is a stronger foundation than a large catalogue of names attached to fragile effects.
