### P061. Separate HLG-derived development from RAW development

**Entry gate:** P060. **Primary seam:** LogC reference, signal descriptor, P010 packing, codec and editor validation.

**Research objective.** Offer a useful HDR-derived route without falsely describing ISP-processed footage as unprocessed sensor data.

**Implementation method.** Inspect source tags, decode the actual transfer and color representation, and preserve the fact that upstream ISP processing may not be invertible. Keep source lineage in every recipe and output. Do not invent missing scene values from flattened SDR.

**Test-first fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Acceptance oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply one inverse curve to every source regardless of metadata.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Source normalization router and lineage assertions. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p061-01"></a>
#### TC-P061-01. Wrong LogC domain coefficients

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Use a coefficient set belonging to a different input convention while retaining the LogC3 label.

**Required response.** Fail independent black, grey, branch, and inverse tests before producing an accepted export.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Using sensor-signal coefficients on exposure-domain values must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat near the branch cut and with highlights above scene-linear one.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p061-02"></a>
#### TC-P061-02. Eight-bit data in ten-bit storage

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Quantize the source or intermediate to eight bits before packing into a Main10 output.

**Required response.** Fail useful precision qualification despite the ten-bit container and profile indication.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Bitstream depth metadata alone must not establish ten-bit image fidelity.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat at camera input, GPU texture, bitmap conversion, and codec input boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p061-03"></a>
#### TC-P061-03. Range and matrix contradiction

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Provide a sidecar and stream whose range, YUV matrix, transfer, or RGB gamut disagree.

**Required response.** Reject contradictory accepted metadata and require a documented interoperable interpretation.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Rec.709 YUV coefficients must not imply Rec.709 RGB primaries automatically.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with full/video level confusion and an incorrect HLG transfer tag.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p061-04"></a>
#### TC-P061-04. P010 plane geometry fault

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Change row stride, crop, plane arrangement, or sample alignment while keeping nominal dimensions.

**Required response.** Handle only explicitly supported layouts with bounds checks and exact unpacked-code verification.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Writing ten-bit values into the low six-bit-aligned position must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with padded rows, chroma endpoints, and unsupported plane layouts.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p061-05"></a>
#### TC-P061-05. Unconsented clipping

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Supply encoded or intermediate values outside the selected delivery domain without clipping permission.

**Required response.** Reject or request an explicit clipping policy and record affected counts when clipping is authorized.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Silently clamping highlights while claiming full retained range must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with negative channels, saturated colors, and extreme exposure adjustments.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p061-06"></a>
#### TC-P061-06. Source-lineage laundering

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Export an SDR or HLG-derived source under a RAW-derived or native-camera-equivalent label.

**Required response.** Reject the label even when the final file is ten-bit and visually flat.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Changing the encoding cannot upgrade the source acquisition category.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat through import, recipe selection, export naming, and shared metadata.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p061-07"></a>
#### TC-P061-07. Double viewing transform

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Apply a display or log transform twice through preview, development, or editor configuration.

**Required response.** Detect the mismatch using reference patches and preserve separate clean and rendered branches.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** A generic player thumbnail must not certify correct color interpretation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with manual editor assignments and automatically detected source tags.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p061-08"></a>
#### TC-P061-08. Consumer round-trip discrepancy

**Baseline fixture.** The same visible frame supplied as declared HLG, SDR, and an untagged imported video.

**Adversarial operation.** Decode or import the accepted file in an independent consumer using the documented settings.

**Required response.** Match the declared numeric and visual reference within the stated codec and transform tolerance.

**Baseline oracle.** Each path receives its correct or explicitly unresolved interpretation; none is silently promoted to RAW-derived Log.

**False-pass control.** Successful file opening alone must not count as interoperability.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exact consumer versions, range settings, and sidecar availability.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p062"></a>
### P062. Implement display and Log export branches

**Entry gate:** P061. **Primary seam:** LogC reference, signal descriptor, P010 packing, codec and editor validation.

**Research objective.** Keep a clean grading master and a rendered film result conceptually and operationally separate.

**Implementation method.** Branch from a declared working image. The clean Log export excludes film grain, halation, virtual-lens rendering, and display tone mapping unless an explicitly named processed master is selected. The rendered delivery has its own output transform and reproducible recipe.

**Test-first fixture.** A take exported once as a clean Log master and again with strong grain, halation, and virtual defocus.

**Acceptance oracle.** The clean master remains unaffected while the rendered result records all processing stages.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply the display transform before both branches and call one output clean Log.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Output graph policies and branch-independence tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

Marketing text must not imply sensor enlargement, guaranteed ARRI equivalence, or recovered clipped detail.

**Test-first fixture.** A rendered SDR import exported with a large-format recipe and a ten-bit codec.

**Acceptance oracle.** The interface identifies a simulated look from an SDR source rather than native large-format or sensor-derived Log capture.

**Deliberate mutation.** Build export labels only from the selected film preset name.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Claim linter and source-aware product wording. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="workstream-09"></a>
## Workstream 09. GPU execution, precision, and render scheduling

Acceleration is accepted only after it reproduces declared mathematics and respects capture budgets. Select the first backend from measured compatibility, not prestige. The existing application may already provide an EGL path; preserve useful infrastructure and add a graph boundary around it. Benchmark intermediate formats and synchronization because implicit conversions can be more damaging than an obviously slow shader. A fast preview and a high-quality developer need related but separately declared quality policies.

**Integration seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling. **Accountable specialty:** GPU and scheduling engineer.

**Measurement domain:** differential error, resource lifetime, bounded memory, and sustained throughput. **Evidence family:** backend capabilities, fence traces, graph descriptors, tiled goldens, and full-pipeline timings.

**Primary background:** [^A04][^A05][^A09][^R01] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p065"></a>
### P065. Define a typed render graph

**Entry gate:** P049, P056, P060. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Prevent incompatible signal domains and geometry from being connected silently.

**Implementation method.** Give every node declared input and output descriptors, precision requirements, spatial halo, temporal context, and deterministic parameters. Validate graph edges before allocation. Nodes report whether they alter geometry, exposure, color, texture, or time.

**Test-first fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Acceptance oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**Deliberate mutation.** Represent all intermediate images as untyped texture handles.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Render graph schema and static compatibility validator. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p065-01"></a>
#### TC-P065-01. Unsupported precision format

**Baseline fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Adversarial operation.** Remove a required renderable or importable format while leaving the graphics API otherwise available.

**Required response.** Report the specific backend route unavailable or choose a separately qualified alternative.

**Baseline oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**False-pass control.** Silently replacing a high-precision intermediate with RGBA8 must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with missing extensions, incompatible surfaces, and unavailable image imports.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p065-02"></a>
#### TC-P065-02. Accumulated floating-point error

**Baseline fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Adversarial operation.** Run signed, high-range, and cancellation-sensitive values through repeated or wide-support operations.

**Required response.** Remain inside the declared error budget or promote the affected stage to sufficient precision.

**Baseline oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**False-pass control.** Using FP16 everywhere without differential validation must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with long blur accumulations, matrices, and highlight reconstruction attempts.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p065-03"></a>
#### TC-P065-03. In-flight resource reuse

**Baseline fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Adversarial operation.** Delay completion while the resource pool attempts to recycle a texture or buffer for a newer frame.

**Required response.** Honor ownership and synchronization so neither stale nor partially written data reaches accepted output.

**Baseline oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**False-pass control.** Recycling immediately after command submission must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat during cancellation, context loss, and rapid mode switching.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p065-04"></a>
#### TC-P065-04. Tile seam stress

**Baseline fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Adversarial operation.** Position structured detail and bright impulses exactly on tile boundaries with spatial effects enabled.

**Required response.** Match the untiled reference within the declared tolerance using adequate halos and global coordinates.

**Baseline oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**False-pass control.** Independent tile-local random seeds or missing overlap must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat at corners, varying tile sizes, and maximum configured blur radius.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p065-05"></a>
#### TC-P065-05. Temporal chunk discontinuity

**Baseline fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Adversarial operation.** Resume or begin a chunk while a moving object and focus transition cross its boundary.

**Required response.** Reconstruct required context and emit each output frame once with stable temporal behavior.

**Baseline oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**False-pass control.** Empty-history restart at every chunk must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with scene cuts, overlap trimming, and replaced model identities.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p065-06"></a>
#### TC-P065-06. Critical-path resource contention

**Baseline fixture.** A film-density node connected directly to an encoded YUV surface and a display overlay connected to clean-master export.

**Adversarial operation.** Increase inference or preview work until it competes with capture and encoding.

**Required response.** Degrade optional monitoring first while retaining the selected source contract or stopping honestly.

**Baseline oracle.** The graph validator rejects both invalid connections before processing frames.

**False-pass control.** Hidden source frame drops to preserve preview smoothness must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with scopes, denoising, thumbnails, and background file operations.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p065-07"></a>

<a id="p066"></a>
### P066. Select and qualify the first GPU backend

**Entry gate:** P065. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Choose the backend that meets correctness and integration goals on the actual target phone.

**Implementation method.** Compare available EGL/OpenGL ES or Vulkan paths using the same small reference kernels and resource-lifetime tests. Record required extensions and formats. Start with one maintained backend; a second requires a demonstrated coverage or performance benefit.

**Test-first fixture.** A device supporting the API version but lacking a required renderable high-precision format.

**Acceptance oracle.** The backend reports unavailable for that route and retains the CPU reference rather than silently lowering precision.

**Deliberate mutation.** Assume an API version number guarantees every required texture and surface capability.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Backend decision record and capability probe. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p067"></a>
### P067. Validate half and full precision boundaries

**Entry gate:** P066. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Use numerical error budgets to decide where FP16 is sufficient and where FP32 is required.

**Implementation method.** Compare CPU double references with GPU outputs for signed dark values, bright highlights, matrix cancellation, and long accumulations. Test overflow, denormal handling, and texture conversion. Precision reductions must be explicit graph decisions with bounded error.

**Test-first fixture.** A bright narrow highlight convolved with a large kernel and a near-neutral matrix cancellation case.

**Acceptance oracle.** The chosen precision stays within the declared error budget or the graph promotes the affected operation.

**Deliberate mutation.** Replace every intermediate with FP16 without testing accumulated error.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Precision budget and CPU-GPU differential suite. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p068"></a>
### P068. Implement synchronization and ownership barriers

**Entry gate:** P067. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Prevent stale textures, unsafe reuse, and hidden CPU-GPU stalls.

**Implementation method.** Associate each resource with a frame identity and lifetime. Use backend-appropriate fences and barriers, bound in-flight work, and verify completion before reuse or release. Separate correctness synchronization from performance measurements.

**Test-first fixture.** A slow GPU frame followed by rapid cancellation and reuse of the same texture pool slot.

**Acceptance oracle.** The next frame cannot read partially written or previous-generation data and cancellation releases only completed ownership.

**Deliberate mutation.** Recycle a texture immediately after command submission.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** GPU resource owner and delayed-completion tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p069"></a>
### P069. Implement tiled spatial rendering

**Entry gate:** P068. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Support high-resolution development with bounded memory and seam-free spatial effects.

**Implementation method.** Compute each node halo from the maximum kernel support, process overlap regions, and crop only after dependencies finish. Use global coordinates for grain and lens effects. Compare tiled and untiled reference outputs at boundaries and corners.

**Test-first fixture.** A bright impulse centered exactly on a tile boundary with halation, blur, and deterministic grain enabled.

**Acceptance oracle.** The assembled result matches the declared untiled tolerance and contains no seam or repeated grain block.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply every effect independently inside tiles without overlap.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Tile planner and boundary equivalence tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Required response.** Report end-to-end latency and bottlenecks rather than extrapolating from the fastest kernel.

**Baseline oracle.** The assembled result matches the declared untiled tolerance and contains no seam or repeated grain block.

**False-pass control.** A standalone model benchmark must not become a recording frame-rate claim.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat cold, warm, sustained, and thermally constrained runs.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p070"></a>
### P070. Implement temporal chunk boundaries

**Entry gate:** P069. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Make deferred video processing reproducible across chunks and resumed jobs.

**Implementation method.** Declare history and lookahead per temporal node, checkpoint relevant state, and include overlap frames that are not duplicated in final output. Bind caches to source, model, graph, and algorithm identities. Scene cuts invalidate appropriate history.

**Test-first fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Acceptance oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**Deliberate mutation.** Restart the temporal model from an empty state at every export chunk.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Temporal chunk contract and uninterrupted-versus-resumed tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p070-01"></a>
#### TC-P070-01. Unsupported precision format

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Remove a required renderable or importable format while leaving the graphics API otherwise available.

**Required response.** Report the specific backend route unavailable or choose a separately qualified alternative.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Silently replacing a high-precision intermediate with RGBA8 must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with missing extensions, incompatible surfaces, and unavailable image imports.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p070-02"></a>
#### TC-P070-02. Accumulated floating-point error

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Run signed, high-range, and cancellation-sensitive values through repeated or wide-support operations.

**Required response.** Remain inside the declared error budget or promote the affected stage to sufficient precision.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Using FP16 everywhere without differential validation must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with long blur accumulations, matrices, and highlight reconstruction attempts.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p070-03"></a>
#### TC-P070-03. In-flight resource reuse

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Delay completion while the resource pool attempts to recycle a texture or buffer for a newer frame.

**Required response.** Honor ownership and synchronization so neither stale nor partially written data reaches accepted output.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Recycling immediately after command submission must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat during cancellation, context loss, and rapid mode switching.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p070-04"></a>
#### TC-P070-04. Tile seam stress

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Position structured detail and bright impulses exactly on tile boundaries with spatial effects enabled.

**Required response.** Match the untiled reference within the declared tolerance using adequate halos and global coordinates.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Independent tile-local random seeds or missing overlap must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat at corners, varying tile sizes, and maximum configured blur radius.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p070-05"></a>
#### TC-P070-05. Temporal chunk discontinuity

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Resume or begin a chunk while a moving object and focus transition cross its boundary.

**Required response.** Reconstruct required context and emit each output frame once with stable temporal behavior.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Empty-history restart at every chunk must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with scene cuts, overlap trimming, and replaced model identities.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p070-06"></a>
#### TC-P070-06. Critical-path resource contention

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Increase inference or preview work until it competes with capture and encoding.

**Required response.** Degrade optional monitoring first while retaining the selected source contract or stopping honestly.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Hidden source frame drops to preserve preview smoothness must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with scopes, denoising, thumbnails, and background file operations.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p070-07"></a>
#### TC-P070-07. Graphics context loss

**Baseline fixture.** A subject crossing a chunk boundary during a focus pull with a process restart at the boundary.

**Adversarial operation.** Invalidate the backend context or surface during initialization, rendering, or cleanup.

**Required response.** Reach a defined recovery or failure state without publishing unverified frames or leaking resources.

**Baseline oracle.** The resumed output preserves temporal continuity within the declared tolerance and exact frame count.

**False-pass control.** Using stale handles after context recreation must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with retained source availability and a queued development job.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.

<a id="p071"></a>
### P071. Prioritize reliable capture over preview quality

**Entry gate:** P070. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Prevent inference and effects from consuming resources required for source recording.

**Implementation method.** Define resource budgets and degradation order: reduce monitoring work, lower inference frequency, pause optional effects, then stop capture only under its own safety policy. Record which preview quality was active. Never silently alter the selected source recording mode mid-take.

**Test-first fixture.** Increasing inference load while the camera and encoder approach their measured timing budget.

**Acceptance oracle.** The preview degrades visibly and source cadence remains intact until a separately documented capture limit is reached.

**Deliberate mutation.** Lower recording resolution without changing the active mode label.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Resource scheduler and capture-priority stress tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p072"></a>
### P072. Measure full-pipeline performance

**Entry gate:** P071. **Primary seam:** GPU graph, texture formats, synchronization, tiling, scheduling.

**Research objective.** Report end-to-end behaviour rather than isolated shader or model latency.

**Implementation method.** Measure capture, copies, inference, rendering, encoding, decoding, I/O, and queue occupancy together. Warm up where appropriate, retain cold-start results separately, and report sustained thermal state. Compare live and deferred modes as different workflows.

**Test-first fixture.** A fast standalone depth model whose integrated path stalls because of repeated format conversion and memory copies.

**Acceptance oracle.** The report attributes the actual bottleneck and does not advertise standalone inference latency as camera frame rate.

**Deliberate mutation.** Compute end-to-end performance from the fastest individual kernel.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Integrated performance report and optimization priorities. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="workstream-10"></a>
## Workstream 10. Film-negative response and stock modelling

The film engine should distinguish a measured material model from a creative approximation. Start with a compact, testable exposure-to-density system, then improve it with licensed data and independent references. A stock label is not permission to invent exact spectral sensitivity. Separate stock, exposure, processing, and finishing so users can understand what each control changes. The clean source remains outside this irreversible rendering branch.

**Integration seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation. **Accountable specialty:** film-response researcher.

**Measurement domain:** sensitometric coherence, color stability, generalization, and evidence quality. **Evidence family:** exposure wedges, stock parameter versions, owned comparison scenes, and ablation renders.

**Primary background:** [^F01][^F02][^F03] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p073"></a>
### P073. Define stock profiles and evidence levels

**Entry gate:** P007, P049, P056. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Represent stock behaviour independently of virtual format and final film appearance.

**Implementation method.** Store stock family, balance, response model, parameter units, source references, licence state, and confidence. Distinguish measured parameters from reconstructed artistic controls. Keep display names independent of stable profile identifiers and version every numerical change.

**Test-first fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Acceptance oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use a stock marketing name as proof that all numerical parameters are physically measured.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Stock schema and evidence-level validator. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p073-01"></a>
#### TC-P073-01. Stock identity without measurements

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Attach a famous stock name to an unmeasured generic response model.

**Required response.** Keep the model labelled reconstructed or synthetic and separate the name from any calibrated fidelity claim.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** A marketing label alone must not establish measured material behavior.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat for daylight, tungsten, monochrome, and historical-stock interpretations.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p073-02"></a>
#### TC-P073-02. Exposure-domain confusion

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Move exposure adjustment after the negative response while presenting it as incident exposure.

**Required response.** Fail the declared graph contract and expose differing shadow, highlight, and texture behavior.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** One post-LUT contrast control cannot stand in for every physical stage.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exposure, development, printing, and final display grading controls.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p073-03"></a>
#### TC-P073-03. Nonmonotonic density fit

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Introduce a spline overshoot or malformed point that reverses density ordering locally.

**Required response.** Reject or constrain the fit according to the stock model’s declared behavior before release.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** A smooth-looking curve that reverses an exposure wedge must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat near toe, midsection, shoulder, and interpolation endpoints.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p073-04"></a>
#### TC-P073-04. Neutral and saturated stress

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Render neutral steps beside extreme saturated lights under the same stock profile.

**Required response.** Keep neutral behavior controlled and all outputs finite while documenting unsupported spectral accuracy.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** Unbounded cross-channel coupling or hidden per-face correction must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across exposure brackets and several independently captured scenes.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p073-05"></a>
#### TC-P073-05. Overfit reference image

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Tune a stock interpretation to one attractive frame and evaluate it on withheld exposure and scene conditions.

**Required response.** Report generalization failures rather than selecting only favorable comparisons.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** A single successful still must not qualify a stock library.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with skin, foliage, fabric, night lighting, and broad highlights.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p073-06"></a>
#### TC-P073-06. Unrequested beautification

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Enable face smoothing or geometry alteration as an invisible part of a stock look.

**Required response.** Reject hidden content alteration and preserve source texture unless an explicit optional adjustment is selected.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** A flattering result must not hide unrequested facial processing.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with multiple people, skin tones, profile views, and moving faces.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p073-07"></a>
#### TC-P073-07. Unversioned profile change

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Modify numerical stock parameters while retaining an existing immutable recipe identifier.

**Required response.** Create a new profile version and preserve reproducibility of earlier renders.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** Overwriting stable profile bytes in place must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with curve, grain, halation, and print-response changes.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p073-08"></a>
#### TC-P073-08. Clipped-source overclaim

**Baseline fixture.** Two creative interpretations of the same nominal stock with different density curves and uncertain source data.

**Adversarial operation.** Use a source with irreversibly clipped regions and apply a soft film shoulder.

**Required response.** Render the desired appearance while retaining the limitation that missing source detail was not recovered.

**Baseline oracle.** The catalogue exposes them as versioned interpretations rather than falsely identical calibrated materials.

**False-pass control.** Softer highlight appearance must not be reported as recovered sensor information.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with clipped individual channels and fully clipped white regions.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p074"></a>
### P074. Implement an abstract sensitometric reference

**Entry gate:** P073. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Create a stable monotonic exposure-to-density baseline before claiming stock fidelity.

**Implementation method.** Use a documented toy curve with explicit toe, approximately linear midsection, and shoulder parameters. Test monotonicity, continuity, exposure scaling, and finite behaviour. Label the curve synthetic; it is a mathematical fixture, not a Kodak profile.

**Test-first fixture.** A logarithmically spaced exposure wedge spanning shadows, midtones, and highlights.

**Acceptance oracle.** The density response follows its declared monotonic shape and does not invent detail after source clipping.

**Deliberate mutation.** Relabel a generic sigmoid as a measured Vision3 curve.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Abstract density reference and response-curve tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p075"></a>
### P075. Build data ingestion for sensitometry

**Entry gate:** P074. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Import licensed response measurements without confusing plot axes, densities, or exposure conventions.

**Implementation method.** Capture units, reference exposure, measurement conditions, channel interpretation, and digitization uncertainty. Validate monotonic intervals and interpolation behaviour. Retain raw measurement points separately from fitted coefficients and never overwrite original data.

**Test-first fixture.** A curve table with reversed log-exposure order and one point copied in linear exposure units.

**Acceptance oracle.** The importer flags inconsistent axes before producing a stock profile.

**Deliberate mutation.** Fit all numeric columns without inspecting their physical meaning.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Sensitometry importer and unit-consistency checks. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p076"></a>
### P076. Model channel interaction conservatively

**Entry gate:** P075. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Add color response beyond independent tone curves while preserving explicit assumptions.

**Implementation method.** Define whether channel coupling acts on exposure, density, or reconstructed transmission. Fit or tune with held-out references, constrain instability, and separate creative saturation from material response. Document that RGB input cannot uniquely recover the original spectrum.

**Test-first fixture.** Neutral exposures and strongly saturated lights that stress cross-channel response.

**Acceptance oracle.** Neutral behaviour remains controlled, saturated inputs stay finite, and unsupported spectral fidelity is not claimed.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply an arbitrary color matrix after every stage and call the result spectral simulation.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Channel-coupling model and stability tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p077"></a>
### P077. Implement exposure and development controls

**Entry gate:** P076. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Make exposure compensation, push/pull interpretation, and final contrast distinct operations.

**Implementation method.** Exposure changes scale incident scene exposure before the negative response. Development controls modify explicitly modelled material parameters and are labelled approximations unless measured. A final grade acts after the declared finishing stage. Save all three independently.

**Test-first fixture.** Three renders adjusted to similar midtone brightness by exposure, development, and display contrast respectively.

**Acceptance oracle.** The graph records different operations and preserves their different shadow, highlight, and grain consequences.

**Deliberate mutation.** Implement every control as the same post-LUT contrast multiplier.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Exposure-development-grade parameter contract. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

### P078. Protect skin and neutrals without hidden beautification

**Entry gate:** P077. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Avoid unwanted image alteration disguised as film fidelity.

**Implementation method.** First improve stock and camera calibration rather than masking errors with face-specific smoothing. Any optional skin-aware adjustment must be visible, reversible, temporally stable, and excluded from clean masters. Never alter identity or facial geometry.

**Test-first fixture.** Several skin tones under mixed lighting beside neutral and saturated reference objects.

**Acceptance oracle.** The rendering preserves texture and geometry, with optional adjustments clearly recorded and independently switchable.

**Deliberate mutation.** Silently smooth faces to make a film preset appear more flattering.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Skin-texture evaluation and optional adjustment policy. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p079"></a>
### P079. Validate stock behaviour across exposure

**Entry gate:** P078. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Judge an emulation using exposure series rather than one selected attractive still.

**Implementation method.** Render bracketed neutral, skin, fabric, foliage, and highlight scenes with fixed finishing. Compare density response, hue stability, noise interaction, and clipping. Keep an independent validation set and report where the approximation diverges from reference material.

**Test-first fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Acceptance oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**Deliberate mutation.** Remove unfavorable exposure brackets from the comparison set.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Stock exposure-series benchmark and limitation notes. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p079-01"></a>
#### TC-P079-01. Stock identity without measurements

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Attach a famous stock name to an unmeasured generic response model.

**Required response.** Keep the model labelled reconstructed or synthetic and separate the name from any calibrated fidelity claim.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** A marketing label alone must not establish measured material behavior.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat for daylight, tungsten, monochrome, and historical-stock interpretations.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p079-02"></a>
#### TC-P079-02. Exposure-domain confusion

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Move exposure adjustment after the negative response while presenting it as incident exposure.

**Required response.** Fail the declared graph contract and expose differing shadow, highlight, and texture behavior.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** One post-LUT contrast control cannot stand in for every physical stage.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exposure, development, printing, and final display grading controls.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p079-03"></a>
#### TC-P079-03. Nonmonotonic density fit

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Introduce a spline overshoot or malformed point that reverses density ordering locally.

**Required response.** Reject or constrain the fit according to the stock model’s declared behavior before release.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** A smooth-looking curve that reverses an exposure wedge must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat near toe, midsection, shoulder, and interpolation endpoints.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p079-04"></a>
#### TC-P079-04. Neutral and saturated stress

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Render neutral steps beside extreme saturated lights under the same stock profile.

**Required response.** Keep neutral behavior controlled and all outputs finite while documenting unsupported spectral accuracy.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** Unbounded cross-channel coupling or hidden per-face correction must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across exposure brackets and several independently captured scenes.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p079-05"></a>
#### TC-P079-05. Overfit reference image

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Tune a stock interpretation to one attractive frame and evaluate it on withheld exposure and scene conditions.

**Required response.** Report generalization failures rather than selecting only favorable comparisons.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** A single successful still must not qualify a stock library.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with skin, foliage, fabric, night lighting, and broad highlights.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p079-06"></a>
#### TC-P079-06. Unrequested beautification

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Enable face smoothing or geometry alteration as an invisible part of a stock look.

**Required response.** Reject hidden content alteration and preserve source texture unless an explicit optional adjustment is selected.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** A flattering result must not hide unrequested facial processing.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with multiple people, skin tones, profile views, and moving faces.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p079-07"></a>
#### TC-P079-07. Unversioned profile change

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Modify numerical stock parameters while retaining an existing immutable recipe identifier.

**Required response.** Create a new profile version and preserve reproducibility of earlier renders.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** Overwriting stable profile bytes in place must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with curve, grain, halation, and print-response changes.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p079-08"></a>
#### TC-P079-08. Clipped-source overclaim

**Baseline fixture.** A stock interpretation tuned on a correctly exposed portrait but tested several stops under and over that exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Use a source with irreversibly clipped regions and apply a soft film shoulder.

**Required response.** Render the desired appearance while retaining the limitation that missing source detail was not recovered.

**Baseline oracle.** The report exposes failures in shadow color and highlight saturation rather than selecting only the best exposure.

**False-pass control.** Softer highlight appearance must not be reported as recovered sensor information.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with clipped individual channels and fully clipped white regions.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p080"></a>
### P080. Package a small validated stock library

**Entry gate:** P079. **Primary seam:** negative exposure model, density response, stock profiles, validation.

**Research objective.** Prioritize a few coherent profiles over an unverified catalogue of hundreds.

**Implementation method.** Select initial daylight, tungsten, and monochrome interpretations based on available evidence and rights. Freeze profile IDs, add preview thumbnails rendered from owned fixtures, and document calibration status. Require regression renders for every later update.

**Test-first fixture.** A profile update improving one reference scene while breaking a neutral exposure wedge.

**Acceptance oracle.** The update is blocked or released as a distinct experimental profile rather than silently replacing the stable default.

**Deliberate mutation.** Update all presets in place without rendering regression fixtures.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Initial versioned stock pack and profile acceptance report. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="workstream-11"></a>
## Workstream 11. Grain, halation, print rendering, and material texture

Texture must respond to exposure, scale, and processing order instead of behaving like a decorative overlay. Separate photographic grain from phone noise, lens diffusion from emulsion halation, and clean large-format appearance from aged-film damage. Reference algorithms can establish statistical and spatial properties before detailed stock calibration is available. A material model earns its label through measurable behaviour and transparent approximation, not through an exaggerated effect slider.

**Integration seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model. **Accountable specialty:** film-texture and finishing engineer.

**Measurement domain:** texture statistics, spatial scale, energy behavior, and temporal coherence. **Evidence family:** uniform patches, point-light sequences, spectrum measurements, and material-stage ablations.

**Primary background:** [^F01][^F02][^F03] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p081"></a>
### P081. Establish deterministic grain coordinates

**Entry gate:** P065, P073, P080. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Make texture reproducible across tiles, resolutions, retries, and rendering order.

**Implementation method.** Use an explicit take seed and frame identity with global image or virtual-gate coordinates. Counter-based randomness avoids dependence on thread scheduling. Define whether a retimed repeated frame shares its original grain or receives a new simulated exposure; record that policy.

**Test-first fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Acceptance oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**Deliberate mutation.** Reseed the random generator from wall-clock time for every tile.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Grain seed contract and render-order invariance tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p081-01"></a>
#### TC-P081-01. Render-order dependence

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Render the same material effect with different tile ordering, thread scheduling, and restart boundaries.

**Required response.** Preserve the declared deterministic result using stable global coordinates and frame identities.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** Wall-clock or tile-local random seeding must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with a fixed take seed and several independent output resolutions.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p081-02"></a>
#### TC-P081-02. Exposure-independent texture

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Apply the candidate effect across a controlled exposure wedge with identical scene structure.

**Required response.** Match the profile’s declared exposure-dependent statistics rather than an arbitrary constant overlay.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** An effect that ignores its specified density or exposure dependence must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat for neutral, colored, dark, and highlight patches.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p081-03"></a>
#### TC-P081-03. Virtual-format scaling error

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Change virtual gate and output resolution while keeping the same material profile.

**Required response.** Maintain the intended material scale through crop and resampling with no arbitrary pixel-radius substitution.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** Fixed pixel-sized grain across all virtual formats must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat small-format and large-format recipes at preview and final delivery sizes.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p081-04"></a>
#### TC-P081-04. Kernel energy and boundary error

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Place bright emitters near borders and compare the effect at several support radii.

**Required response.** Follow the documented energy and border policy without unexplained brightness growth or tile seams.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** An unnormalized kernel whose energy grows with radius must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat isolated points, broad sources, corners, and partially off-frame emitters.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p081-05"></a>
#### TC-P081-05. Halation and bloom conflation

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Enable only one of the material-halation or optical-diffusion stages, then enable both.

**Required response.** Produce separately controlled, attributable responses rather than identical duplicated glow.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** A red edge outline on all pale objects must not qualify as emulsion halation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with moderate pale surfaces, clipped lights, and saturated emitters.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p081-06"></a>
#### TC-P081-06. Damage in clean defaults

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Load a clean large-format or 35mm recipe with no aging controls selected.

**Required response.** Produce no unrequested scratches, burns, flicker, or gate weave.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** Using damage to make every film preset visibly obvious must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat after preset switching, saved recipe reopening, and reset-to-default.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p081-07"></a>
#### TC-P081-07. Noise mistaken for grain

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Render a noisy source with sensor-noise reduction and material grain controlled independently.

**Required response.** Keep both stages separately inspectable and avoid reporting sensor noise as a calibrated film texture.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** Adding grain to conceal excessive denoising must not pass detail preservation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat low-light skin, smooth walls, and moving fine textures.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p081-08"></a>
#### TC-P081-08. Combined finishing instability

**Baseline fixture.** The same frame rendered as one image, many tiles, and a resumed job using the same recipe.

**Adversarial operation.** Run moving high-contrast scenes through the full negative, texture, halation, print, and display chain.

**Required response.** Remain temporally coherent and allow ablation to identify any stage causing artifacts.

**Baseline oracle.** Grain placement agrees under the declared deterministic contract and never repeats a tile-local pattern.

**False-pass control.** Passing isolated still tests cannot excuse shimmer or hue pumping in the complete clip.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exposure changes, bright object motion, and chunk boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p082"></a>
### P082. Model exposure-dependent grain statistics

**Entry gate:** P081. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Control grain intensity and channel relationships in the appropriate material domain.

**Implementation method.** Begin with synthetic statistical fixtures, then fit licensed reference material. Measure variance, distribution, spatial spectrum, and channel covariance across exposure levels. Keep a simple Gaussian reference clearly labelled as scaffolding rather than physically complete film grain.

**Test-first fixture.** Uniform exposure patches spanning deep shadow through highlights and a neutral color patch.

**Acceptance oracle.** The measured statistics match the profile targets without unwanted hue shifts or repeating overlays.

**Deliberate mutation.** Add identical-strength monochrome noise to every output pixel after display encoding.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Grain-statistics model and exposure-series tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p083"></a>
### P083. Scale grain by virtual gate and delivery geometry

**Entry gate:** P082. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Keep grain size meaningful when switching among small and large film formats.

**Implementation method.** Define grain dimensions in a declared virtual material coordinate system, then map through crop, scan, and output resampling. Test the same material profile across formats and resolutions. Do not confuse larger output resolution with a physically larger negative.

**Test-first fixture.** One stock rendered as Super 8, Super 16, Super 35, and fifteen-perforation large format at two delivery sizes.

**Acceptance oracle.** The apparent grain scale follows the declared gate and sampling model rather than arbitrary preset-specific pixel counts.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use a fixed two-pixel grain radius for every virtual format and output resolution.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Format-aware grain mapping and resolution consistency tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.
