<a id="tc-p083-05"></a>
#### TC-P083-05. Halation and bloom conflation

**Baseline fixture.** One stock rendered as Super 8, Super 16, Super 35, and fifteen-perforation large format at two delivery sizes.

**Adversarial operation.** Enable only one of the material-halation or optical-diffusion stages, then enable both.

**Required response.** Produce separately controlled, attributable responses rather than identical duplicated glow.

**Baseline oracle.** The apparent grain scale follows the declared gate and sampling model rather than arbitrary preset-specific pixel counts.

**False-pass control.** A red edge outline on all pale objects must not qualify as emulsion halation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with moderate pale surfaces, clipped lights, and saturated emitters.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p083-06"></a>
#### TC-P083-06. Damage in clean defaults

**Baseline fixture.** One stock rendered as Super 8, Super 16, Super 35, and fifteen-perforation large format at two delivery sizes.

**Adversarial operation.** Load a clean large-format or 35mm recipe with no aging controls selected.

**Required response.** Produce no unrequested scratches, burns, flicker, or gate weave.

**Baseline oracle.** The apparent grain scale follows the declared gate and sampling model rather than arbitrary preset-specific pixel counts.

**False-pass control.** Using damage to make every film preset visibly obvious must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat after preset switching, saved recipe reopening, and reset-to-default.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p083-07"></a>
#### TC-P083-07. Noise mistaken for grain

**Baseline fixture.** One stock rendered as Super 8, Super 16, Super 35, and fifteen-perforation large format at two delivery sizes.

**Adversarial operation.** Render a noisy source with sensor-noise reduction and material grain controlled independently.

**Required response.** Keep both stages separately inspectable and avoid reporting sensor noise as a calibrated film texture.

**Baseline oracle.** The apparent grain scale follows the declared gate and sampling model rather than arbitrary preset-specific pixel counts.

**False-pass control.** Adding grain to conceal excessive denoising must not pass detail preservation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat low-light skin, smooth walls, and moving fine textures.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p083-08"></a>
#### TC-P083-08. Combined finishing instability

**Baseline fixture.** One stock rendered as Super 8, Super 16, Super 35, and fifteen-perforation large format at two delivery sizes.

**Adversarial operation.** Run moving high-contrast scenes through the full negative, texture, halation, print, and display chain.

**Required response.** Remain temporally coherent and allow ablation to identify any stage causing artifacts.

**Baseline oracle.** The apparent grain scale follows the declared gate and sampling model rather than arbitrary preset-specific pixel counts.

**False-pass control.** Passing isolated still tests cannot excuse shimmer or hue pumping in the complete clip.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exposure changes, bright object motion, and chunk boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p084"></a>
### P084. Implement emulsion halation separately from bloom

**Entry gate:** P083. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Create a controlled material scattering model instead of outlining all bright objects in red.

**Implementation method.** Operate from the appropriate pre-display signal, use bounded multi-scale kernels, and preserve energy accounting under the chosen approximation. Separate stock-related color weighting from lens or filter bloom. Include broad highlights, edges, and isolated emitters in validation.

**Test-first fixture.** A bright white window, a narrow colored point light, and an ordinary pale surface at moderate exposure.

**Acceptance oracle.** Halation follows the declared intensity and spatial model without creating identical red borders on every pale object.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply a red edge detector to the final display image and call it halation.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Halation model, kernel tests, and controlled-light benchmark. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p084-01"></a>
#### TC-P084-01. Render-order dependence

**Baseline fixture.** A bright white window, a narrow colored point light, and an ordinary pale surface at moderate exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Render the same material effect with different tile ordering, thread scheduling, and restart boundaries.

**Required response.** Preserve the declared deterministic result using stable global coordinates and frame identities.

**Baseline oracle.** Halation follows the declared intensity and spatial model without creating identical red borders on every pale object.

**False-pass control.** Wall-clock or tile-local random seeding must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with a fixed take seed and several independent output resolutions.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p084-02"></a>
#### TC-P084-02. Exposure-independent texture

**Baseline fixture.** A bright white window, a narrow colored point light, and an ordinary pale surface at moderate exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Apply the candidate effect across a controlled exposure wedge with identical scene structure.

**Required response.** Match the profile’s declared exposure-dependent statistics rather than an arbitrary constant overlay.

**Baseline oracle.** Halation follows the declared intensity and spatial model without creating identical red borders on every pale object.

**False-pass control.** An effect that ignores its specified density or exposure dependence must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat for neutral, colored, dark, and highlight patches.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p084-03"></a>
#### TC-P084-03. Virtual-format scaling error

**Baseline fixture.** A bright white window, a narrow colored point light, and an ordinary pale surface at moderate exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Change virtual gate and output resolution while keeping the same material profile.

**Required response.** Maintain the intended material scale through crop and resampling with no arbitrary pixel-radius substitution.

**Baseline oracle.** Halation follows the declared intensity and spatial model without creating identical red borders on every pale object.

**False-pass control.** Fixed pixel-sized grain across all virtual formats must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat small-format and large-format recipes at preview and final delivery sizes.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p084-04"></a>
#### TC-P084-04. Kernel energy and boundary error

**Baseline fixture.** A bright white window, a narrow colored point light, and an ordinary pale surface at moderate exposure.

**Adversarial operation.** Place bright emitters near borders and compare the effect at several support radii.

**Required response.** Follow the documented energy and border policy without unexplained brightness growth or tile seams.

**Baseline oracle.** Halation follows the declared intensity and spatial model without creating identical red borders on every pale object.

**False-pass control.** An unnormalized kernel whose energy grows with radius must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat isolated points, broad sources, corners, and partially off-frame emitters.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.

<a id="p085"></a>
### P085. Implement optical bloom and diffusion

**Entry gate:** P084. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Treat lens or filter scatter as a distinct, optional image-formation component.

**Implementation method.** Use normalized kernels or an explicitly documented flare model in the relevant exposure domain. Control veiling glare, local spread, and highlight behavior independently from emulsion effects. Validate the interaction with clipping and virtual bokeh.

**Test-first fixture.** A point light near a dark face, a broad soft source, and a highlight already clipped in the source.

**Acceptance oracle.** The effect remains finite and cannot claim to restore the clipped source; broad sources do not receive implausible identical halos.

**Deliberate mutation.** Blur a thresholded eight-bit image and add it without any energy or clipping policy.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Optical diffusion module and energy-response tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p086"></a>
### P086. Model print and scan finishing

**Entry gate:** P085. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Make negative rendering, print response, and scan characteristics independently editable.

**Implementation method.** Define density-to-transmission conversion, virtual printing exposure, print response, and scanning or display interpretation. Label unmeasured stages as reconstructed. Avoid double inversion or double display transfer, and keep a bypass for inspecting the negative-stage output.

**Test-first fixture.** A neutral density wedge processed through negative-only, print, and final delivery branches.

**Acceptance oracle.** Each branch has a declared domain and the final neutral ordering remains correct without hidden duplicate transforms.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply a negative inversion twice because both the stock and print nodes assume encoded input.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Print-scan graph and domain-boundary tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p087"></a>
### P087. Add aging and mechanical imperfections as optional layers

**Entry gate:** P086. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Support expressive damaged-film looks without making damage synonymous with cinematic quality.

**Implementation method.** Keep dust, scratches, gate weave, flicker, burns, and frame instability in a separately named effects group. Give each deterministic timing and geometry controls. Defaults for clean 35mm and large-format looks should not add arbitrary damage.

**Test-first fixture.** A clean large-format preset and an explicitly aged Super 8 preset rendered from the same source.

**Acceptance oracle.** The clean preset contains no unrequested scratches or gate jitter, and the aged effects are reproducible and independently removable.

**Deliberate mutation.** Enable strong scratches in every preset to make the film simulation more obvious.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Optional aging module and clean-default tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Baseline oracle.** The clean preset contains no unrequested scratches or gate jitter, and the aged effects are reproducible and independently removable.

**False-pass control.** Passing isolated still tests cannot excuse shimmer or hue pumping in the complete clip.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exposure changes, bright object motion, and chunk boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p088"></a>
### P088. Validate the combined material pipeline

**Entry gate:** P087. **Primary seam:** grain generator, spatial kernels, density texture, print and scan model.

**Research objective.** Evaluate interactions that isolated effect tests cannot reveal.

**Implementation method.** Render controlled exposure sequences with denoise, virtual optics, negative response, grain, halation, bloom, and print finishing. Measure seams, clipping, noise amplification, temporal shimmer, and color drift. Use ablations to identify which stage causes a failure.

**Test-first fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Acceptance oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**Deliberate mutation.** Approve the combined pipeline because every effect passed its own still-image test.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Combined film-material regression suite. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p088-01"></a>
#### TC-P088-01. Render-order dependence

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Render the same material effect with different tile ordering, thread scheduling, and restart boundaries.

**Required response.** Preserve the declared deterministic result using stable global coordinates and frame identities.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** Wall-clock or tile-local random seeding must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with a fixed take seed and several independent output resolutions.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p088-02"></a>
#### TC-P088-02. Exposure-independent texture

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Apply the candidate effect across a controlled exposure wedge with identical scene structure.

**Required response.** Match the profile’s declared exposure-dependent statistics rather than an arbitrary constant overlay.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** An effect that ignores its specified density or exposure dependence must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat for neutral, colored, dark, and highlight patches.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p088-03"></a>
#### TC-P088-03. Virtual-format scaling error

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Change virtual gate and output resolution while keeping the same material profile.

**Required response.** Maintain the intended material scale through crop and resampling with no arbitrary pixel-radius substitution.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** Fixed pixel-sized grain across all virtual formats must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat small-format and large-format recipes at preview and final delivery sizes.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p088-04"></a>
#### TC-P088-04. Kernel energy and boundary error

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Place bright emitters near borders and compare the effect at several support radii.

**Required response.** Follow the documented energy and border policy without unexplained brightness growth or tile seams.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** An unnormalized kernel whose energy grows with radius must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat isolated points, broad sources, corners, and partially off-frame emitters.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p088-05"></a>
#### TC-P088-05. Halation and bloom conflation

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Enable only one of the material-halation or optical-diffusion stages, then enable both.

**Required response.** Produce separately controlled, attributable responses rather than identical duplicated glow.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** A red edge outline on all pale objects must not qualify as emulsion halation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with moderate pale surfaces, clipped lights, and saturated emitters.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p088-06"></a>
#### TC-P088-06. Damage in clean defaults

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Load a clean large-format or 35mm recipe with no aging controls selected.

**Required response.** Produce no unrequested scratches, burns, flicker, or gate weave.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** Using damage to make every film preset visibly obvious must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat after preset switching, saved recipe reopening, and reset-to-default.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p088-07"></a>
#### TC-P088-07. Noise mistaken for grain

**Baseline fixture.** A moving bright subject crossing a dark textured background while grain and halation are enabled.

**Adversarial operation.** Render a noisy source with sensor-noise reduction and material grain controlled independently.

**Required response.** Keep both stages separately inspectable and avoid reporting sensor noise as a calibrated film texture.

**Baseline oracle.** The complete sequence remains temporally stable and each effect can be disabled to isolate artifacts.

**False-pass control.** Adding grain to conceal excessive denoising must not pass detail preservation.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat low-light skin, smooth walls, and moving fine textures.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p088-08"></a>
#### TC-P088-08. Combined finishing instability

**Adversarial operation.** Run moving high-contrast scenes through the full negative, texture, halation, print, and display chain.

**False-pass control.** Passing isolated still tests cannot excuse shimmer or hue pumping in the complete clip.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with exposure changes, bright object motion, and chunk boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="workstream-12"></a>
## Workstream 12. Virtual formats, lens geometry, and optical parameterization

A virtual format is a coordinate and optical model, not a sensor upgrade. Keep acquisition gate, crop, output aspect ratio, focal length, aperture geometry, focus, and material scale distinct. Match the field of view actually recorded before interpreting a virtual focal length. Thin-lens mathematics provides a reference, while real-lens characteristics require additional measured or explicitly creative models. The interface must not turn relative model depth into invented metres.

**Integration seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles. **Accountable specialty:** virtual optics and geometry engineer.

**Measurement domain:** dimensional correctness, field-of-view consistency, blur shape, and parameter honesty. **Evidence family:** known-distance scenes, perfect-depth renders, point-spread measurements, and gate metadata.

**Primary background:** [^C02][^F04][^D01] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p089"></a>
### P089. Specify all six requested virtual formats

**Entry gate:** P003, P049, P056. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Represent Super 8, Super 16, standard 35mm, Super 35, five-perforation 65mm, and fifteen-perforation large-format acquisition coherently.

**Implementation method.** Use sourced gate definitions when available and explicitly provisional geometry otherwise. Store perforation orientation, image area, crop, and delivery framing separately. A seventy-millimetre exhibition label must not be substituted for an unsourced acquisition gate.

**Test-first fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Acceptance oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**Deliberate mutation.** Assign a different color LUT to each format and omit gate geometry entirely.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Virtual-format registry and geometry validation. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p089-01"></a>
#### TC-P089-01. Unit and parameter substitution

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Substitute metres for millimetres, diameter for radius, or transmission stop for aperture f-number without conversion.

**Required response.** Reject or detect the mismatch through dimensional and independent optical tests.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** A plausible-looking blur cannot justify inconsistent physical units.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across focal length, focus distance, gate width, and output pixel conversion.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p089-02"></a>
#### TC-P089-02. Relative depth presented as metric

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Supply an uncalibrated relative depth field to an operation requiring physical distance.

**Required response.** Require validated scale information or switch to an explicitly relative creative control.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** A raw model value must not be displayed as metres.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat after scene cuts and changes in model normalization.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p089-03"></a>
#### TC-P089-03. Focus-plane and infinity limits

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Place objects on the focus plane, nearer, farther, and at the mathematical infinity limit.

**Required response.** Return zero defocus at focus, correct signed ordering, and finite limiting behavior.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** Division by zero or sign loss near focus must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across valid apertures, focal lengths, and virtual gates.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p089-04"></a>
#### TC-P089-04. Field-of-view incompatibility

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Select a virtual lens whose coverage conflicts with the recorded source and intended framing.

**Required response.** Show the required crop or unsupported coverage without inventing unseen image content.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** Changing a focal-length label alone must not imply a new camera viewpoint.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with stabilization crops, portrait output, and different physical phone lenses.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p089-05"></a>
#### TC-P089-05. Aperture normalization

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Change bokeh radius and blade count for an isolated point source at fixed exposure.

**Required response.** Maintain the declared energy normalization and shape behavior rather than arbitrary intensity shifts.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** A larger blur kernel must not gain brightness simply because it contains more samples.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat circular, polygonal, and optional asymmetric profiles.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p089-06"></a>
#### TC-P089-06. Foreground ordering stress

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Place a blurred foreground object in front of an in-focus subject and a bright far background.

**Required response.** Respect depth ordering and coverage under the selected rendering model.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** A background gather blur that leaks through opaque foreground boundaries must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat near image edges and with partial pixel coverage.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p089-07"></a>
#### TC-P089-07. Lens-character provenance

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Load a creative lens profile beside a measured profile with similar display names.

**Required response.** Preserve distinct evidence labels and parameter identities without implying equal physical calibration.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** Plausible aberration values must not be called measured without references.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat vignetting, cat-eye bokeh, breathing, and chromatic effects.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p089-08"></a>
#### TC-P089-08. Format and stock independence

**Baseline fixture.** Two large-format recipes sharing a stock but using five-perforation vertical and fifteen-perforation horizontal acquisition models.

**Adversarial operation.** Change acquisition gate while holding stock fixed, then change stock while holding gate fixed.

**Required response.** Modify only the intended geometry or material components and retain explicit interactions.

**Baseline oracle.** The format records differ in geometry while the shared stock identity remains unchanged.

**False-pass control.** A format selector implemented solely as a color LUT must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat standard 35mm versus Super 35 and five- versus fifteen-perforation large format.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p090"></a>
### P090. Map captured field of view to virtual lenses

**Entry gate:** P089. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Prevent a selected cinema focal length from implying a different viewpoint or unseen image coverage.

**Implementation method.** Use calibrated or explicitly estimated source intrinsics, crop, stabilization transform, and output framing. Derive the compatible virtual focal length from gate and field of view. Clearly mark incompatible lens selections that would require cropping or unavailable wider coverage.

**Test-first fixture.** A wide phone capture paired with a long virtual focal-length selection that would require substantial cropping.

**Acceptance oracle.** The interface shows the crop or rejects unsupported coverage instead of inventing wider scene content.

**Deliberate mutation.** Change only the displayed focal length while leaving geometry unexplained.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Field-of-view mapping and framing guidance. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p091"></a>
### P091. Implement signed thin-lens defocus

**Entry gate:** P090. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Create an independently testable geometric reference for blur magnitude and foreground-background ordering.

**Implementation method.** Use consistent length units and explicit f-number. Compute signed circle-of-confusion diameter from focal length, object distance, focus distance, and aperture. Convert to output pixels through the virtual gate. Handle infinity and reject impossible geometry.

**Test-first fixture.** Objects in front of, on, and behind a focus plane, including an infinitely distant background.

**Acceptance oracle.** Focus-plane blur is zero, signs distinguish near and far, and stopping down scales diameter as expected.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use a T-stop directly as an f-number without accounting for transmission semantics.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Thin-lens reference code and dimensional tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p092"></a>
### P092. Separate metric and relative focus controls

**Entry gate:** P091. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Avoid displaying absolute distances unsupported by the depth estimator.

**Implementation method.** Type depth outputs as metric, inverse metric, relative depth, or relative inverse depth. Require a validated scale calibration before metric optics. Offer relative focus and artist-controlled blur for uncalibrated scenes, with clear labels and bounded defaults.

**Test-first fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Acceptance oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**Deliberate mutation.** Label every model depth value as a physical distance.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Depth-unit contract and honest focus UI. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across focal length, focus distance, gate width, and output pixel conversion.

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Supply an uncalibrated relative depth field to an operation requiring physical distance.

**Required response.** Require validated scale information or switch to an explicitly relative creative control.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** A raw model value must not be displayed as metres.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat after scene cuts and changes in model normalization.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p092-03"></a>
#### TC-P092-03. Focus-plane and infinity limits

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Place objects on the focus plane, nearer, farther, and at the mathematical infinity limit.

**Required response.** Return zero defocus at focus, correct signed ordering, and finite limiting behavior.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** Division by zero or sign loss near focus must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across valid apertures, focal lengths, and virtual gates.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p092-04"></a>
#### TC-P092-04. Field-of-view incompatibility

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Select a virtual lens whose coverage conflicts with the recorded source and intended framing.

**Required response.** Show the required crop or unsupported coverage without inventing unseen image content.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** Changing a focal-length label alone must not imply a new camera viewpoint.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with stabilization crops, portrait output, and different physical phone lenses.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p092-05"></a>
#### TC-P092-05. Aperture normalization

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Change bokeh radius and blade count for an isolated point source at fixed exposure.

**Required response.** Maintain the declared energy normalization and shape behavior rather than arbitrary intensity shifts.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** A larger blur kernel must not gain brightness simply because it contains more samples.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat circular, polygonal, and optional asymmetric profiles.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p092-06"></a>
#### TC-P092-06. Foreground ordering stress

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Place a blurred foreground object in front of an in-focus subject and a bright far background.

**Required response.** Respect depth ordering and coverage under the selected rendering model.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** A background gather blur that leaks through opaque foreground boundaries must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat near image edges and with partial pixel coverage.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p092-07"></a>
#### TC-P092-07. Lens-character provenance

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Load a creative lens profile beside a measured profile with similar display names.

**Required response.** Preserve distinct evidence labels and parameter identities without implying equal physical calibration.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** Plausible aberration values must not be called measured without references.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat vignetting, cat-eye bokeh, breathing, and chromatic effects.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p092-08"></a>
#### TC-P092-08. Format and stock independence

**Baseline fixture.** A monocular model output whose numeric scale changes after a scene cut.

**Adversarial operation.** Change acquisition gate while holding stock fixed, then change stock while holding gate fixed.

**Required response.** Modify only the intended geometry or material components and retain explicit interactions.

**Baseline oracle.** The app does not interpret the raw value as metres and resets or realigns relative focus appropriately.

**False-pass control.** A format selector implemented solely as a color LUT must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat standard 35mm versus Super 35 and five- versus fifteen-perforation large format.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p093"></a>
### P093. Implement aperture and bokeh shape models

**Entry gate:** P092. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Create controlled blur kernels with explicit shape and normalization.

**Implementation method.** Start with a circular reference, then add polygonal blades and optional measured or creative asymmetry. Define kernel support, energy normalization, sampling quality, and behavior near image boundaries. Keep a parameter reset that returns exactly to the reference.

**Test-first fixture.** A grid of bright points at different depths and positions across the frame.

**Acceptance oracle.** Bokeh shape and energy follow the selected model without random brightness changes when aperture shape changes.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use an unnormalized polygon mask whose brightness grows with blur radius.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Aperture kernel library and point-light tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Required response.** Reject or detect the mismatch through dimensional and independent optical tests.

**Baseline oracle.** Bokeh shape and energy follow the selected model without random brightness changes when aperture shape changes.

**False-pass control.** A plausible-looking blur cannot justify inconsistent physical units.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat across focal length, focus distance, gate width, and output pixel conversion.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.

### P094. Add field-dependent lens characteristics

**Entry gate:** P093. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Model cat-eye bokeh, vignetting, aberration, and breathing only with explicit provenance and limits.

**Implementation method.** Separate geometric defocus from field-dependent appearance. Parameterize position, wavelength or channel approximation, focus changes, and exposure effects. Distinguish measured lens profiles from creative profiles. Test edge cases near the frame boundary and extreme focus values.

**Test-first fixture.** Off-axis highlights during a gradual focus pull with vignetting and longitudinal color effects enabled.

**Acceptance oracle.** The effects change continuously and remain within their declared model rather than jumping between arbitrary presets.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply fixed chromatic offsets independent of depth and call them a calibrated lens.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Lens-character profile schema and continuity tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

### P095. Implement optional anamorphic interpretation

**Entry gate:** P094. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Treat anamorphic squeeze, framing, flare, and bokeh as distinct controls rather than one stretch filter.

**Implementation method.** Declare whether the source used a physical adapter or a virtual interpretation. Preserve source aspect ratio and avoid double desqueeze. Parameterize oval bokeh and optional flare independently, and label unsupported optical reconstruction honestly.

**Test-first fixture.** A clip recorded through a physical anamorphic adapter and an ordinary spherical phone clip.

**Acceptance oracle.** Each receives the correct geometry path and the ordinary clip is labelled simulated rather than physically anamorphic capture.

**Deliberate mutation.** Desqueeze every clip whenever an anamorphic preset is selected.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Anamorphic mode contract and geometry regression tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p096"></a>
### P096. Validate virtual optics against controlled geometry

**Entry gate:** P095. **Primary seam:** virtual gate model, field-of-view mapping, circle of confusion, lens profiles.

**Research objective.** Establish that the model behaves coherently before comparing it with famous films.

**Implementation method.** Use known-distance objects, sharp source capture, controlled point lights, and repeatable focus positions. Compare physical measurements where available and model predictions otherwise. Keep approximation error distinct from depth-estimation error through synthetic perfect-depth tests.

**Test-first fixture.** A controlled three-plane scene rendered once with known depths and once with estimated depths.

**Acceptance oracle.** The report separates lens-rendering defects from depth-estimation failures and does not blame one for the other.

**Deliberate mutation.** Evaluate only the complete ML pipeline with no perfect-depth reference.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Optical validation laboratory and error decomposition. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat vignetting, cat-eye bokeh, breathing, and chromatic effects.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p096-08"></a>
#### TC-P096-08. Format and stock independence

**Baseline fixture.** A controlled three-plane scene rendered once with known depths and once with estimated depths.

**Adversarial operation.** Change acquisition gate while holding stock fixed, then change stock while holding gate fixed.

**Required response.** Modify only the intended geometry or material components and retain explicit interactions.

**Baseline oracle.** The report separates lens-rendering defects from depth-estimation failures and does not blame one for the other.

**False-pass control.** A format selector implemented solely as a color LUT must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat standard 35mm versus Super 35 and five- versus fifteen-perforation large format.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="workstream-13"></a>
## Workstream 13. Offline depth estimation and model engineering

Machine learning supplies scene information to a deterministic renderer; it does not replace the recorded scene with generated video. Choose model weights, export tools, delegates, and licences deliberately. A model listed for a device remains a candidate until its integrated accuracy, memory, latency, and thermal behavior are measured. Relative depth is often sufficient for an honest creative focus control, but absolute optical claims require more evidence.

**Integration seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference. **Accountable specialty:** on-device machine-learning engineer.

**Measurement domain:** depth semantics, conversion fidelity, boundary accuracy, and integrated resource use. **Evidence family:** model hashes, licences, preprocessing tensors, aligned depth maps, and sustained device measurements.

**Primary background:** [^D01][^D02][^D03][^D04] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p097"></a>
### P097. Define the depth-provider interface

**Entry gate:** P007, P065. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Make depth semantics, confidence, geometry, and latency explicit at the model boundary.

**Implementation method.** Return model identity, units, coordinate transform, valid region, confidence policy, source timestamp, and processing status with each depth field. Support unavailable or stale results. Keep inference independent of camera ownership and prohibit a depth result from modifying source evidence.

**Test-first fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Acceptance oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**Deliberate mutation.** Return only a float array with no source identity or coordinate metadata.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Depth provider contract and stale-result tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p097-01"></a>
#### TC-P097-01. Model identity substitution

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Replace a model asset with another variant or converted file while retaining a cached result.

**Required response.** Invalidate incompatible caches and report the actual model identity before accepting depth output.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** A filename match alone must not establish identical weights.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with precision changes, runtime versions, and different model variants.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p097-02"></a>
#### TC-P097-02. Preprocessing geometry error

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Use a non-square source with known corner markers and alter resizing, padding, or channel order.

**Required response.** Match the specified tensor preparation and restore output coordinates correctly.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** Unrecorded stretching or swapped color channels must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat portrait, landscape, cropped, and rotated source frames.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p097-03"></a>
#### TC-P097-03. Conversion accuracy regression

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Compare exported or quantized model results against the approved host baseline on withheld scenes.

**Required response.** Meet declared depth and boundary tolerances or remain experimental despite successful loading.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** A model that merely runs is not numerically qualified.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat hair, glass, low light, thin objects, and saturated illumination.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p097-04"></a>
#### TC-P097-04. Offline asset unavailability

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Disable networking and remove or corrupt a required local model asset.

**Required response.** Report the missing capability while preserving ordinary capture and source retention.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** An offline camera must not hang waiting for an undisclosed cloud dependency.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat first installation, asset update, and a previously working offline session.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p097-05"></a>
#### TC-P097-05. Delegate failure and fallback

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Fail runtime or delegate initialization while a preview or development job is active.

**Required response.** Use only an explicitly qualified fallback or disable optional depth processing with a clear reason.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** Silently changing to an untested backend or uploading frames must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat CPU, GPU, and available accelerator configurations as applicable.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p097-06"></a>
#### TC-P097-06. Stale depth result

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Delay inference until its result no longer matches the current source timestamp or crop.

**Required response.** Reject or explicitly reproject the result under a validated policy rather than applying it blindly.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** A float array without temporal and geometric identity must not be accepted.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat rapid camera movement, rotation, source switches, and scene cuts.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p097-07"></a>
#### TC-P097-07. Confidence misrepresentation

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Provide unstable or unreliable predictions while their confidence metadata claims certainty.

**Required response.** Expose uncalibrated confidence and reduce rendering reliance according to the declared policy.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** An arbitrary confidence score must not be presented as a calibrated probability.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat transparent surfaces, low texture, mirrors, and unfamiliar scenes.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p097-08"></a>
#### TC-P097-08. Integrated load and thermal drift

**Baseline fixture.** A depth map computed for an earlier cropped frame arriving after the current preview has changed orientation.

**Adversarial operation.** Run inference alongside actual capture, rendering, and encoding for a sustained interval.

**Required response.** Measure complete workload behavior and choose live or deferred operation from evidence.

**Baseline oracle.** The consumer detects the mismatched timestamp and geometry instead of applying the map to the wrong image.

**False-pass control.** Standalone model latency must not become a full-camera frame-rate guarantee.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat cold start, warm operation, memory pressure, and severe thermal conditions.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p098"></a>
### P098. Select a licensable baseline model

**Entry gate:** P097. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Choose the smallest credible model that can establish the pipeline without blocking future commercial use.

**Implementation method.** Review the exact weight licence, code licence, export dependencies, and redistribution conditions. Record model hashes and training-domain limitations. Evaluate a small baseline against owned test clips before adding larger alternatives.

**Test-first fixture.** Two similarly named model variants with different licences and substantially different memory requirements.

**Acceptance oracle.** The package includes only approved weights and reports the selected variant exactly.

**Deliberate mutation.** Assume all variants inherit the most permissive licence in the repository.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Model selection record and licence manifest. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p099"></a>
### P099. Verify image preprocessing

**Entry gate:** P098. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Prevent silent accuracy loss from wrong normalization, resizing, channel order, or crop mapping.

**Implementation method.** Match the chosen model specification exactly and preserve the transform from source pixels to model coordinates. Use known color and geometry fixtures, compare host and device preprocessing, and invert padding or crop transforms during output alignment.

**Test-first fixture.** A non-square frame with colored corner markers and a bright thin object near the padded boundary.

**Acceptance oracle.** Host and device tensors agree and the returned depth aligns with the original object position.

**Deliberate mutation.** Stretch every input to a square without recording the geometry transform.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Preprocessing reference and host-device tensor comparisons. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p100"></a>
### P100. Export and validate model numerics

**Entry gate:** P099. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Treat model conversion as a potential behavioral change, not merely a packaging step.

**Implementation method.** Compare original and exported outputs on a fixed representative corpus. Record operator substitutions, precision changes, unsupported operations, and backend versions. Quantization requires its own calibration and held-out assessment, especially near difficult boundaries.

**Test-first fixture.** Original and quantized model outputs on glass, hair, low light, and thin foreground objects.

**Acceptance oracle.** The converted model meets declared depth and boundary tolerances or remains an experimental option.

**Deliberate mutation.** Accept conversion because the exported file loads successfully.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Model conversion report and numerical regression suite. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Research objective.** Run the approved model locally with bounded ownership and an explicit fallback policy.

**Test-first fixture.** Airplane mode, a missing model asset, and a delegate initialization failure during preview.

**Required deliverable.** Offline inference integration and no-network tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Required response.** Meet declared depth and boundary tolerances or remain experimental despite successful loading.

**Baseline oracle.** The UI reports the issue, avoids network-dependent generation, and preserves ordinary recording.

**False-pass control.** A model that merely runs is not numerically qualified.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat hair, glass, low light, thin objects, and saturated illumination.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p101-04"></a>
#### TC-P101-04. Offline asset unavailability

**Baseline fixture.** Airplane mode, a missing model asset, and a delegate initialization failure during preview.

**Adversarial operation.** Disable networking and remove or corrupt a required local model asset.

**Required response.** Report the missing capability while preserving ordinary capture and source retention.

**Baseline oracle.** The UI reports the issue, avoids network-dependent generation, and preserves ordinary recording.

**False-pass control.** An offline camera must not hang waiting for an undisclosed cloud dependency.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat first installation, asset update, and a previously working offline session.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p101-05"></a>
#### TC-P101-05. Delegate failure and fallback

**Baseline fixture.** Airplane mode, a missing model asset, and a delegate initialization failure during preview.

**Adversarial operation.** Fail runtime or delegate initialization while a preview or development job is active.

**Required response.** Use only an explicitly qualified fallback or disable optional depth processing with a clear reason.

**Baseline oracle.** The UI reports the issue, avoids network-dependent generation, and preserves ordinary recording.

**False-pass control.** Silently changing to an untested backend or uploading frames must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat CPU, GPU, and available accelerator configurations as applicable.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p101-06"></a>
#### TC-P101-06. Stale depth result

**Baseline fixture.** Airplane mode, a missing model asset, and a delegate initialization failure during preview.

**Adversarial operation.** Delay inference until its result no longer matches the current source timestamp or crop.

**Required response.** Reject or explicitly reproject the result under a validated policy rather than applying it blindly.

**Baseline oracle.** The UI reports the issue, avoids network-dependent generation, and preserves ordinary recording.

**False-pass control.** A float array without temporal and geometric identity must not be accepted.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat rapid camera movement, rotation, source switches, and scene cuts.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p101-07"></a>
#### TC-P101-07. Confidence misrepresentation

**Baseline fixture.** Airplane mode, a missing model asset, and a delegate initialization failure during preview.

**Adversarial operation.** Provide unstable or unreliable predictions while their confidence metadata claims certainty.

**Required response.** Expose uncalibrated confidence and reduce rendering reliance according to the declared policy.

**Baseline oracle.** The UI reports the issue, avoids network-dependent generation, and preserves ordinary recording.

**False-pass control.** An arbitrary confidence score must not be presented as a calibrated probability.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat transparent surfaces, low texture, mirrors, and unfamiliar scenes.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p101-08"></a>

**Baseline fixture.** Airplane mode, a missing model asset, and a delegate initialization failure during preview.

**Adversarial operation.** Run inference alongside actual capture, rendering, and encoding for a sustained interval.

**Required response.** Measure complete workload behavior and choose live or deferred operation from evidence.

**Baseline oracle.** The UI reports the issue, avoids network-dependent generation, and preserves ordinary recording.

**False-pass control.** Standalone model latency must not become a full-camera frame-rate guarantee.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat cold start, warm operation, memory pressure, and severe thermal conditions.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p102"></a>
### P102. Construct a difficult-scene depth corpus

**Entry gate:** P101. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Evaluate the scenes that determine whether synthetic cinema blur is usable.

**Implementation method.** Include hair, fur, glasses, mirrors, water, smoke, fences, thin wires, low texture, motion blur, low light, and crossing subjects. Obtain consent and rights for all footage. Use synthetic geometry where ground truth is available and honest qualitative labels elsewhere.

**Test-first fixture.** A scene with a person behind a fence and a reflection that appears at a different apparent depth.

**Acceptance oracle.** The evaluation records specific boundary and ordering failures rather than averaging them away in one global score.

**Deliberate mutation.** Benchmark only isolated portraits against simple backgrounds.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Difficult-scene corpus and per-category evaluation protocol. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p102-01"></a>
#### TC-P102-01. Model identity substitution

**Baseline fixture.** A scene with a person behind a fence and a reflection that appears at a different apparent depth.

**Adversarial operation.** Replace a model asset with another variant or converted file while retaining a cached result.

**Required response.** Invalidate incompatible caches and report the actual model identity before accepting depth output.

**Baseline oracle.** The evaluation records specific boundary and ordering failures rather than averaging them away in one global score.

**False-pass control.** A filename match alone must not establish identical weights.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with precision changes, runtime versions, and different model variants.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.

**Adversarial operation.** Use a non-square source with known corner markers and alter resizing, padding, or channel order.

**Required response.** Match the specified tensor preparation and restore output coordinates correctly.

**Baseline oracle.** The evaluation records specific boundary and ordering failures rather than averaging them away in one global score.

**False-pass control.** Unrecorded stretching or swapped color channels must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat portrait, landscape, cropped, and rotated source frames.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.

<a id="p103"></a>
### P103. Estimate confidence and uncertainty

**Entry gate:** P102. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Prevent uncertain depth from producing unnecessarily aggressive visual artifacts.

**Implementation method.** Use available model confidence or explicitly defined proxy measures, consistency checks, and boundary uncertainty. Calibrate thresholds against held-out footage. Confidence controls rendering strength and fallback; it must not be presented as a probability without calibration.

**Test-first fixture.** A low-texture wall and a transparent glass edge where repeated estimates vary significantly.

**Acceptance oracle.** The renderer receives low-confidence regions and can reduce blur instead of forcing an unstable segmentation boundary.

**Deliberate mutation.** Treat every depth pixel as equally reliable.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Confidence policy and uncertainty-aware rendering tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p104"></a>
### P104. Qualify integrated depth performance on the S23

**Entry gate:** P103. **Primary seam:** depth provider interface, model packaging, preprocessing, on-device inference.

**Research objective.** Decide what can run live and what belongs in deferred development.

**Implementation method.** Measure latency, memory, energy, thermal state, and boundary quality while capture and preview are active. Test sustained operation, not just a single inference. Record input resolution and inference cadence separately from output video resolution.

**Test-first fixture.** A model that runs quickly when isolated but reduces recording stability during a sustained take.

**Acceptance oracle.** The scheduler chooses a lower-cost preview or deferred-only policy rather than hiding dropped source frames.

**Deliberate mutation.** Advertise model inference rate as full-resolution rendered recording rate.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Physical inference qualification and live-versus-deferred decision. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.
