<a id="p124"></a>
### P124. Checkpoint temporal rendering safely

**Entry gate:** P123. **Primary seam:** media library, import inspection, render jobs, checkpoints, export.

**Research objective.** Resume expensive work without changing the visual result at the restart boundary.

**Implementation method.** Checkpoint verified chunks and relevant temporal state with source, graph, model, profile, and algorithm hashes. Validate complete files before resuming. Recompute overlap where required and ensure final assembly contains each output frame exactly once.

**Test-first fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Acceptance oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**Deliberate mutation.** Validate a checkpoint only by its output filename and frame number.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Resume manifest and uninterrupted-equivalence tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p124-01"></a>
#### TC-P124-01. Ambiguous imported signal

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Import media with absent or contradictory color tags, rotation, or timing metadata.

**Required response.** Separate detected facts from user interpretation and avoid silent normalization to an assumed source type.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** Filename extension alone must not determine transfer or dynamic range.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat HDR-looking untagged clips, variable rates, and portrait rotation.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p124-02"></a>
#### TC-P124-02. Mutable recipe during export

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Change UI parameters after a render has begun but before it finishes.

**Required response.** Keep the running job bound to its frozen recipe and create a new version for subsequent edits.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** Reading live slider values for successive output frames must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat stock, focus, grain seed, output range, and source interpretation changes.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p124-03"></a>
#### TC-P124-03. Checkpoint identity mismatch

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Replace source, model, profile, or graph while retaining a previously completed chunk cache.

**Required response.** Reject incompatible resume data or start a distinct job with new identities.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** Filename and frame number alone must not validate a checkpoint.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat one changed identity field at a time and inspect specific rejection reasons.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p124-04"></a>
#### TC-P124-04. Cancellation at acceptance boundary

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Cancel during rendering, verification, publication, or final cleanup.

**Required response.** Acknowledge cancellation only after ownership is controlled and never publish a cancelled job as accepted.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** A late worker callback that reverses cancellation must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat with process restart and an already retained partial output.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p124-05"></a>
#### TC-P124-05. Temporary storage exhaustion

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Make remaining space insufficient for intermediate work or duplicate publication storage.

**Required response.** Pause or fail safely before source loss, preserving recoverable artifacts and clear cleanup choices.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** Budgeting only final output bytes must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat before rendering, during chunk assembly, and during gallery publication.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p124-06"></a>
#### TC-P124-06. Missing or revoked media access

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Revoke the source grant or remove a file while the library still has a cached thumbnail.

**Required response.** Show actual availability and preserve historical metadata without treating the thumbnail as accessible media.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** Thumbnail presence must not certify a valid source or output.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat local files, document-provider grants, and recovered private media.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p124-07"></a>
#### TC-P124-07. Resume boundary duplication

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Assemble chunks whose temporal overlap contains repeated or omitted output frames.

**Required response.** Emit the exact intended timeline once and maintain declared temporal continuity.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** A playable movie with duplicated overlap frames must fail cadence integrity.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat fractional rates, audio-bearing clips, and scene cuts at boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p124-08"></a>
#### TC-P124-08. Shared bundle privacy and interpretation

**Baseline fixture.** A stopped render resumed after the depth model file has been replaced with a different version.

**Adversarial operation.** Export a result with private paths or without necessary signal and recipe metadata.

**Required response.** Redact personal information while retaining the technical interpretation needed for correct use.

**Baseline oracle.** The old checkpoint is rejected or a new job is created; mixed-model output is never silently assembled.

**False-pass control.** A Log master without its required interpretation record must not be silently presented as universally self-describing.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat clean Log, rendered SDR, HDR-derived looks, and unverified partial exports.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p125"></a>
### P125. Budget disk and intermediate storage

**Entry gate:** P124. **Primary seam:** media library, import inspection, render jobs, checkpoints, export.

**Research objective.** Prevent high-quality development from filling storage and destroying recoverability.

**Implementation method.** Estimate source, proxy, temporary, finalization, and publication requirements separately. Use conservative reserves and measured growth, not a fixed generic percentage. Allow explicit cleanup of reproducible intermediates while protecting originals and sole retained outputs.

**Test-first fixture.** A long RAW source whose planned ten-bit export requires temporary duplication during publication.

**Acceptance oracle.** The job declines or pauses safely before exhausting reserved space and explains which data can be removed safely.

**Deliberate mutation.** Budget only the final output size and ignore temporary files.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Storage planner and low-space continuation policy. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p126"></a>
### P126. Build a trustworthy clip library

**Entry gate:** P125. **Primary seam:** media library, import inspection, render jobs, checkpoints, export.

**Research objective.** Keep source, result, metadata, thumbnail, and recovery identities paired.

**Implementation method.** Index exact media identities, recipe versions, verification status, duration, geometry, and availability. Thumbnails are derived previews, not proof of output validity. Handle revoked grants and missing files without corrupting the library or silently deleting historical records.

**Test-first fixture.** A thumbnail remains cached after the underlying media permission is revoked.

**Acceptance oracle.** The library shows unavailable media clearly and does not imply that the thumbnail represents accessible verified footage.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use thumbnail existence as the media availability check.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Clip library schema and missing-media tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p127"></a>
### P127. Export interoperable result bundles

**Entry gate:** P126. **Primary seam:** media library, import inspection, render jobs, checkpoints, export.

**Research objective.** Deliver video with the metadata needed to understand and reproduce it.

**Implementation method.** Include source lineage, recipe, profile and model identities, timing mapping, color interpretation, calibration status, clipping counts, and verification summary. Redact personal paths and identifiers in shared reports. Keep optional large intermediates separate from the default share bundle.

**Test-first fixture.** A LogC3 result shared without its sidecar and a rendered movie result containing private filesystem paths in metadata.

**Acceptance oracle.** The UI warns about required interpretation information and sanitizes the public report without losing technical provenance.

**Deliberate mutation.** Publish private absolute paths or omit essential Log interpretation metadata.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Export bundle schema and privacy-preserving share tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p128"></a>
### P128. Validate long-form development end to end

**Entry gate:** P127. **Primary seam:** media library, import inspection, render jobs, checkpoints, export.

**Research objective.** Prove that the deferred workflow survives realistic interruptions and large media.

**Implementation method.** Run complete import, recipe edit, render, cancel, resume, verify, publish, and re-open workflows. Use rotated, variable-rate, audio-bearing, high-resolution, and corrupt-edge fixtures. Record limitations separately for software and physical-device execution.

**Test-first fixture.** A multi-minute clip with audio, orientation metadata, temporal effects, and one process termination during rendering.

**Acceptance oracle.** The final accepted result has correct timing, orientation, audio, provenance, and no duplicated checkpoint boundary frames.

**Deliberate mutation.** Validate only short silent landscape clips.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** End-to-end deferred-development acceptance report. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p128-05"></a>
#### TC-P128-05. Temporary storage exhaustion

**Baseline fixture.** A multi-minute clip with audio, orientation metadata, temporal effects, and one process termination during rendering.

**Adversarial operation.** Make remaining space insufficient for intermediate work or duplicate publication storage.

**Required response.** Pause or fail safely before source loss, preserving recoverable artifacts and clear cleanup choices.

**Baseline oracle.** The final accepted result has correct timing, orientation, audio, provenance, and no duplicated checkpoint boundary frames.

**False-pass control.** Budgeting only final output bytes must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat before rendering, during chunk assembly, and during gallery publication.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p128-06"></a>
#### TC-P128-06. Missing or revoked media access

**Baseline fixture.** A multi-minute clip with audio, orientation metadata, temporal effects, and one process termination during rendering.

**Adversarial operation.** Revoke the source grant or remove a file while the library still has a cached thumbnail.

**Required response.** Show actual availability and preserve historical metadata without treating the thumbnail as accessible media.

**Baseline oracle.** The final accepted result has correct timing, orientation, audio, provenance, and no duplicated checkpoint boundary frames.

**False-pass control.** Thumbnail presence must not certify a valid source or output.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat local files, document-provider grants, and recovered private media.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p128-07"></a>
#### TC-P128-07. Resume boundary duplication

**Baseline fixture.** A multi-minute clip with audio, orientation metadata, temporal effects, and one process termination during rendering.

**Adversarial operation.** Assemble chunks whose temporal overlap contains repeated or omitted output frames.

**Required response.** Emit the exact intended timeline once and maintain declared temporal continuity.

**Baseline oracle.** The final accepted result has correct timing, orientation, audio, provenance, and no duplicated checkpoint boundary frames.

**False-pass control.** A playable movie with duplicated overlap frames must fail cadence integrity.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat fractional rates, audio-bearing clips, and scene cuts at boundaries.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p128-08"></a>
#### TC-P128-08. Shared bundle privacy and interpretation

**Baseline fixture.** A multi-minute clip with audio, orientation metadata, temporal effects, and one process termination during rendering.

**Adversarial operation.** Export a result with private paths or without necessary signal and recipe metadata.

**Required response.** Redact personal information while retaining the technical interpretation needed for correct use.

**Baseline oracle.** The final accepted result has correct timing, orientation, audio, provenance, and no duplicated checkpoint boundary frames.

**False-pass control.** A Log master without its required interpretation record must not be silently presented as universally self-describing.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat clean Log, rendered SDR, HDR-derived looks, and unverified partial exports.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="workstream-17"></a>
## Workstream 17. Professional camera interface and accessible interaction

The interface should make technically sophisticated controls understandable without hiding their consequences. Preserve the current native application and evolve it through tested components rather than replacing it for visual novelty. Capture controls need stable placement, readable status, and trustworthy applied values. A creative preset must never obscure source quality or recovery state. Accessibility, landscape operation, large text, and interrupted workflows are part of image-making reliability.

**Integration seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI. **Accountable specialty:** native interaction and accessibility engineer.

**Measurement domain:** task completion, semantic clarity, state visibility, and source-versus-look separation. **Evidence family:** interaction traces, accessibility trees, matched screen states, and real-phone task observations.

**Primary background:** [^A08][^A10][^R01] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p129"></a>
### P129. Define the camera screen information hierarchy

**Entry gate:** P017, P024, P121. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Keep recording, source mode, exposure, audio, and warnings visible without overcrowding the viewfinder.

**Implementation method.** Separate persistent capture controls from expandable advanced settings. Show requested versus applied values only where meaningful and label provisional information. Design portrait and landscape layouts around stable Record and Stop targets, not a scrolling toolbar.

**Test-first fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Acceptance oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**Deliberate mutation.** Place Stop inside a scrollable control list that moves during recording.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Camera screen specification and layout interaction tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p129-01"></a>
#### TC-P129-01. Landscape and large-text stress

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Open advanced controls with increased font scale in landscape during an active take.

**Required response.** Keep Record or Stop, essential warnings, and selected source status reachable and readable.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** Critical actions hidden inside scrolling content must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat small display settings, orientation changes, and simultaneous audio and storage warnings.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p129-02"></a>
#### TC-P129-02. Source-look label confusion

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Select a large-format film recipe while the underlying source remains a lower-resolution SDR or experimental RAW route.

**Required response.** Display the actual source and simulated look independently with their evidence status.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** Renaming a source mode after the virtual format must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat preset changes, saved recipe reopening, and export sharing.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p129-03"></a>
#### TC-P129-03. Invalid control draft

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Enter an incomplete or out-of-range numeric value and interrupt editing before Apply.

**Required response.** Preserve committed settings and keep the draft visibly unapplied or invalid.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** Partially typed input reaching the camera must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat shutter, ISO, focus distance, ROI coordinates, and output dimensions.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p129-04"></a>
#### TC-P129-04. Stale or wrong-domain scope

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Feed a monitoring aid delayed preview samples or a display-clipped image from an unclipped source.

**Required response.** Identify freshness and measurement domain instead of falsely reporting sensor conditions.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** An RGB8 preview histogram must not certify source bit depth or sensor clipping.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat waveform, false color, focus peaking, and color histogram.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p129-05"></a>
#### TC-P129-05. Nonvisual interaction

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Perform the core phase task using accessibility navigation and spoken state information.

**Required response.** Expose usable names, order, values, and cancellation without relying only on color or precision gestures.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** An unlabeled custom canvas as the only control must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat camera operation, ROI selection, focus editing, and recovery export.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p129-06"></a>
#### TC-P129-06. Premature success indication

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Finish frame submission while verification or publication still remains incomplete.

**Required response.** Show the actual remaining stage and withhold accepted completion until its gate passes.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** A one-hundred-percent banner before required verification must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat encoder drain, full decode, sidecar export, and gallery commit.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p129-07"></a>
#### TC-P129-07. Unfair comparison view

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Compare outputs at different times, scales, or display transforms without making those differences visible.

**Required response.** Align comparable content or clearly disclose the mismatch before presenting a preference judgment.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** Automatically enhancing one side of a comparison must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat source-versus-result, recipe revisions, and different output aspect ratios.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p129-08"></a>
#### TC-P129-08. Real shooting interruption

**Baseline fixture.** Landscape mode with large text, a storage warning, microphone meters, and the manual controls panel open.

**Adversarial operation.** Perform the task on the physical phone with a thermal warning, permission issue, or recovery event.

**Required response.** Let the user understand what was saved and complete the appropriate next action without hidden state.

**Baseline oracle.** Record and Stop remain reachable, warnings remain readable, and the viewfinder is not accidentally replaced by settings.

**False-pass control.** A desktop mockup cannot substitute for observed physical task completion.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat one-handed operation, outdoor visibility, and finding an interrupted take.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p130"></a>
### P130. Implement source and look selection separately

**Entry gate:** P129. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Prevent users from confusing capture capability with a virtual film format.

**Implementation method.** Use distinct selectors for physical source mode, virtual format, stock, lens interpretation, and finishing recipe. Show computational cost and calibration status where relevant. Changing a look must not silently alter recording resolution or source lineage.

**Test-first fixture.** Selecting an IMAX-style recipe while the active source is a qualified 1080p SDR mode.

**Acceptance oracle.** The interface preserves and displays the source mode while labelling the large-format appearance as simulated.

**Deliberate mutation.** Rename the active recording mode IMAX 70mm after a preset selection.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Separated control model and truthfulness UI tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p131"></a>
### P131. Design manual controls for deliberate operation

**Entry gate:** P130. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Offer precise adjustment without accidental changes during a take.

**Implementation method.** Provide bounded sliders, numeric entry, reset, and explicit apply behavior where needed. Keep units visible and disable unavailable controls with reasons. Distinguish draft values from committed effective targets and observed sensor results.

**Test-first fixture.** A user types an invalid shutter value, rotates the phone, and then returns to the controls.

**Acceptance oracle.** The invalid draft is not applied, valid state survives appropriately, and the source recording configuration remains unchanged.

**Deliberate mutation.** Apply every partially typed numeric string immediately to the camera.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Manual interaction contract and draft-state tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p132"></a>
### P132. Build scopes with declared signal domains

**Entry gate:** P131. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Make waveform, histogram, clipping, and false color informative rather than misleading.

**Implementation method.** Label whether a scope measures source, working image, encoded Log, or display preview. Record sampling resolution and freshness. Preview-only RGB8 aids cannot certify sensor clipping or ten-bit precision. Keep scope computation off critical capture ownership.

**Test-first fixture.** A clipped display preview of an unclipped high-range source and a stale waveform after inference load spikes.

**Acceptance oracle.** The scope identifies its domain and stale status rather than falsely declaring source clipping from the preview.

**Deliberate mutation.** Label every preview histogram sensor exposure regardless of its input.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Scope domain model and monitoring correctness tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Baseline fixture.** A clipped display preview of an unclipped high-range source and a stale waveform after inference load spikes.

**Adversarial operation.** Perform the task on the physical phone with a thermal warning, permission issue, or recovery event.

**Required response.** Let the user understand what was saved and complete the appropriate next action without hidden state.

**Baseline oracle.** The scope identifies its domain and stale status rather than falsely declaring source clipping from the preview.

**False-pass control.** A desktop mockup cannot substitute for observed physical task completion.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat one-handed operation, outdoor visibility, and finding an interrupted take.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p133"></a>
### P133. Implement accessible focus and recipe controls

**Entry gate:** P132. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Make visual editing possible without relying solely on tiny unlabeled gestures.

**Implementation method.** Provide accessible names, state descriptions, keyboard or switch navigation where applicable, and numeric alternatives for ROIs and focus controls. Do not convey failure only through color. Preserve focus order across panels and orientation changes.

**Test-first fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Acceptance oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**Deliberate mutation.** Expose a custom control only as an unlabeled canvas.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Accessibility interaction tests and semantic control audit. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p133-01"></a>
#### TC-P133-01. Landscape and large-text stress

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Open advanced controls with increased font scale in landscape during an active take.

**Required response.** Keep Record or Stop, essential warnings, and selected source status reachable and readable.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** Critical actions hidden inside scrolling content must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat small display settings, orientation changes, and simultaneous audio and storage warnings.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p133-02"></a>
#### TC-P133-02. Source-look label confusion

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Select a large-format film recipe while the underlying source remains a lower-resolution SDR or experimental RAW route.

**Required response.** Display the actual source and simulated look independently with their evidence status.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** Renaming a source mode after the virtual format must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat preset changes, saved recipe reopening, and export sharing.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p133-03"></a>
#### TC-P133-03. Invalid control draft

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Enter an incomplete or out-of-range numeric value and interrupt editing before Apply.

**Required response.** Preserve committed settings and keep the draft visibly unapplied or invalid.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** Partially typed input reaching the camera must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat shutter, ISO, focus distance, ROI coordinates, and output dimensions.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p133-04"></a>
#### TC-P133-04. Stale or wrong-domain scope

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Feed a monitoring aid delayed preview samples or a display-clipped image from an unclipped source.

**Required response.** Identify freshness and measurement domain instead of falsely reporting sensor conditions.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** An RGB8 preview histogram must not certify source bit depth or sensor clipping.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat waveform, false color, focus peaking, and color histogram.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p133-05"></a>
#### TC-P133-05. Nonvisual interaction

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Perform the core phase task using accessibility navigation and spoken state information.

**Required response.** Expose usable names, order, values, and cancellation without relying only on color or precision gestures.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** An unlabeled custom canvas as the only control must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat camera operation, ROI selection, focus editing, and recovery export.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p133-06"></a>
#### TC-P133-06. Premature success indication

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Finish frame submission while verification or publication still remains incomplete.

**Required response.** Show the actual remaining stage and withhold accepted completion until its gate passes.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** A one-hundred-percent banner before required verification must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat encoder drain, full decode, sidecar export, and gallery commit.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p133-07"></a>
#### TC-P133-07. Unfair comparison view

**Baseline fixture.** A screen-reader user selects a grey-reference ROI, changes virtual focus, and cancels a development job.

**Adversarial operation.** Compare outputs at different times, scales, or display transforms without making those differences visible.

**Required response.** Align comparable content or clearly disclose the mismatch before presenting a preference judgment.

**Baseline oracle.** All actions have usable labels and state feedback, and cancellation remains available without a precision gesture.

**False-pass control.** Automatically enhancing one side of a comparison must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat source-versus-result, recipe revisions, and different output aspect ratios.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.

<a id="p134"></a>
### P134. Design transparent progress and failure states

**Entry gate:** P133. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Tell users what is happening without fabricated percentages or vague success banners.

**Implementation method.** Progress should identify capture, inference, rendering, verification, or publication. Use indeterminate states when remaining work is unknown. Errors distinguish unsupported mode, unavailable model, source corruption, output failure, and retained recoverable footage.

**Test-first fixture.** A render reaches its final frame but still requires full decode verification and gallery publication.

**Acceptance oracle.** The UI does not show completed until acceptance and publication policy are satisfied.

**Deliberate mutation.** Show one hundred percent success immediately after the last frame is submitted to the encoder.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Progress semantics and failure-state screenshots/tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p135"></a>
### P135. Build side-by-side comparison tools

**Entry gate:** P134. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Help users judge real improvements with matched inputs and controllable viewing.

**Implementation method.** Provide synchronized playback, split views, exposure-consistent comparisons, effect bypass, and recipe metadata. Avoid comparing different moments or differently scaled thumbnails. Allow inspecting clean source and processed output without accidental double transforms.

**Test-first fixture.** Two renders of the same clip with different duration mappings and different display transforms.

**Acceptance oracle.** The comparison aligns time explicitly and makes differing transforms visible rather than implying a fair matched test.

**Deliberate mutation.** Compare unrelated frames and automatically boost one version’s contrast.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Comparison viewer and synchronized playback tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p136"></a>
### P136. Run usability acceptance on the physical phone

**Entry gate:** P135. **Primary seam:** native screens, control models, accessibility semantics, monitoring UI.

**Research objective.** Validate real shooting ergonomics rather than relying on static mockups.

**Implementation method.** Test outdoor readability, one-handed operation, landscape framing, gloves where relevant, large text, interruptions, and recovery discovery. Observe user tasks and errors. Keep aesthetic preferences separate from measurable task completion and footage safety.

**Test-first fixture.** A user starts a take, receives a thermal warning, stops, finds the retained clip, and shares its evidence.

**Acceptance oracle.** The task completes without hidden controls or ambiguity about whether footage was saved.

**Deliberate mutation.** Approve the UI from a desktop screenshot without a real shooting workflow.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Physical usability report and prioritized corrections. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="workstream-18"></a>
## Workstream 18. Movie recipes, reference scholarship, and offline catalogues

A movie lookup should return a sourced reconstruction recipe, not an assertion that one LUT reproduces an entire production. Separate documented stock and format facts from inferred optics and creative finishing. Movies can contain multiple acquisition methods and looks, and different releases may differ. The catalogue must be usable offline, transparent about uncertainty, and careful with reference-image rights. Search quality should help users discover relevant techniques without inventing production metadata.

**Integration seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages. **Accountable specialty:** movie catalogue and scholarly evidence editor.

**Measurement domain:** field-level provenance, retrieval correctness, rights compliance, and reconstruction transparency. **Evidence family:** primary-source citations, recipe versions, search fixtures, and distributable-asset manifests.

**Primary background:** [^F04][^F05][^F06] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p137"></a>
### P137. Define the movie evidence schema

**Entry gate:** P007, P073, P089, P121. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Represent production facts, reconstruction choices, and unknowns as different data types.

**Implementation method.** Store movie, scene family, acquisition format, stock, camera and lens facts, processing notes, release reference, citations, confidence, and our recipe parameters. Every documented or contradicted claim needs a source; unknown values remain null rather than guessed.

**Test-first fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Acceptance oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**Deliberate mutation.** Fill missing lens fields with plausible cinema equipment and mark them documented.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Movie-claim schema and evidence-state tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p137-01"></a>
#### TC-P137-01. Missing production fact

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Remove verified lens or scene-specific stock information from an otherwise complete movie record.

**Required response.** Keep the fact unknown while allowing a clearly labelled creative reconstruction.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** A plausible equipment guess marked documented must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat camera, lens, stock, process, and release-version fields.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p137-02"></a>
#### TC-P137-02. Whole-film overgeneralization

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Provide a source describing several acquisition methods and attempt to assign one to every shot.

**Required response.** Represent supported variants and preserve uncertainty at scene level.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** A title match alone must not establish every scene’s technical recipe.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat mixed color/monochrome, mixed formats, and location-specific stock choices.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p137-03"></a>
#### TC-P137-03. Creative edit overwrites evidence

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Change virtual aperture, grade, or grain inside a user derivative recipe.

**Required response.** Create a new reconstruction version without altering historical production facts.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** User preferences must not replace the cinematographer’s sourced metadata.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat recipe save, rename, share, and update from a newer catalogue package.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p137-04"></a>
#### TC-P137-04. Offline search ambiguity

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Search misspelled titles, alternate titles, or stock names without network access.

**Required response.** Return relevant local candidates with transparent matching and evidence status.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** A remote generation call must not be required for basic catalogue lookup.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat filtered searches for format, monochrome, and scene family.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p137-05"></a>
#### TC-P137-05. Publicly accessible but unlicensed asset

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Offer a web-accessible still, LUT, or profile whose redistribution permission is unknown.

**Required response.** Retain appropriate citation metadata while excluding unapproved bytes from the release bundle.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** Public visibility must not be treated as a redistribution licence.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat promotional images, commercial LUTs, and research model weights.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p137-06"></a>
#### TC-P137-06. Reference edition conflict

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Supply references from different film releases or display assumptions with different appearance.

**Required response.** Keep separate targets or explicit uncertainty rather than inventing one definitive look.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** Averaging inconsistent editions into a historical fact must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat theatrical, digital, HDR, and unidentified reference versions.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p137-07"></a>
#### TC-P137-07. Parameter matching alters content

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Use an automatic look suggestion that changes facial geometry or replaces scene texture.

**Required response.** Reject unrequested content synthesis and restrict matching to declared rendering parameters.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** A visually similar generated scene is not preserved camera footage.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat faces, text, fine patterns, and moving objects.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p137-08"></a>
#### TC-P137-08. Preference mistaken for factual accuracy

**Baseline fixture.** A film with documented stock choices but no verified lens information for the selected scene.

**Adversarial operation.** Give a popular reconstructed recipe higher user ratings than a well-sourced alternative.

**Required response.** Keep appearance preference separate from evidence completeness and historical claims.

**Baseline oracle.** The recipe can use a clearly reconstructed virtual lens while retaining the production lens field as unknown.

**False-pass control.** Popularity cannot certify a stock or lens identification.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat blind comparisons, expert review, and conflicting production sources.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p138"></a>
### P138. Build the first sourced recipe family

**Entry gate:** P137. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Demonstrate the database with a small, well-supported set rather than hundreds of names.

**Implementation method.** Use primary production accounts where available and separate daylight, low-light, monochrome, and format variants. Record the exact scope of each source. Do not extend a statement about a whole production into an unsupported claim about every shot.

**Test-first fixture.** A production account documenting several stocks used under different shooting conditions.

**Acceptance oracle.** The database creates separate supported variants and clearly marks any scene-specific reconstruction.

**Deliberate mutation.** Assign one stock and one lens to every scene because the film title matches.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Initial recipe family with source-to-field traceability. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Baseline oracle.** The database creates separate supported variants and clearly marks any scene-specific reconstruction.

**False-pass control.** A plausible equipment guess marked documented must fail.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.

<a id="p139"></a>
### P139. Version creative reconstruction parameters

**Entry gate:** P138. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Make our interpretation editable without modifying the underlying production facts.

**Implementation method.** Keep a recipe graph linked to, but distinct from, evidence records. Version exposure, stock model, virtual lens, grain, halation, print response, and grade independently. A user adaptation becomes a derivative recipe with its own name and provenance.

**Test-first fixture.** A user changes the virtual aperture and print contrast of a movie-inspired recipe.

**Acceptance oracle.** The original documented facts remain unchanged and the edited appearance is stored as a user reconstruction.

**Deliberate mutation.** Overwrite the cinematographer’s documented settings with the user’s creative changes.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Reconstruction versioning and immutable fact tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p140"></a>
### P140. Implement offline search and filtering

**Entry gate:** P139. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Make the catalogue useful without network dependence or opaque recommendation behavior.

**Implementation method.** Index titles, alternate titles, stock names, formats, scene families, and evidence quality. Support typo-tolerant discovery with explicit matching behavior. Keep local user recipes private and allow sorting by relevant technical criteria rather than invented popularity.

**Test-first fixture.** A search for a misspelled film title while the phone is offline and a filter for monochrome large-format recipes.

**Acceptance oracle.** The correct local candidates appear with their evidence status and no network request is required.

**Deliberate mutation.** Call a remote language model for every catalogue search.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Offline search index and deterministic retrieval tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p141"></a>
### P141. Manage reference media rights and attribution

**Entry gate:** P140. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Avoid bundling copyrighted frames or proprietary look data without the required permission.

**Implementation method.** Store links and factual citations separately from distributable assets. Use owned comparison footage and approved thumbnails. Track model, profile, LUT, image, and text rights independently. Unknown redistribution status blocks packaging that asset until reviewed.

**Test-first fixture.** A useful production still with an accessible public URL but no permission to bundle it in the app.

**Acceptance oracle.** The catalogue can retain a citation while excluding the image bytes from the distributable package.

**Deliberate mutation.** Treat public web accessibility as a redistribution licence.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Content rights manifest and package licence gate. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p142"></a>
### P142. Implement constrained reference matching

**Entry gate:** P141. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Use optional analysis to suggest renderer parameters without replacing source content.

**Implementation method.** Analyze approved reference material for broad color, tone, texture, and contrast characteristics. Fit bounded parameters in our renderer, preserve scene structure, and expose the result as a suggestion. Keep lighting and composition mismatch visible as limitations.

**Test-first fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Acceptance oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use unconstrained neural stylization and call altered faces faithful source footage.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Parameter suggestion prototype and structure-preservation tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p142-01"></a>
#### TC-P142-01. Missing production fact

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Remove verified lens or scene-specific stock information from an otherwise complete movie record.

**Required response.** Keep the fact unknown while allowing a clearly labelled creative reconstruction.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** A plausible equipment guess marked documented must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat camera, lens, stock, process, and release-version fields.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p142-02"></a>
#### TC-P142-02. Whole-film overgeneralization

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Provide a source describing several acquisition methods and attempt to assign one to every shot.

**Required response.** Represent supported variants and preserve uncertainty at scene level.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** A title match alone must not establish every scene’s technical recipe.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat mixed color/monochrome, mixed formats, and location-specific stock choices.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p142-03"></a>
#### TC-P142-03. Creative edit overwrites evidence

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Change virtual aperture, grade, or grain inside a user derivative recipe.

**Required response.** Create a new reconstruction version without altering historical production facts.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** User preferences must not replace the cinematographer’s sourced metadata.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat recipe save, rename, share, and update from a newer catalogue package.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p142-04"></a>
#### TC-P142-04. Offline search ambiguity

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Search misspelled titles, alternate titles, or stock names without network access.

**Required response.** Return relevant local candidates with transparent matching and evidence status.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** A remote generation call must not be required for basic catalogue lookup.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat filtered searches for format, monochrome, and scene family.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p142-05"></a>
#### TC-P142-05. Publicly accessible but unlicensed asset

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Offer a web-accessible still, LUT, or profile whose redistribution permission is unknown.

**Required response.** Retain appropriate citation metadata while excluding unapproved bytes from the release bundle.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** Public visibility must not be treated as a redistribution licence.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat promotional images, commercial LUTs, and research model weights.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p142-06"></a>
#### TC-P142-06. Reference edition conflict

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Supply references from different film releases or display assumptions with different appearance.

**Required response.** Keep separate targets or explicit uncertainty rather than inventing one definitive look.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** Averaging inconsistent editions into a historical fact must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat theatrical, digital, HDR, and unidentified reference versions.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p142-07"></a>
#### TC-P142-07. Parameter matching alters content

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Use an automatic look suggestion that changes facial geometry or replaces scene texture.

**Required response.** Reject unrequested content synthesis and restrict matching to declared rendering parameters.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** A visually similar generated scene is not preserved camera footage.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat faces, text, fine patterns, and moving objects.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p142-08"></a>
#### TC-P142-08. Preference mistaken for factual accuracy

**Baseline fixture.** A reference shot with dramatic directional lighting and a user source recorded under flat overhead light.

**Adversarial operation.** Give a popular reconstructed recipe higher user ratings than a well-sourced alternative.

**Required response.** Keep appearance preference separate from evidence completeness and historical claims.

**Baseline oracle.** The tool proposes a bounded grade but does not claim to recreate the missing lighting geometry.

**False-pass control.** Popularity cannot certify a stock or lens identification.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat blind comparisons, expert review, and conflicting production sources.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p143"></a>
### P143. Support release-specific and scene-specific looks

**Entry gate:** P142. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Avoid treating every distribution version of a film as one fixed color target.

**Implementation method.** Record reference edition, format, display assumptions, and scene family when known. Permit several interpretations under one movie title. A missing edition remains unknown; the app must not infer a theatrical print response from an arbitrary screenshot.

**Test-first fixture.** Two legally obtained references from different releases with visibly different contrast and color treatment.

**Acceptance oracle.** The database preserves separate recipe targets and identifies which reference supports each.

**Deliberate mutation.** Average all references into one supposedly definitive movie look.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Release-aware catalogue and ambiguity tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p144"></a>
### P144. Validate recipe fidelity and honesty

**Entry gate:** P143. **Primary seam:** movie evidence schema, recipe database, search, rights-aware content packages.

**Research objective.** Evaluate whether recipes are coherent and enjoyable without overstating historical or physical accuracy.

**Implementation method.** Use matched owned sources, blind preference tests, parameter ablations, and expert review where possible. Score evidence completeness separately from appearance preference. A popular recipe may remain reconstructed; a well-sourced recipe may need artistic refinement.

**Test-first fixture.** One visually preferred recipe with uncertain production facts and another fully sourced but less preferred interpretation.

**Acceptance oracle.** The app reports these different qualities without promoting preference into factual certainty.

**Deliberate mutation.** Use user star ratings as evidence that a stock identification is correct.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Recipe evaluation report and catalogue quality policy. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.
