<a id="workstream-19"></a>
## Workstream 19. Validation infrastructure, security, release, and operations

Release readiness combines numerical correctness, real-device evidence, media integrity, user control, and maintainable distribution. Automated tests must exercise production paths and fail for meaningful defects; a large test count is not itself quality. Protect imported media and model packages as untrusted input. Preserve privacy by default. Release claims must be generated from evidence for exact configurations, not from the ambition of this directive.

**Integration seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging. **Accountable specialty:** quality, security, and release lead.

**Measurement domain:** critical defect detection, privacy, preservation, reproducibility, and claim accuracy. **Evidence family:** test reports, mutation results, threat-model fixtures, signed build identities, and physical acceptance records.

**Primary background:** [^A08][^A07][^A09][^R01] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p145"></a>
### P145. Build the layered automated test system

**Entry gate:** P004, P032, P064, P128, P136, P144. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Separate host arithmetic, JVM policies, Android integration, GPU parity, and physical acceptance.

**Implementation method.** Run fast deterministic contracts on every change, then focused integration suites and scheduled device experiments. Preserve failing evidence and classify unavailable hardware explicitly. Tests must call production interfaces or declared independent references, not duplicate trivial implementations.

**Test-first fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Acceptance oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**Deliberate mutation.** Count skipped hardware tests as passing tests in the release summary.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Layered CI plan and machine-readable evidence aggregation. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p145-01"></a>
#### TC-P145-01. Skipped test laundering

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Combine passing host tests with unavailable hardware and a failing critical integration test.

**Required response.** Keep every result category visible and block claims requiring the missing or failing evidence.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** Counting skips as passes must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat emulator-only, GPU-unavailable, and physical-codec-unavailable environments.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p145-02"></a>
#### TC-P145-02. Critical mutant survives

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Insert a plausible fault into a production seam and run the intended regression suite.

**Required response.** Require the relevant test to fail; surviving critical mutants expose insufficient assertions.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** High line coverage without fault detection must not count as adequate protection.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat timestamp pairing, source retention, range signalling, and checkpoint identity mutants.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p145-03"></a>
#### TC-P145-03. Hostile imported file

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Submit malformed lengths, excessive dimensions, nonfinite transforms, or archive traversal paths.

**Required response.** Reject within bounded resource limits without escaping storage or corrupting retained media.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** Trusting extensions or unvalidated headers must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat parser truncation, decompression pressure, and repeated invalid imports.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p145-04"></a>
#### TC-P145-04. Unexpected network transmission

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Observe capture and development traffic with local assets already installed.

**Required response.** Transmit no frames, depth, audio, or private metadata under the offline default.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** An analytics thumbnail upload contradicts the local-processing claim.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat startup, errors, crashes, export, and model initialization.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p145-05"></a>
#### TC-P145-05. Thermal safety pressure

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Exercise sustained workloads until the operating-system thermal policy requires action.

**Required response.** Reduce optional work or stop capture according to the documented preservation policy.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** Bypassing protection to sustain an advertised rate must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat warm starts, charging, longer duration, and combined rendering load where safely testable.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p145-06"></a>
#### TC-P145-06. Update threatens private media

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Install an authorized signed update over a version containing sources, profiles, and recovery data.

**Required response.** Preserve compatible data and provide explicit migration or refusal rather than destructive convenience.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** Uninstalling silently to solve signing mismatch must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat interrupted migration, rollback limits, and pending render jobs.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p145-07"></a>
#### TC-P145-07. Release claim exceeds evidence

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Generate release notes for features with mixed implemented, experimental, and physically qualified states.

**Required response.** Describe each scope accurately and exclude unsupported native-resolution or camera-equivalence claims.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** Copying the aspirational roadmap into the implemented list must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat source modes, live depth, deferred optics, and calibration status.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p145-08"></a>
#### TC-P145-08. Critical preservation defect

**Baseline fixture.** A green host suite alongside an unavailable physical ten-bit codec test and a failing GPU color test.

**Adversarial operation.** Demonstrate a path that deletes the sole retained take despite otherwise excellent visual quality.

**Required response.** Block release until the defect is fixed and a reproducing regression test passes.

**Baseline oracle.** The report keeps the GPU failure and unavailable device gate visible and does not declare the release fully qualified.

**False-pass control.** Aesthetic quality cannot waive a data-loss gate.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat capture failure, publication failure, cancellation, and cold-start recovery.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p146"></a>
### P146. Add property and mutation testing

**Entry gate:** P145. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Prove that tests can detect plausible defects rather than merely execute lines.

**Implementation method.** Generate valid and invalid numeric domains, temporal event sequences, geometry combinations, and malformed records. Introduce selected mutants such as range confusion, timestamp reuse, CFA swaps, and missing hash checks. Require critical mutants to be killed by the intended tests.

**Test-first fixture.** A mutation replacing exact timestamp pairing with nearest-neighbor matching.

**Acceptance oracle.** The metadata association test fails for the deliberately close-but-wrong timestamp fixture.

**Deliberate mutation.** Run only happy-path examples with conveniently identical metadata.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Property generators and critical mutation catalogue. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p147"></a>
### P147. Secure media and profile import boundaries

**Entry gate:** P146. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Treat external files, archives, LUTs, models, and profiles as hostile until validated.

**Implementation method.** Bound lengths, dimensions, nesting, decompression, and allocation before use. Validate paths and hashes, restrict URI grants, and keep native parsers current. Reject nonfinite matrices and dangerous archive paths. Fuzz parsers with retained minimal reproducers.

**Test-first fixture.** A profile containing NaN, a huge declared image dimension, and an archive path attempting parent traversal.

**Acceptance oracle.** All inputs fail safely without excessive allocation, file escape, or source corruption.

**Deliberate mutation.** Trust extension names and allocate according to unvalidated headers.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Import threat model and parser fuzz corpus. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Required response.** Keep every result category visible and block claims requiring the missing or failing evidence.

**Baseline oracle.** All inputs fail safely without excessive allocation, file escape, or source corruption.

**False-pass control.** Counting skips as passes must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat emulator-only, GPU-unavailable, and physical-codec-unavailable environments.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p147-02"></a>

**Baseline oracle.** All inputs fail safely without excessive allocation, file escape, or source corruption.

**False-pass control.** High line coverage without fault detection must not count as adequate protection.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat timestamp pairing, source retention, range signalling, and checkpoint identity mutants.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.

<a id="p148"></a>
### P148. Verify offline privacy and permissions

**Entry gate:** P147. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Make local processing and minimum permission use observable properties.

**Implementation method.** Audit network traffic, permission prompts, logging, crash reports, and exported metadata. The default render path must not upload frames, depth maps, faces, or audio. Optional content downloads are explicit and separable from operation after installation.

**Test-first fixture.** Airplane-mode capture and development with all model assets installed, plus a diagnostic export.

**Acceptance oracle.** The workflow succeeds locally and the report omits personal paths and unnecessary identifiers.

**Deliberate mutation.** Send image thumbnails to analytics while describing the app as entirely offline.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Use a deterministic fixture seed and a versioned oracle. The named false implementation must be rejected. If an expected result changes, document the reason before updating the test; never regenerate references merely to obtain green.

**Required deliverable.** Privacy test report and permission inventory. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p149"></a>
### P149. Establish thermal and endurance acceptance

**Entry gate:** P148. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Use conservative safety policies and measured operating envelopes.

**Implementation method.** Run controlled sustained tests across relevant source and render configurations, record ambient conditions and device state, and observe thermal callbacks. Reduce optional preview work first. Severe pressure triggers a controlled stop that preserves footage; do not bypass protections.

**Test-first fixture.** A prolonged high-resolution take followed by deferred depth rendering while the phone is already warm.

**Acceptance oracle.** The app follows its documented limits, retains media, and does not claim unlimited performance from a short cold run.

**Deliberate mutation.** Ignore severe thermal status to maintain an advertised frame-rate claim.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Endurance protocol and configuration-specific operating envelope. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p150"></a>
### P150. Prepare signing and reproducible distribution

**Entry gate:** P149. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Separate debug convenience from a maintainable release and update process.

**Implementation method.** Use owner-controlled signing, pinned dependencies, reproducible source records, and explicit version migration tests. Keep secrets outside the repository. Verify installation and update without losing private sources, profiles, recipes, or recovery records.

**Test-first fixture.** An update from an earlier signed release containing private RAW sources and a pending render job.

**Acceptance oracle.** The update preserves compatible data and handles migration explicitly; signing mismatch is not solved by silently uninstalling user data.

**Deliberate mutation.** Recommend uninstalling the previous app without warning about private footage loss.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Inspect resource and metadata boundaries in addition to the visible result. The test must reach production logic rather than assert only mock calls. Capture red, green, mutation sensitivity, and the remaining integration conditions separately.

**Required deliverable.** Release signing plan and update preservation tests. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p151"></a>
### P151. Generate honest release notes and capability badges

**Entry gate:** P150. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Tie every public capability claim to current evidence and documented limits.

**Implementation method.** Build release summaries from accepted records, including exact supported tuples and experimental features. Separate software tests from physical qualification. Keep known failures visible and avoid general camera-equivalence or universal-resolution language.

**Test-first fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Acceptance oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**Deliberate mutation.** Copy aspirational requirements directly into the implemented features list.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Evidence-driven release notes and claim audit. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**False-pass control.** High line coverage without fault detection must not count as adequate protection.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat timestamp pairing, source retention, range signalling, and checkpoint identity mutants.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p151-03"></a>
#### TC-P151-03. Hostile imported file

**Baseline fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Adversarial operation.** Submit malformed lengths, excessive dimensions, nonfinite transforms, or archive traversal paths.

**Required response.** Reject within bounded resource limits without escaping storage or corrupting retained media.

**Baseline oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**False-pass control.** Trusting extensions or unvalidated headers must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat parser truncation, decompression pressure, and repeated invalid imports.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p151-04"></a>
#### TC-P151-04. Unexpected network transmission

**Baseline fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Adversarial operation.** Observe capture and development traffic with local assets already installed.

**Required response.** Transmit no frames, depth, audio, or private metadata under the offline default.

**Baseline oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**False-pass control.** An analytics thumbnail upload contradicts the local-processing claim.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat startup, errors, crashes, export, and model initialization.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p151-05"></a>
#### TC-P151-05. Thermal safety pressure

**Baseline fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Adversarial operation.** Exercise sustained workloads until the operating-system thermal policy requires action.

**Required response.** Reduce optional work or stop capture according to the documented preservation policy.

**Baseline oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**False-pass control.** Bypassing protection to sustain an advertised rate must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat warm starts, charging, longer duration, and combined rendering load where safely testable.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p151-06"></a>
#### TC-P151-06. Update threatens private media

**Baseline fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Adversarial operation.** Install an authorized signed update over a version containing sources, profiles, and recovery data.

**Required response.** Preserve compatible data and provide explicit migration or refusal rather than destructive convenience.

**Baseline oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**False-pass control.** Uninstalling silently to solve signing mismatch must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat interrupted migration, rollback limits, and pending render jobs.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p151-07"></a>
#### TC-P151-07. Release claim exceeds evidence

**Baseline fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Adversarial operation.** Generate release notes for features with mixed implemented, experimental, and physically qualified states.

**Required response.** Describe each scope accurately and exclude unsupported native-resolution or camera-equivalence claims.

**Baseline oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**False-pass control.** Copying the aspirational roadmap into the implemented list must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat source modes, live depth, deferred optics, and calibration status.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p151-08"></a>
#### TC-P151-08. Critical preservation defect

**Baseline fixture.** A release with qualified SDR recording, experimental RAW development, and deferred-only depth effects.

**Adversarial operation.** Demonstrate a path that deletes the sole retained take despite otherwise excellent visual quality.

**Required response.** Block release until the defect is fixed and a reproducing regression test passes.

**Baseline oracle.** The release notes reflect those scopes and do not advertise live RAW cinema capture or universal 8K support.

**False-pass control.** Aesthetic quality cannot waive a data-loss gate.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat capture failure, publication failure, cancellation, and cold-start recovery.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p152"></a>
### P152. Run the production readiness review

**Entry gate:** P151. **Primary seam:** CI, host and device tests, security boundaries, release packaging.

**Research objective.** Make a deliberate release decision based on critical risks and complete workflows.

**Implementation method.** Review footage retention, crash recovery, color signalling, temporal artifacts, licensing, privacy, accessibility, and update safety. Resolve or explicitly defer noncritical issues. A critical data-loss or misleading-capture defect blocks release regardless of visual quality.

**Test-first fixture.** A visually excellent build that occasionally deletes the only staging copy after a failed publication.

**Acceptance oracle.** The release is blocked until preservation is fixed and regression evidence exists.

**Deliberate mutation.** Waive a critical data-loss issue because promotional footage looks convincing.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Close the phase only when the deliverable, focused tests, and relevant regression evidence agree. Preserve blocked hardware or rights gates explicitly. A documentation update can describe implementation but cannot substitute for its execution evidence.

**Required deliverable.** Production readiness dossier and signed-off decision record. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Baseline oracle.** The release is blocked until preservation is fixed and regression evidence exists.

**False-pass control.** Counting skips as passes must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat emulator-only, GPU-unavailable, and physical-codec-unavailable environments.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.

<a id="workstream-20"></a>
## Workstream 20. Advanced research and strictly bounded firmware investigation

Advanced work follows evidence, not the assumption that software can remove every physical limitation. Firmware and HAL investigation is a separate research track with explicit user authorization, device-specific recovery planning, and no dependency from the usable film app. Begin with public documentation, exported diagnostics, and reversible tests. Treat hidden vendor capabilities as unknown until independently verified. Improvements are accepted for measured benefit to captured information or reliable operation, not for lower-level access alone.

**Integration seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation. **Accountable specialty:** advanced research investigator.

**Measurement domain:** hypothesis specificity, reversibility, measured benefit, and authorization boundaries. **Evidence family:** device-specific diagnostics, baseline comparisons, risk decisions, and retained experimental logs.

**Primary background:** [^S01][^S02][^S03][^A03][^A09] The following requirements are proposed project policy; cited sources do not certify the implementation.


<a id="p153"></a>
### P153. Identify the actual blocked capability

**Entry gate:** P008, P016, P040, P152. **Primary seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation.

**Research objective.** State a concrete research question before proposing firmware work.

**Implementation method.** Use current public diagnostics and failed qualified app experiments to locate the bottleneck: sensor stream, HAL exposure, codec interface, synchronization, or app performance. Specify the desired observation and an alternative application-level path. Avoid vague goals such as unlock everything.

**Test-first fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Acceptance oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**Deliberate mutation.** Attribute every low frame rate to Samsung restrictions without measurements.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the red assertion before implementation. After green, remove the deliberate defect and run the adjacent regression suite. A successful demonstration without retained inputs and an independently inspectable result does not close this phase.

**Required deliverable.** Blocked-capability hypothesis and evidence dossier. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.


<a id="tc-p153-01"></a>
#### TC-P153-01. Wrong bottleneck attribution

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Present a throughput problem caused by storage or scheduling as evidence of a hidden firmware restriction.

**Required response.** Require controlled isolation of the bottleneck before low-level modification is proposed.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** Assuming every slow path is vendor blocking must fail.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat acquisition-only, saved-source, development, and encoder-stage measurements.

**Evidence obligation.** Save the baseline, perturbed input, outcome, and detecting assertion under this case identifier.


<a id="tc-p153-02"></a>
#### TC-P153-02. Incomplete public source

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Provide a public kernel or firmware-related package that omits proprietary imaging components.

**Required response.** Describe exactly what can be inspected and keep missing components unknown.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** A source archive must not be called a complete camera firmware implementation without evidence.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat different device variants and software versions.

**Evidence obligation.** Retain exact input identities, observed transitions, and the independent comparison result.


<a id="tc-p153-03"></a>
#### TC-P153-03. Unexplored reversible alternative

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Fail one codec or camera interface while another public route remains untested.

**Required response.** Evaluate plausible reversible alternatives before declaring the broader capture goal blocked.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** One failed P010 route must not prove all ten-bit encoding impossible.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat surface input, reduced geometry, deferred processing, and scheduling changes.

**Evidence obligation.** Record the failure boundary and show that unrelated valid behavior remains intact.


<a id="tc-p153-04"></a>
#### TC-P153-04. Missing explicit modification authorization

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Prepare a flashing or irreversible device-change step without fresh specific user approval.

**Required response.** Keep the operation unexecuted and continue non-destructive application work.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** A general app-development request does not authorize an irreversible flash.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat bootloader changes, security-state changes, and unverified recovery images.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p153-05"></a>
#### TC-P153-05. Advertised unlock without delivery

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Change reported capability metadata but obtain no valid new sensor output.

**Required response.** Fail the acquisition hypothesis despite the expanded mode menu.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** A newly visible setting is not proof of useful capture.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat sample receipt, decoded fidelity, sustained cadence, and thermal checks.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p153-06"></a>
#### TC-P153-06. Computational capture overclaim

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Merge multiple exposures and present the result as a single unchanged sensor exposure.

**Required response.** Label computational acquisition and measure motion artifacts and retained information separately.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** An attractive merge cannot erase its source-sampling provenance.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat moving subjects, clipped channels, alignment failures, and temporal ghosts.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p153-07"></a>
#### TC-P153-07. Advanced model cost regression

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Adopt a larger research model that improves one artifact but exceeds practical memory or time budgets.

**Required response.** Report the quality-cost tradeoff and retain the stable baseline until the adoption gate passes.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** A leaderboard position alone cannot justify replacement.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat difficult-scene quality, sustained device load, and deferred job interruption.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p153-08"></a>
#### TC-P153-08. Unreproducible research closure

**Baseline fixture.** A RAW route limited by measured disk throughput rather than a denied camera mode.

**Adversarial operation.** Archive only favorable outputs while omitting failed experiments and essential setup details.

**Required response.** Preserve enough evidence to reconstruct decisions and reproduce qualified results independently.

**Baseline oracle.** The research plan addresses storage and buffering before proposing a firmware modification.

**False-pass control.** A promotional reel cannot substitute for an engineering archive.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat fresh-maintainer reproduction of capture, film rendering, optics, and rejected hypotheses.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="p154"></a>
### P154. Survey public firmware and HAL information

**Entry gate:** P153. **Primary seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation.

**Research objective.** Research the device architecture without modifying the user’s phone.

**Implementation method.** Inspect official architecture documentation, available source releases, public logs, and lawful device diagnostics. Record exact model and firmware applicability. Separate kernel source availability from access to proprietary camera processing components.

**Test-first fixture.** A public source package that lacks the proprietary imaging component needed for the proposed change.

**Acceptance oracle.** The report records the missing component rather than claiming the source package is a complete camera firmware implementation.

**Deliberate mutation.** Assume publishing a kernel source tree exposes every camera algorithm and sensor mode.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the fixture independent of UI state. Run the positive path, the named mutation, and the relevant boundary cases. Refactor only after the focused assertions pass; preserve the original failing log as evidence of test sensitivity.

**Required deliverable.** Non-destructive architecture research report. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

<a id="p155"></a>
### P155. Evaluate reversible application-level alternatives

**Entry gate:** P154. **Primary seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation.

**Research objective.** Exhaust useful normal-app approaches before escalating risk.

**Implementation method.** Compare alternate stream combinations, smaller source sizes, different codec interfaces, deferred development, CPU-GPU scheduling, and retained RAW workflows. Measure the information and quality tradeoffs. Keep each alternative honestly labelled by source lineage.

**Test-first fixture.** A surface-only ten-bit encoder that could support a qualified GPU route even though the P010 Image developer is unavailable.

**Acceptance oracle.** The plan explores that interface before declaring the sensor-to-Log goal impossible.

**Deliberate mutation.** Treat failure of one codec input interface as proof that every ten-bit path is unavailable.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Separate arithmetic correctness from framework and hardware behavior. Complete host checks first, then exercise the real integration seam. An unavailable device gate remains unavailable and must not inherit a pass from a synthetic fixture.

**Required deliverable.** Alternative-path experiments and comparative decision. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Entry gate:** P155. **Primary seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation.

A general request to build an app does not authorize flashing. Keep ordinary development operational without firmware changes.

### P157. Design instrumented low-level experiments

**Entry gate:** P156. **Primary seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation.

**Research objective.** Make any authorized low-level change minimal, observable, and reversible where technically possible.

**Implementation method.** Change one hypothesized constraint at a time, preserve the baseline, record checksums and logs, and define failure triggers before execution. Do not disable thermal safeguards or falsify capability metadata to make unsupported modes appear available.

**Test-first fixture.** A modification that changes advertised stream metadata but produces no valid additional sensor frames.

**Acceptance oracle.** The experiment fails its actual-delivery hypothesis despite the expanded menu.

**Deliberate mutation.** Call an advertised mode unlocked without capturing and validating its output.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Record the complete input contract and failure policy before coding. Validate rejected inputs as carefully as accepted outputs. Confirm that failure leaves prior sources and accepted artifacts intact, then run the owner component’s regression suite.

**Required deliverable.** Instrumented experimental protocol and observation schema. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Entry gate:** P158. **Primary seam:** capability research, experimental branches of the design, physical validation.

**Research objective.** Investigate richer depth, multi-view cues, or research models only after the baseline product is stable.

**Implementation method.** Compare real synchronized inputs where available, improved temporal models, and calibrated geometry under explicit resource and privacy limits. Keep the original on-device workflow usable. New models require licensing, conversion, and difficult-scene validation again.

**Test-first fixture.** A larger temporal model improving some boundaries but causing memory pressure and unacceptable deferred rendering time.

**Acceptance oracle.** The decision reports the quality-cost tradeoff rather than replacing the stable path automatically.

**Deliberate mutation.** Adopt a larger model solely because its benchmark ranking is higher.

**Red–green–refactor protocol.** Keep the acceptance threshold fixed for this experiment. Run a baseline, the deliberate fault, and a repaired implementation. Report all outcomes with units and artifact identities; a favorable average cannot erase a catastrophic individual failure.

**Required deliverable.** Advanced optics research comparison and adoption gate. Include its implementation identity, test results, and unresolved qualification gates in the phase evidence record.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat bootloader changes, security-state changes, and unverified recovery images.

**Evidence obligation.** Keep the complete result, including rejection reasons and any retained recovery artifacts.


<a id="tc-p160-05"></a>
#### TC-P160-05. Advertised unlock without delivery

**Baseline fixture.** A new maintainer rebuilding the app and reproducing one capture, one film render, and one virtual-lens evaluation.

**Adversarial operation.** Change reported capability metadata but obtain no valid new sensor output.

**Required response.** Fail the acquisition hypothesis despite the expanded mode menu.

**Baseline oracle.** The archive provides enough information to reproduce qualified behaviour and clearly identifies unavailable physical prerequisites.

**False-pass control.** A newly visible setting is not proof of useful capture.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat sample receipt, decoded fidelity, sustained cadence, and thermal checks.

**Evidence obligation.** Bind measurements to the source revision and the actual backend or test environment.


<a id="tc-p160-06"></a>
#### TC-P160-06. Computational capture overclaim

**Baseline fixture.** A new maintainer rebuilding the app and reproducing one capture, one film render, and one virtual-lens evaluation.

**Adversarial operation.** Merge multiple exposures and present the result as a single unchanged sensor exposure.

**Required response.** Label computational acquisition and measure motion artifacts and retained information separately.

**Baseline oracle.** The archive provides enough information to reproduce qualified behaviour and clearly identifies unavailable physical prerequisites.

**False-pass control.** An attractive merge cannot erase its source-sampling provenance.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat moving subjects, clipped channels, alignment failures, and temporal ghosts.

**Evidence obligation.** Record each repetition separately; do not replace individual failures with an aggregate pass.


<a id="tc-p160-07"></a>
#### TC-P160-07. Advanced model cost regression

**Baseline fixture.** A new maintainer rebuilding the app and reproducing one capture, one film render, and one virtual-lens evaluation.

**Adversarial operation.** Adopt a larger research model that improves one artifact but exceeds practical memory or time budgets.

**Required response.** Report the quality-cost tradeoff and retain the stable baseline until the adoption gate passes.

**Baseline oracle.** The archive provides enough information to reproduce qualified behaviour and clearly identifies unavailable physical prerequisites.

**False-pass control.** A leaderboard position alone cannot justify replacement.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat difficult-scene quality, sustained device load, and deferred job interruption.

**Evidence obligation.** Preserve the negative-control result and explain which assertion detects the false success.


<a id="tc-p160-08"></a>
#### TC-P160-08. Unreproducible research closure

**Baseline fixture.** A new maintainer rebuilding the app and reproducing one capture, one film render, and one virtual-lens evaluation.

**Adversarial operation.** Archive only favorable outputs while omitting failed experiments and essential setup details.

**Required response.** Preserve enough evidence to reconstruct decisions and reproduce qualified results independently.

**Baseline oracle.** The archive provides enough information to reproduce qualified behaviour and clearly identifies unavailable physical prerequisites.

**False-pass control.** A promotional reel cannot substitute for an engineering archive.

**Repetition plan.** Repeat fresh-maintainer reproduction of capture, film rendering, optics, and rejected hypotheses.

**Evidence obligation.** Attach the final evidence manifest and unresolved limits before requesting acceptance review.


<a id="reference-code"></a>
## Appendix A. Executable reference code and test-first examples

### A.1 Execution boundary

The following source files are complete host reference files, not fragments of an Android application. Python uses the standard library. Kotlin uses the standard library and JDK. The code is deliberately small enough to inspect and execute. It demonstrates numerical domains, exact timestamps, source lineage, state transitions, deterministic texture coordinates, resource leases, and explicit graph edges.

The Python suite contains 53 named tests. Its initial 48 tests failed against unimplemented boundaries before passing; five additional overflow and evidence-type checks were then written, observed failing, and repaired. The Kotlin suite contains 32 named checks, all observed failing at unimplemented boundaries before passing against the included implementation. This proves the stated host behavior under the included fixtures; it does not prove camera availability, sustained recording, sensor precision, film fidelity, GPU behavior, Android lifecycle correctness, or physical depth accuracy.

The toy density function is not a Kodak profile. The counter-based Gaussian sampler is not a complete physical film-grain simulation. The temporal helper assumes already aligned inputs and is not optical flow. The evidence conjunction is a small test model, not the complete release policy. The atomic JSON helper does not establish Android provider durability or directory-fsync guarantees. The Kotlin lease permits idempotent concurrent close but does not make arbitrary concurrent borrowing safe. These limitations are part of the reference contract.

### A.2 Running Python

```sh
cd reference
python -m unittest -v test_reference.py
```

### A.3 Python implementation: `reference/cinema_reference.py`

```python
"""Original executable host reference contracts for the S23 cinema directive.

Python 3.11+, standard library only. Not an Android camera implementation.
LogC3 EI800 exposure-domain constants follow ARRI's 2017 VFX specification.
The toy density curve and white Gaussian noise are test scaffolds, NOT a
calibrated Kodak stock or a physically complete film-grain implementation.
"""
from __future__ import annotations
import hashlib
import json
import math
import os
import tempfile
from dataclasses import dataclass, field
from pathlib import Path
from typing import Any, Iterable, Mapping

CUT = 0.010591
A, B, C, D, E, F = 5.555556, 0.052272, 0.247190, 0.385537, 5.367655, 0.092809


def finite(value: float, name: str = 'value') -> float:
    value = float(value)
    if not math.isfinite(value):
        raise ValueError(f'{name} must be finite')
    return value


def integer(value: int, name: str) -> int:
    if isinstance(value, bool) or not isinstance(value, int):
        raise ValueError(f'{name} must be an integer, not bool')
    return value


def logc3_encode(value: float) -> float:
    x = finite(value)
    return finite(C * math.log10(A*x+B) + D if x > CUT else E*x+F, "encoded LogC3")


def logc3_decode(value: float) -> float:
    y = finite(value)
    try:
        x = (10**((y-D)/C)-B)/A if y > E*CUT+F else (y-F)/E
    except OverflowError as exc:
        raise ValueError('Log input exceeds finite reference domain') from exc
    return finite(x, 'decoded exposure')


def normalize_raw(code: float, black: float, white: float) -> float:
    code, black, white = finite(code), finite(black), finite(white)
    if white <= black:
        raise ValueError('White level must exceed black level')
    return finite(finite(code-black, "RAW numerator") / finite(white-black, "RAW denominator"), "normalized RAW")


def quantize_luma10(value: float, allow_clip: bool = False) -> int:
    x = finite(value)
    if not 0 <= x <= 1:
        if not allow_clip:
            raise ValueError('Clipping requires explicit caller authorization')
        x = min(1.0, max(0.0, x))
    # Defined half-up rounding; this is luma only, not a chroma formula.
    return int(math.floor(64+876*x+0.5))


def pack_p010_row(codes: Iterable[int], row_stride: int) -> bytes:
    values = list(codes)
    integer(row_stride, 'row_stride')
    if row_stride < 2*len(values) or row_stride % 2:
        raise ValueError('Stride must be even and large enough')
    result = bytearray(row_stride)
    for i, code in enumerate(values):
        integer(code, 'code')
        if not 0 <= code <= 1023:
            raise ValueError('Ten-bit code out of range')
        result[2*i:2*i+2] = (code << 6).to_bytes(2, 'little')
    return bytes(result)


def unpack_p010_row(data: bytes, width: int) -> list[int]:
    integer(width, 'width')
    if width < 0 or len(data) < 2*width:
        raise ValueError('Insufficient row data')
    values=[]
    for i in range(width):
        word = int.from_bytes(data[2*i:2*i+2], 'little')
        if word & 63:
            raise ValueError('P010 sample has nonzero low six bits')
        values.append(word >> 6)
    return values


def pts_us(index: int, rate_num: int, rate_den: int) -> int:
    for value, name in ((index,'index'),(rate_num,'rate_num'),(rate_den,'rate_den')):
        integer(value,name)
    if index < 0 or rate_num <= 0 or rate_den <= 0:
        raise ValueError('Invalid frame index or rational frame rate')
    return index*rate_den*1_000_000//rate_num


def pair_exact(timestamps: Iterable[int], metadata: Mapping[int, Any]) -> list[Any]:
    ts = list(timestamps)
    if any(isinstance(t,bool) or not isinstance(t,int) or t<0 for t in ts):
        raise ValueError('Sensor timestamps must be nonnegative integers')
    if any(a >= b for a,b in zip(ts, ts[1:])):
        raise ValueError('Sensor timestamps must be strictly increasing')
    missing=[t for t in ts if t not in metadata]
    if missing:
        raise ValueError(f'Missing exact metadata for {missing[0]}')
    return [metadata[t] for t in ts]


def coc_mm(focal_mm: float, f_number: float, focus_mm: float, object_mm: float) -> float:
    """Signed thin-lens circle diameter at the focused image plane.

    Positive = farther than focus, negative = nearer. A finite virtual focus
    is required. Object distance may be positive infinity. Units are millimetres.
    f-number controls aperture geometry; a T-stop is not substituted here.
    """
    f,n,s=finite(focal_mm),finite(f_number),finite(focus_mm)
    u=float(object_mm)
    if f<=0 or n<=0 or s<=f or math.isnan(u) or u<=f:
        raise ValueError('Invalid thin-lens geometry')
    denominator = finite(n*(s-f), "optical denominator")
    if denominator <= 0: raise ValueError("Optical denominator underflow")
    return finite(f*f/denominator * (1-s/u), "circle of confusion")


def coc_pixels(diameter_mm: float, gate_width_mm: float, output_width: int) -> float:
    d,w=finite(diameter_mm),finite(gate_width_mm)
    integer(output_width,'output_width')
    if w<=0 or output_width<=0:
        raise ValueError('Gate and output width must be positive')
    return d*output_width/w


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class DepthSample:
    value: float
    units: str


def metric_distance(sample: DepthSample) -> float:
    if sample.units!='metres':
        raise ValueError('Relative depth requires a validated metric calibration')
    value=finite(sample.value)
    if value<=0: raise ValueError('Depth must be positive')
    return value


def focal_for_fov(gate_width_mm: float, horizontal_degrees: float) -> float:
    g,a=finite(gate_width_mm),finite(horizontal_degrees)
    if g<=0 or not 0<a<180: raise ValueError('Invalid gate or field of view')
    return g/(2*math.tan(math.radians(a)/2))


def temporal_depth(current: float, reprojected_previous: float,
                   history_weight: float, occluded: bool=False) -> float:
    a,b,w=finite(current),finite(reprojected_previous),finite(history_weight)
    if a<=0 or b<=0 or not 0<=w<=1: raise ValueError('Invalid depth or history weight')
    # Caller must supply already reprojected, scale-aligned depth. This helper
    # does not estimate optical flow, detect occlusions, or establish metres.
    return a if occluded else (1-w)*a+w*b


def exposure_seconds(angle: float, rate_num: int, rate_den: int) -> float:
    a=finite(angle)
    integer(rate_num,'rate_num'); integer(rate_den,'rate_den')
    if not 0<a<=360 or rate_num<=0 or rate_den<=0:
        raise ValueError('Invalid shutter angle or frame rate')
    return a/360*rate_den/rate_num


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class ModeEvidence:
    advertised: bool
    configured: bool
    samples_received: bool
    independently_decoded: bool
    physical_protocol_passed: bool

    def __post_init__(self) -> None:
        if any(type(value) is not bool for value in (
            self.advertised, self.configured, self.samples_received,
            self.independently_decoded, self.physical_protocol_passed
        )):
            raise ValueError("Evidence fields require actual booleans")

    @property
    def certified(self) -> bool:
        # Simplified conjunction for one exact configuration, not a production
        # certification policy. Production additionally binds hashes and dates.
        return all((self.advertised,self.configured,self.samples_received,
                    self.independently_decoded,self.physical_protocol_passed))


def validate_lineage(origin: str, label: str, encoded_bits: int) -> None:
    permitted = {
        'RAW_SENSOR': {'RAW_DERIVED_LOG','RAW_DERIVED_LOOK'},
        'HLG10': {'HLG_DERIVED_LOG','HLG_DERIVED_LOOK'},
        'SDR8': {'SDR_DERIVED_LOOK'},
    }
    if origin not in permitted or label not in permitted[origin]:
        raise ValueError('Output label contradicts source lineage')
    if encoded_bits not in (8,10,12,16):
        raise ValueError('Unrecognized storage precision')
    if label.endswith('_LOG') and encoded_bits<10:
        raise ValueError('This project requires at least ten-bit Log delivery')


def canonical_json(value: Any) -> bytes:
    # This local canonical form is NOT a claim to implement RFC 8785.
    return json.dumps(value,sort_keys=True,separators=(',',':'),
                      ensure_ascii=False,allow_nan=False).encode('utf-8')


def resume_key(source_hash: str, model_hash: str, graph_hash: str, version: str) -> str:
    parts=[source_hash,model_hash,graph_hash,version]
    if any(not isinstance(x,str) or not x for x in parts):
        raise ValueError('All identities must be nonempty strings')
    return hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(parts)).hexdigest()


def atomic_json_write(destination: Path, value: Any) -> None:
    """Same-directory replacement reference; Android provider semantics differ."""
    payload=canonical_json(value)  # Validate BEFORE modifying any files.
    destination=Path(destination)
    fd,name=tempfile.mkstemp(prefix='.'+destination.name+'.',dir=destination.parent)
    try:
        with os.fdopen(fd,'wb') as stream:
            stream.write(payload); stream.flush(); os.fsync(stream.fileno())
        os.replace(name,destination)
        # Directory fsync is intentionally not claimed by this portable helper.
        # Crash-durable production journals need filesystem-specific validation.
    finally:
        try: os.unlink(name)
        except FileNotFoundError: pass


def grain_sample(seed: int, frame: int, x: int, y: int, channel: int) -> float:
    values=(seed,frame,x,y,channel)
    for v in values: integer(v,'counter')
    digest=hashlib.sha256(canonical_json(values)).digest()
    u=(int.from_bytes(digest[:8],'big')+0.5)/2**64
    v=(int.from_bytes(digest[8:16],'big')+0.5)/2**64
    u=min(1-2**-53,max(2**-53,u))
    return math.sqrt(-2*math.log(u))*math.cos(2*math.pi*v)


def toy_density(exposure: float) -> float:
    x=finite(exposure)
    if x<=0: raise ValueError('Toy sensitometry requires positive exposure')
    z=math.log10(x)
    # Stable logistic: abstract monotonic fixture, not manufacturer calibration.
    p=1/(1+math.exp(-z)) if z>=0 else math.exp(z)/(1+math.exp(z))
    return 0.1+2.8*p


def transmittance(density: float) -> float:
    return 10**(-finite(density))


def validate_claim(status: str, references: list[str]) -> None:
    if status not in {'documented','reconstructed','unknown','contradicted'}:
        raise ValueError('Unknown evidence status')
    if status in {'documented','contradicted'} and not references:
        raise ValueError('Documented and contradicted claims need references')


@dataclass(frozen=True)
class RecorderState:
    phase: str='IDLE'
    generation: int=0
    expected: frozenset[str]=field(default_factory=frozenset)
    seen: frozenset[str]=field(default_factory=frozenset)


def reduce_recorder(state: RecorderState, event: str, generation: int,
                    track: str|None=None, expected: tuple[str,...]=('video',)) -> RecorderState:
    if event not in {'start','sample','stop','finalize','fail'}:
        raise ValueError('Unknown recorder event')
    integer(generation,'generation')
    if event=='start':
        if state.phase not in {'IDLE','FINALIZED','ERROR'} or generation<=state.generation:
            raise ValueError('Cannot start this generation')
        tracks=frozenset(expected)
        if not tracks or not tracks<={'video','audio'} or 'video' not in tracks:
            raise ValueError('Invalid selected track set')
        return RecorderState('STARTING',generation,tracks,frozenset())
    if generation!=state.generation:
        return state
    if event=='sample':
        if state.phase not in {'STARTING','RECORDING'}: return state
        if track not in state.expected: raise ValueError('Unexpected track')
        seen=state.seen|{track}
        phase='RECORDING' if seen==state.expected else 'STARTING'
        return RecorderState(phase,generation,state.expected,seen)
    if event=='stop' and state.phase in {'STARTING','RECORDING'}:
        return RecorderState('STOPPING',generation,state.expected,state.seen)
    if event=='finalize' and state.phase=='STOPPING':
        return RecorderState('FINALIZED',generation,state.expected,state.seen)
    if event=='fail':
        return RecorderState('ERROR',generation,state.expected,state.seen)
    return state
```

### A.4 Python tests: `reference/test_reference.py`

```python
"""Executable host contracts. These tests do not certify an Android device."""
import math
import tempfile
import unittest
from pathlib import Path
import cinema_reference as c


class LogEncodingTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_black_is_published_ei800_intercept(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.logc3_encode(0), 0.092809, places=12)

    def test_middle_grey_is_near_documented_value(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.logc3_encode(0.18), 0.3910068, places=6)

    def test_signed_values_round_trip(self):
        for x in (-0.01, -0.001, 0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.02, 0.18, 1, 4, 16):
            self.assertAlmostEqual(c.logc3_decode(c.logc3_encode(x)), x, places=9)

    def test_curve_is_monotonic_over_operating_domain(self):
        xs = [-0.01 + i * 0.001 for i in range(32000)]
        ys = [c.logc3_encode(x) for x in xs]
        self.assertTrue(all(a < b for a, b in zip(ys, ys[1:])))

    def test_nonfinite_values_are_rejected(self):
        for x in (math.nan, math.inf, -math.inf):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.logc3_encode(x)
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.logc3_decode(x)

    def test_rounded_branch_coefficients_have_bounded_join(self):
        x = 0.010591
        self.assertLess(abs(c.logc3_encode(x) - c.logc3_encode(x + 1e-12)), 3e-7)


class NumericContractsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_black_normalization_retains_negative_noise(self):
        self.assertLess(c.normalize_raw(60, 64, 1023), 0)

    def test_invalid_white_level_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.normalize_raw(64, 64, 64)

    def test_legal_luma_endpoints(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.quantize_luma10(0), 64)
        self.assertEqual(c.quantize_luma10(1), 940)

    def test_quantization_rejects_unconsented_clipping(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.quantize_luma10(1.1)
        self.assertEqual(c.quantize_luma10(1.1, allow_clip=True), 940)

    def test_p010_row_obeys_stride_and_bit_alignment(self):
        row = c.pack_p010_row([64, 512, 940], row_stride=10)
        self.assertEqual(len(row), 10)
        self.assertEqual(c.unpack_p010_row(row, 3), [64, 512, 940])
        self.assertEqual(row[6:], b'\0\0\0\0')
        self.assertTrue(all(int.from_bytes(row[i:i+2], 'little') & 63 == 0 for i in (0,2,4)))

    def test_p010_invalid_codes_and_stride_are_rejected(self):
        for codes, stride in (([1024], 2), ([-1], 2), ([1, 2], 3), ([True], 2)):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.pack_p010_row(codes, stride)

    def test_p010_unpack_rejects_low_bit_pollution(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.unpack_p010_row(b'\x01\x10', 1)

    def test_cfr_integer_arithmetic_avoids_accumulating_rounding(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.pts_us(24000, 24000, 1001), 1001000000)
        for i in range(24000):
            self.assertLessEqual(abs(c.pts_us(i, 24000, 1001) - i*1001*1e6/24000), 1)

    def test_cfr_invalid_values_rejected(self):
        for args in ((-1,24,1),(1,0,1),(1,24,0),(1.5,24,1)):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.pts_us(*args)

    def test_timestamp_pairing_is_exact_not_nearest(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.pair_exact([100,200], {200:'b',100:'a'}), ['a','b'])
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.pair_exact([100], {101:'near'})

    def test_duplicate_sensor_timestamps_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.pair_exact([100,100], {100:'a'})


class OpticalContractsTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_focus_plane_is_sharp(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.coc_mm(50, 2, 2000, 2000), 0)

    def test_near_and_far_blur_have_opposite_signs(self):
        self.assertLess(c.coc_mm(50, 2, 2000, 1000), 0)
        self.assertGreater(c.coc_mm(50, 2, 2000, 4000), 0)

    def test_stopping_down_halves_diameter(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.coc_mm(50,4,2000,4000)*2, c.coc_mm(50,2,2000,4000))

    def test_infinity_limit_is_finite(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.coc_mm(50,2,2000,math.inf), 2500/(2*1950))

    def test_gate_conversion_is_explicit(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.coc_pixels(0.1, 50, 4000), 8)

    def test_invalid_optical_geometry_rejected(self):
        for args in ((50,0,2000,4000),(50,2,40,4000),(50,2,2000,40)):
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.coc_mm(*args)

    def test_relative_depth_cannot_masquerade_as_metres(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.metric_distance(c.DepthSample(0.5, 'relative'))
        self.assertEqual(c.metric_distance(c.DepthSample(2.0, 'metres')), 2.0)

    def test_fov_lens_is_derived_from_gate_and_angle(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.focal_for_fov(36, 90), 18)

    def test_occlusion_disables_history_blending(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.temporal_depth(2, 100, 0.9, occluded=True), 2)

    def test_temporal_history_weight_is_bounded(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.temporal_depth(2,4,0.25), 2.5)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.temporal_depth(2,4,1.2)

    def test_shutter_angle_converts_to_seconds(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.exposure_seconds(180,24,1), 1/48)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.exposure_seconds(361,24,1)


class EvidenceAndPersistenceTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_advertised_is_not_certified(self):
        e = c.ModeEvidence(True, True, True, True, False)
        self.assertFalse(e.certified)

    def test_all_evidence_required(self):
        self.assertTrue(c.ModeEvidence(True,True,True,True,True).certified)

    def test_source_lineage_disallows_raw_label_for_sdr(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.validate_lineage('SDR8', 'RAW_DERIVED_LOG', 10)
        c.validate_lineage('RAW_SENSOR', 'RAW_DERIVED_LOG', 10)

    def test_ten_bit_output_alone_does_not_upgrade_source(self):
        c.validate_lineage('SDR8', 'SDR_DERIVED_LOOK', 10)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.validate_lineage('HLG10', 'RAW_DERIVED_LOG', 10)

    def test_resume_key_covers_model_and_source(self):
        a = c.resume_key('a','m1','graph','v1')
        self.assertNotEqual(a, c.resume_key('a','m2','graph','v1'))
        self.assertNotEqual(a, c.resume_key('b','m1','graph','v1'))

    def test_canonical_manifest_is_order_independent(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.canonical_json({'a':1,'b':2}),c.canonical_json({'b':2,'a':1}))
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.canonical_json({'x':math.nan})

    def test_atomic_write_preserves_unrelated_source(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p = Path(d)/'result.json'; source=Path(d)/'source.raw'
            source.write_bytes(b'unchanged')
            c.atomic_json_write(p, {'status':'partial'})
            c.atomic_json_write(p, {'status':'verified'})
            self.assertIn('verified', p.read_text())
            self.assertEqual(source.read_bytes(), b'unchanged')

    def test_corrupt_manifest_does_not_replace_valid_output(self):
        with tempfile.TemporaryDirectory() as d:
            p=Path(d)/'x.json'; p.write_text('previous')
            with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.atomic_json_write(p, {'bad': math.nan})
            self.assertEqual(p.read_text(), 'previous')

    def test_counter_noise_is_reproducible(self):
        self.assertEqual(c.grain_sample(123,4,5,6,0), c.grain_sample(123,4,5,6,0))
        self.assertNotEqual(c.grain_sample(123,4,5,6,0), c.grain_sample(123,5,5,6,0))

    def test_counter_noise_has_reasonable_synthetic_statistics(self):
        values=[c.grain_sample(991, i, 2,3,0) for i in range(5000)]
        mean=sum(values)/len(values)
        var=sum((v-mean)**2 for v in values)/len(values)
        self.assertLess(abs(mean), .06)
        self.assertLess(abs(var-1), .08)

    def test_film_density_responds_monotonically(self):
        ys=[c.toy_density(2**(i/10)) for i in range(-100,100)]
        self.assertTrue(all(a<b for a,b in zip(ys,ys[1:])))

    def test_density_to_transmission(self):
        self.assertAlmostEqual(c.transmittance(2), .01)

    def test_recipe_requires_evidence_for_documented_claims(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.validate_claim('documented', [])
        c.validate_claim('reconstructed', [])
        c.validate_claim('documented', ['source-1'])

    def test_no_claimed_movie_lens_from_null_fact(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.validate_claim('invented', ['source-1'])


class RecorderStateTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_recording_waits_for_every_selected_track(self):
        s = c.RecorderState()
        s = c.reduce_recorder(s, 'start', 1, expected=('video','audio'))
        s = c.reduce_recorder(s, 'sample', 1, track='video')
        self.assertEqual(s.phase, 'STARTING')
        s = c.reduce_recorder(s, 'sample', 1, track='audio')
        self.assertEqual(s.phase, 'RECORDING')

    def test_stop_cannot_be_undone_by_late_sample(self):
        s=c.reduce_recorder(c.RecorderState(), 'start', 1)
        s=c.reduce_recorder(s,'stop',1)
        self.assertEqual(c.reduce_recorder(s,'sample',1,track='video').phase,'STOPPING')

    def test_stale_generation_is_ignored(self):
        s=c.reduce_recorder(c.RecorderState(),'start',8)
        self.assertEqual(c.reduce_recorder(s,'sample',7,track='video'),s)

    def test_finalize_retains_recorded_status(self):
        s=c.reduce_recorder(c.RecorderState(),'start',1)
        s=c.reduce_recorder(s,'sample',1,track='video')
        s=c.reduce_recorder(s,'stop',1)
        s=c.reduce_recorder(s,'finalize',1)
        self.assertEqual(s.phase,'FINALIZED')
        self.assertEqual(s.seen, frozenset({'video'}))

    def test_unexpected_track_rejected(self):
        s=c.reduce_recorder(c.RecorderState(),'start',1)
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.reduce_recorder(s,'sample',1,track='audio')

    def test_invalid_event_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.reduce_recorder(c.RecorderState(),'mystery',0)


class BoundaryHardeningTests(unittest.TestCase):
    def test_positive_log_overflow_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.logc3_encode(1e308)

    def test_negative_log_overflow_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.logc3_encode(-1e308)

    def test_raw_normalization_rejects_overflowed_intermediate(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.normalize_raw(1.0, -1e308, 1e308)

    def test_optical_overflow_is_rejected(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.coc_mm(1e200, 2.0, 2e200, 3e200)

    def test_evidence_fields_require_actual_booleans(self):
        with self.assertRaises(ValueError): c.ModeEvidence("false", True, True, True, True)

if __name__ == '__main__':
```

### A.5 Running Kotlin/JVM

```sh
kotlinc kotlin/Contracts.kt kotlin/ContractsTest.kt -include-runtime -d contracts.jar
java -jar contracts.jar
```

The concurrency checks propagate worker errors and use bounded waits. An early test-harness attempt revealed an unbounded wait in the red state; the harness was corrected before the retained complete red run. This is why test harnesses themselves need failure-path review.

### A.6 Kotlin implementation: `reference/kotlin/Contracts.kt`

```kotlin
package cinema.reference

import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicBoolean
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger
import kotlin.math.abs
import kotlin.math.max

/** Single-owner lease. Concurrent close is idempotent; do not use a borrowed value after transfer/close. */
class FrameLease<T>(private val value: T, private val release: () -> Unit) : AutoCloseable {
    private val closed = AtomicBoolean(false)
    fun get(): T {
        check(!closed.get()) { "Lease already released" }
        return value
    }
    override fun close() {
        if (closed.compareAndSet(false, true)) release()
    }
}

/** Nonblocking admission gate. This counts leases, not bytes; production also needs a byte budget. */
class LeasePool(private val capacity: Int) {
    private val active = AtomicInteger(0)
    init { require(capacity > 0) { "Capacity must be positive" } }
    fun <T> tryAcquire(value: T, release: () -> Unit = {}): FrameLease<T>? {
        while (true) {
            val count = active.get()
            if (count >= capacity) return null
            if (active.compareAndSet(count, count + 1)) break
        }
        return FrameLease(value) {
            try { release() }
            finally { check(active.decrementAndGet() >= 0) { "Lease accounting underflow" } }
        }
    }
    fun inUse(): Int = active.get()
}

/** Exact integer floor of frameIndex * 1e6 * denominator / numerator; overflow fails explicitly. */
fun presentationUs(index: Long, numerator: Long, denominator: Long): Long {
    require(index >= 0 && numerator > 0 && denominator > 0)
    val scaled = Math.multiplyExact(Math.multiplyExact(index, 1_000_000L), denominator)
    return scaled / numerator
}

enum class Origin { RAW, HLG, SDR }
fun validateLabel(origin: Origin, label: String) {
    val expected = when (origin) {
        Origin.RAW -> "raw-derived"
        Origin.HLG -> "hdr-derived"
        Origin.SDR -> "sdr-derived"
    }
    require(label == expected) { "Origin $origin cannot support label $label" }
}

/** Minimal test descriptor, not the full production contract documented in the directive. */
data class Signal(val primaries: String, val transfer: String, val bits: Int) {
    init { require(primaries.isNotBlank() && transfer.isNotBlank() && bits > 0) }
}
fun requireCompatible(output: Signal, input: Signal) {
    require(output == input) { "Insert an explicit conversion node: $output -> $input" }
}

data class ManualTarget(val generation: Long, val exposureNs: Long, val iso: Int) {
    init { require(generation >= 0 && exposureNs > 0 && iso > 0) }
}
data class ManualResult(val generation: Long, val exposureNs: Long?, val iso: Int?, val aeOff: Boolean)

/** Example 2% policy only. Actual device acceptance requires its own versioned tolerance and freshness rule. */
fun manualReady(target: ManualTarget, result: ManualResult): Boolean {
    val exposure = result.exposureNs ?: return false
    val sensitivity = result.iso ?: return false
    if (result.generation != target.generation || !result.aeOff || exposure <= 0 || sensitivity <= 0) return false
    val exposureError = abs(exposure.toDouble() - target.exposureNs.toDouble())
    val isoError = abs(sensitivity.toDouble() - target.iso.toDouble())
    return exposureError <= max(1.0, target.exposureNs.toDouble() * 0.02) &&
        isoError <= max(1.0, target.iso.toDouble() * 0.02)
}

/** Signed ideal thin-lens CoC diameter in mm. fNumber is geometric N, not a T-stop. */
fun cocMm(focal: Double, fNumber: Double, focus: Double, subject: Double): Double {
    require(focal.isFinite() && focal > 0)
    require(fNumber.isFinite() && fNumber > 0)
    require(focus.isFinite() && focus > focal)
    require((subject.isFinite() && subject > focal) || subject == Double.POSITIVE_INFINITY)
    val result = focal * focal / (fNumber * (focus - focal)) * (1.0 - focus / subject)
    require(result.isFinite()) { "Nonfinite optical result" }
    return result
}
```

### A.7 Kotlin checks: `reference/kotlin/ContractsTest.kt`

```kotlin
package cinema.reference

import java.util.concurrent.CountDownLatch
import java.util.concurrent.atomic.AtomicInteger
import java.util.concurrent.ConcurrentLinkedQueue
import java.util.concurrent.TimeUnit
import kotlin.concurrent.thread
import kotlin.math.abs

private var passed = 0
private var failed = 0
private fun test(name: String, body: () -> Unit) {
    try { body(); passed++; println("PASS $name") }
    catch (e: Throwable) { failed++; println("FAIL $name: ${e::class.simpleName}: ${e.message}") }
}
private inline fun <reified T: Throwable> expectFailure(body: () -> Unit) {
    try { body() } catch (e: Throwable) {
        check(e is T) { "Expected ${T::class.simpleName}, received ${e::class.simpleName}" }
        return
    }
    error("Expected ${T::class.simpleName}")
}
fun main() {
    test("lease exposes the owned value before release") {
        val lease = FrameLease("frame") {}; check(lease.get() == "frame"); lease.close()
    }
    test("lease refuses access after release") {
        val lease = FrameLease(7) {}; lease.close()
        expectFailure<IllegalStateException> { lease.get() }
    }
    test("lease callback executes once") {
        val calls = AtomicInteger(); val lease = FrameLease(3) { calls.incrementAndGet() }
        lease.close(); lease.close(); check(calls.get() == 1)
    }
    test("concurrent closes release exactly once") {
        val calls = AtomicInteger(); val lease = FrameLease(3) { calls.incrementAndGet() }
        val start = CountDownLatch(1)
        val errors = ConcurrentLinkedQueue<Throwable>()
        val workers = List(12) { thread(start = true) {
            try { check(start.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)); lease.close() } catch (e:Throwable) { errors.add(e) }
        } }
        start.countDown(); workers.forEach { it.join(5000); check(!it.isAlive) }
        check(errors.isEmpty()) { "Worker failure: ${errors.peek()}" }; check(calls.get() == 1)
    }
    test("throwing release still leaves lease closed") {
        val lease = FrameLease(3) { throw IllegalStateException("release failed") }
        expectFailure<IllegalStateException> { lease.close() }
        expectFailure<IllegalStateException> { lease.get() }; lease.close()
    }
    test("pool rejects nonpositive capacity") {
        expectFailure<IllegalArgumentException> { LeasePool(0) }
    }
    test("pool refuses an excess lease") {
        val pool = LeasePool(1); val first = checkNotNull(pool.tryAcquire("a"))
        check(pool.tryAcquire("b") == null); first.close()
    }
    test("pool capacity returns on close") {
        val pool = LeasePool(1); checkNotNull(pool.tryAcquire("a")).close()
        checkNotNull(pool.tryAcquire("b")).close(); check(pool.inUse() == 0)
    }
    test("double close cannot underflow pool") {
        val pool = LeasePool(1); val lease = checkNotNull(pool.tryAcquire("a"))
        lease.close(); lease.close(); check(pool.inUse() == 0)
    }
    test("failing resource callback restores capacity") {
        val pool = LeasePool(1)
        val lease = checkNotNull(pool.tryAcquire("a") { throw IllegalStateException("fault") })
        expectFailure<IllegalStateException> { lease.close() }; check(pool.inUse() == 0)
    }
    test("concurrent pool admissions remain bounded") {
        val pool = LeasePool(3); val start = CountDownLatch(1); val acquired = CountDownLatch(20)
        val release = CountDownLatch(1); val accepted = AtomicInteger()
        val errors = ConcurrentLinkedQueue<Throwable>()
        val workers = List(20) { number -> thread {
            var lease:FrameLease<Int>? = null
            try {
                check(start.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)); lease = pool.tryAcquire(number)
                if (lease != null) accepted.incrementAndGet()
            } catch (e:Throwable) { errors.add(e) }
            finally { acquired.countDown() }
            try { check(release.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)); lease?.close() }
            catch (e:Throwable) { errors.add(e) }
        } }
        start.countDown()
        try {
            check(acquired.await(5, TimeUnit.SECONDS)); check(errors.isEmpty()) { "Worker failure: ${errors.peek()}" }
            check(accepted.get() == 3); check(pool.inUse() == 3)
        } finally {
            release.countDown(); workers.forEach { it.join(5000); check(!it.isAlive) }
        }
        check(errors.isEmpty()); check(pool.inUse() == 0)
    }
    test("rational timestamp starts at zero") { check(presentationUs(0, 24, 1) == 0L) }
    test("rational timestamp does not accumulate rounded intervals") {
        check(presentationUs(24000, 24000, 1001) == 1001000000L)
    }
    test("rational timestamp floors exact fraction") { check(presentationUs(1, 24, 1) == 41666L) }
    test("rational timestamp rejects invalid rates") {
        expectFailure<IllegalArgumentException> { presentationUs(1, 0, 1) }
        expectFailure<IllegalArgumentException> { presentationUs(-1, 24, 1) }
    }
```
